title: Bank of England sets out approach to tokenised collateral in central clearing
body:
Bank of England sets out approach to tokenised collateral in central clearing | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Bank of England sets out approach to tokenised collateral in central clearing The Bank of England has today launched a consultation supporting central counterparties (CCPs) acceptance of tokenised forms of eligible collateral. Published on  
        29 October 2026 News release The Bank of England has today launched a consultation supporting central counterparties (CCPs) acceptance of tokenised forms of eligible collateral. Tokenisation could offer opportunities for quicker and more efficient mobilisation and management of collateral, including across jurisdictions. This could support firms to respond more effectively to margin calls, improve collateral management and support innovation in central clearing, contributing to the UK's wholesale digital financial markets strategy. The Bank considers the existing regulatory framework is not a barrier for CCPs accepting tokenised forms of eligible collateral, provided the collateral meets the standards required in central clearing. For example, tokenised collateral must remain capable of being valued, transferred and realised when needed, including in stressed conditions. In order to support CCPs and their participants to explore tokenised collateral, the proposed Supervisory Statement is intended to provide greater clarity on how the Bank would assess applications involving tokenised collateral. Consistent with the principle of same risk, same regulatory outcome, different tokenised collateral arrangements may also achieve those outcomes in different ways. Sarah Breeden, Deputy Governor for Financial Stability, said: “Through today’s consultation, the Bank is further delivering its secondary objective for innovation in financial market infrastructure, while maintaining financial stability. It’s part of a major agenda between authorities and industry to enable the responsible adoption of tokenisation in financial markets.” Notes to editors The consultation paper closes on 12 February 2027. The Bank welcomes responses from across industry, including CCPs and their market participants, infrastructure providers, technology firms and other stakeholders exploring the use of tokenised collateral in central clearing. The consultation forms part of the Bank’s broader work with the FCA, HM Treasury and industry to support the responsible adoption of tokenisation and provide greater clarity on the future development of UK digital wholesale financial markets. title: Partnering with Singapore to bring frontier AI to public health
body: Partnering with Singapore to bring frontier AI to public health Oct 29, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link At the Google for Health Summit in Singapore, we announced a new Google Research hub and initiatives to support frontline clinicians, advance research, and help Singaporeans live healthier lives. Ben King Country Managing Director, Google Singapore Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Read AI-generated summary We are partnering with the Singapore Ministry of Health to deploy frontier AI across their healthcare system. Our new research hub in Singapore will focus on foundational AI models to accelerate local scientific breakthroughs. We are contributing 7 million dollars to support public health intelligence and disease detection across the region. Clinicians will use our AI tools to cross-reference medical guidelines and provide personalized care for their patients. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We're deepening our partnership with Singapore to deploy frontier AI across the nation’s healthcare system. The primary goals of the new collaboration, announced at the Google for Health Summit in Singapore, are to accelerate scientific discoveries, transform clinical care delivery, and empower Singaporeans with proactive health tools. Working closely with local researchers, clinicians, and public agencies, we share a vision of using technology where it will have the greatest impact: driving medical breakthroughs, helping frontline workers focus on patient care, giving people better ways to manage their health, and expanding preventive care across the community. Here is a look at how this work is coming to life across Singapore. Accelerating scientific breakthroughs and local research We’re establishing a Google Research hub in Singapore composed of local research scientists and software engineers. The group will focus on driving advancements in foundational AI models to accelerate scientific breakthroughs. It will also partner with academic institutions, such as the National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University, to help nurture future scientific leaders and provide targeted research support. Google Research will also scale its existing health research initiatives in Singapore. This includes bringing open models like MedGemma to frontline care settings to enable the development of secure, customized solutions while maintaining full data sovereignty. To advance scientific research, Google.org and Google DeepMind are contributing $7 million to the Philanthropy Asia Alliance’s Health for Human Potential Coalition. This includes $1 million for PathGen , an AI platform that uses Google technology to help countries detect disease threats faster and share data for public health intelligence while protecting in-country data sovereignty. Supporting clinicians and advancing population-scale health To support frontline care, Google DeepMind is working with the National University Health System to evaluate our AI co-clinician tool that helps clinicians quickly synthesize information from medical guidelines and literature, and assist doctors with clinical queries as they care for patients. Additionally, Google Cloud is partnering with NHG Health on a population health program that uses AI-driven predictive insights to forecast health risks, such as chronic conditions, across sub-populations. These insights feed directly into an AI health coach on the NHG HealthBot, using Google’s Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience platform, to deliver personalized lifestyle guidance and preventative care reminders to residents. Reinforcing commitments to public health True impact in healthcare requires advanced technology. It also relies on a health system's ability to integrate AI responsibly, govern it safely, and translate it into human-centered care. As countries around the world face shared challenges like an aging population and navigating the shift toward personalized and preventive care, pairing our technical expertise with Singapore’s world-class healthcare institutions will help build a future-ready system that serves as a blueprint for scaling AI safely for public good. title: Ads in AI Mode expand to new markets.
body: Google Ads Ads in AI Mode expand to new markets. Shashi Thakur VP and GM, Google Search Ads and Ads on Google Experiences Oct 28, 2026 We’re bringing ads in AI Mode to new countries. As AI transforms how people search, queries are becoming increasingly conversational. In AI Mode, queries are, on average, three times longer than traditional searches. 1 AI helps us better understand what people are looking for, allowing us to connect them to the businesses and services that best match their needs. Our research shows that people are comfortable with ads in AI Mode and find them highly relevant. In fact, click-through rates are already similar between sponsored and organic product list items within AI Mode. 2 Now we're scaling ads in AI Mode in Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Singapore. In Q4 2026, we plan to expand to additional locales, including Brazil, Mexico, and the United Kingdom. To allow ads in follow-up queries in AI Mode, we are launching multiturn ads in the U.S. Ads will be clearly labeled as “Sponsored.” We’ll continue testing new formats to ensure ads remain helpful and relevant. Learn more here .
retained_feed_body: Google is expanding AI Mode ads to 10 new countries, including Canada and India. See how these relevant sponsored results improve your search experience.

title: Q3 2026 earnings call: Remarks from our CEO
body: Q3 2026 earnings call: Remarks from our CEO Oct 28, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link On today’s Q3 2026 earnings call, Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai recapped a strong quarter, with our full-stack approach driving momentum across the business. Below is an edited transcript of his remarks. Sundar Pichai CEO of Google and Alphabet Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link In this article Q3 was a strong quarter for Alphabet. Our deep, full-stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with many opportunities ahead. Alphabet revenues grew 25% year-over-year. We’re now at a half-trillion-dollar annual run rate — that’s remarkable growth. Search has strong momentum. Our AI investments are driving increased usage and overall query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years. Google Cloud revenues grew 103%. Our AI infrastructure and solutions are the major drivers for Cloud growth and our customers see us as the leading provider here, so there’s huge demand. We are working hard to bring more capacity online to meet this long-term demand. At the same time, we’re seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers, and we expect that to continue as we scale. On our AI models: Customers are using our models more than ever. Our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute — 40% more than last quarter and more than four times what we processed a year ago. And with Gemini 4 Argon and now Carbon, which we announced today, we’re excited to be leading at the frontier. The Gemini app is now at one billion users and is the fastest-growing product in Google’s history. Lastly, we’ve surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, including trials. Today, I'll talk more about our AI progress, our global consumer platforms led by Search and YouTube, then our long-term bets. AI progress Starting with AI, highlighted by our Gemini 4 series of frontier models. We’re seeing strong demand and usage for Argon, which we launched two weeks ago. In fact, on our developer platforms, usage in the first week ramped up three-and-a-half times faster than Gemini 3, even with capacity constraints. Argon is proving to do really well in areas like finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Developers and Cloud customers are already using it for things like untangling legacy codebases, accelerating scientific research, robotics, discovering product improvements, and domain-specific tasks requiring in-depth reasoning. And at Google, just in the last few weeks, teams across Chrome, Ads, and Search have used Argon to write and optimize code much faster, shipping 35% more code with 30% fewer errors. Argon is just the start of the Gemini 4 series. Today, we announced Carbon. It’s our strongest frontier model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. It ranks #1 on the recently updated Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. Carbon outperforms Argon across almost every domain, like full-stack web development, multimodal understanding, complex knowledge work, and scientific reasoning. We're rolling Carbon out first to a subset of trusted cyber defenders before we expand access, and it's being tested by the U.S. government. Beyond our Gemini 4 series, yesterday we announced Genie 4, our most advanced world model yet that simulates safe, realistic, interactive worlds with native audio in real time. This is an important building block for training robots and agents. This rapid progress underscores our incredible model momentum. We’re at the point where AI is helping us increase our training and launch velocity. I would expect the next 12 months to see continued acceleration because of RSI. We have more models coming soon, including more efficient versions to help developers optimize for speed and cost and to deploy across our billions of users. Search Search is bringing the benefits of AI to more people than any other product in the world. Just like our shift to mobile over a decade ago, we are focused on building the best Search user experience, followed by monetization. We are building one seamless experience across AI Overviews, AI Mode, and traditional Search. And people are using our AI features more, searching in entirely new ways. Their queries are longer, personalized, and multimodal. Queries in AI Mode are on average three times longer than traditional searches, and one in five AI Mode searches globally use voice, images, or documents. We’ve now crossed over 50 billion visual searches per month. Agentic experiences One area I’m excited about is helping people get things done, be it booking reservations, filling in forms, scheduling appointments, or making purchases. As AI becomes more personal and starts taking action for people and businesses, trust and security matter more than ever. People already put their trust in Google to get things done in their daily lives, and our leadership here remains an important differentiator. We focused first on getting these agentic experiences right with the Gemini agent for enterprise because the bar for security, safety, and governance is extremely high. As a next step, we’re bringing these features to Search. And also, of course, to our billion users on the Gemini app. People are already using the Gemini app to do more than ask questions; they’re using it to do things, including complex, multi-step agentic queries. Our Gemini 4 series has been a really big step forward here, and has already been handling these complex tasks really well. Agents will operate as a unifying layer across our products, so you’ll see us extend these agentic experiences beyond Search and the Gemini app to Chrome, Android, and our Workspace products as well. YouTube On to YouTube, which continues to lead in the living room as the number-one streaming platform in the U.S. in terms of watch time. It’s also seeing good subscriber growth, as I mentioned. At Made on YouTube last month, we announced more than 30 products and features for creators and viewers. One great example is custom feeds, where you can simply pick a topic you love and get a tailored video home feed based on that topic. Other Bets On to our long-term bets. Waymo is on a great trajectory. We’ve now driven more than 300 million fully autonomous miles. Waymo now operates in 15 major U.S. cities and just recently opened up service to the public in San Antonio, San Diego, and Tampa, with planned expansions into Canada, Germany, Singapore, and Spain. We’re also seeing strong progress across our other long-term initiatives. Isomorphic is using Argon to support drug design research. We demonstrated “magic state cultivation” for the first time in quantum computing, and launched our TPUs into space with Project Suncatcher. So it’s been a busy quarter and there’s much more to come. I want to thank our employees for their work this quarter. Get the latest news from Google in your inbox Sign up for our newsletters with product updates, event information, special offers, and more. Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Press Releases Press Release PDF October 28, 2026 Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT Share The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10 – 2 vote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system. Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little. Inflation remains elevated. The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability. Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting. For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call 202-452-2955. Implementation Note issued October 28, 2026 Last Update:

title: Dive into new topics with immersive explorations in the Gemini app.
body: Dive into new topics with immersive explorations in the Gemini app. Oct 28, 2026 The Gemini app now has a library of immersive explorations , giving you an interactive, visual way to explore topics layer-by-layer, from microscopic systems to deep space and more. You can access this library in the Gemini student hub by clicking on “Try immersive explorations” and will soon be able to access these immersive explorations directly in a chat conversation with Gemini. Whether it’s tracing trade routes on the Silk Road, peering inside a jet engine, or studying the physics of lightning, each scene unfolds into interactive and guided experiences. Tap a label to dig deeper, journeying from sweeping planetary scales straight down to molecules and atoms. Immersive explorations will soon include audio narration to walk you through each layer. This feature is available to all users in English, Indonesian, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, French, and simplified Chinese. Users in all other languages currently receive an English-only experience, with more languages coming soon. Explore the feature today.

body: Chrome’s enhanced autofill helps you fill out forms with suggestions pulled from Gmail. Amanda Lim Product Manager, Chrome Oct 28, 2026 Filling out online forms can be tedious, especially when you have to switch between tabs or search through your inbox to track down information. While autofill has always handled the basics — like your name, address, and credit card number — now it’s handling even more. Starting today, Chrome’s enhanced autofill feature can automatically suggest information pulled directly from Gmail as you fill out online forms. Using Gemini with Personal Intelligence, it can surface details like order numbers, tracking information, and flight bookings, right when you need them. As always, sensitive data is encrypted and you remain in control. You can manage whether enhanced autofill is enabled and what it can access via your Chrome settings. These capabilities are beginning to roll out in the U.S. on desktop, Android and iOS for Gemini in Chrome users with Personal Intelligence enabled.

title: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model
body: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model Oct 28, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Gemini 4 Carbon is our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. Koray Kavukcuoglu SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching. On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates. Building on Gemini 4 Argon , which was launched two weeks ago, Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward. Our researchers and models are working hand in hand to advance capabilities faster, while strengthening our safeguards in tandem. We're taking a deliberate approach to rollout and are actively engaged in the U.S. government’s voluntary process for pre-release model testing. Starting this week, we will make Carbon available to a subset of cyber defenders and will gradually phase access to additional trusted partners through our Fairwind Program . We’re continuing to gather feedback and iterate on guardrails before making Carbon available to developers, businesses, and consumers via our product surfaces as soon as possible. Gemini 4 Carbon will launch at the same introductory price 1 as Argon at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price. Improving coding and reasoning for challenging, long-horizon tasks Designed to take on much harder, long-horizon engineering problems, Carbon is built for sustained agentic workflows. Internally, our teams have seen Carbon run for days to persist through dead ends to tackle complex, multi-step engineering tasks like root-causing and patching subtle bugs across large codebases and low-level systems. Building on user feedback, we focused on improving model performance across a variety of domains, including coding, agentic, and scientific tasks, as well as full-stack web development and multimodal understanding. With improved quality of output and artifacts in web development, Carbon jumps +89 elo points to land at #4 (1768) on WebDev Arena . State-of-the-art cybersecurity performance to help build secure systems Gemini 4 Carbon delivers a significant leap in cybersecurity capabilities. It achieves state-of-the-art performance across the cybersecurity defense lifecycle — vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation. Our teams are already seeing strong gains in cyberdefense. On internal benchmarks, Carbon achieves more than 2x uplift in success rate for generating secure code over Argon. As another example, the Chrome team has reported that Carbon performed more than 10X better than another lab's large frontier model when generating high quality patches. Wiz, our leading Cloud security platform, also observes Carbon leading on benchmarks for web penetration testing, a core capability for Wiz's Scan for Good initiative. Carbon excels across key external benchmarks (evaluated without guardrails): Finding real vulnerabilities: Core to cybersecurity defense is finding real vulnerabilities. Carbon achieves a state-of-the-art 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro , autonomously uncovering complex flaws buried in real-world software. Validating risk through exploitation: To prioritize which vulnerabilities to remediate first or remediate at all, cyber defenders increasingly rely on models to check which vulnerabilities are exploitable. Carbon sets a new state-of-the-art on the popular exploitation benchmark ExploitGym (54.8%). Patching at the root cause: Ultimately after identifying the vulnerabilities, fixing the root cause is a critical step in the cybersecurity defense lifecycle. Carbon reaches 71.0% on Collinear’s CWE-bench , turning validated findings directly into working code fixes. Advancing frontier model safety & security Gemini 4 Carbon builds on the same multi-layered safety and security stack of Argon — combining model training, real-time misuse defenses, prompt-injection resilience, and chain-of-thought monitoring. In particular, we made significant strides in model alignment with Argon, and reported its propensities to behave in an aligned way in our Safety and Security report . With Carbon, we challenged ourselves to go a step further on alignment, and trained the model to respond to complex or high-pressure tasks in the right way. Reducing shortcuts and loophole exploitation: With Carbon, we further mitigated shortcut attempts in training while ensuring high-quality coding performance. Carbon reduced successful cheating on Terminal-Bench 4.0 to 0.0%, with attempts to cheat dropping to 0.4% — all while improving overall accuracy. In live coding environments with our internal teams, we observed that high-severity misalignment alerts dropped by almost 80%. Greater transparency and honesty: In our internal testing, Carbon cuts unsupported claims by approximately 2x over Argon. It puts methodological caveats directly into the deliverable or withholds blocked actions with a clear list of what remains required, rather than fabricating or hedging around missing evidence. Improved collaboration with the user in the face of ambiguity: Rather than guessing or forcing a path forward, Carbon retrieves the relevant sources and surfaces discrepancies to the user before acting — as a result, users should observe a much better collaborative experience with Carbon. Following through without overstepping: Carbon simultaneously reduced overreach by 26% and under-service by 29% resulting in much more reliable execution of multi-step plans end-to-end while respecting project constraints and staying strictly within scope. Resisting prompt injection: While Argon previously led the Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) Benchmark in prompt injection resistance with a very low 0.7% attack success rate, Carbon achieves 0.0% — resisting every evaluated attack attempt. Coming soon to developers, businesses, and consumers Pushing the frontier forward requires moving fast while remaining deliberate about deployment. With Gemini 4 Carbon, our goal is to deliver meaningful leaps in software engineering and cybersecurity defense without compromising on safety or reliability. We’re eager to see how the initial cohort of cyber defenders use this model and we look forward to bringing Carbon to developers, businesses, and consumers soon. Posted in:

title: XREAL AURA: Wired XR glasses to watch, work, and play
body: XREAL AURA: Wired XR glasses to watch, work, and play Oct 28, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link The first wired XR glasses powered by Android XR bring your apps, your shows, and help from Gemini wherever you go. Orders open today in the U.S., Canada, and Korea, and on November 2 in Japan. Shahram Izadi VP & GM, XR Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary We’re launching XREAL AURA, the first wired XR glasses powered by Android XR, to help you work, watch, and play on a private, unbounded canvas. These lightweight glasses project apps into your field of view while keeping you connected to your surroundings, and they feature Gemini to assist with tasks across your screens. You can order your pair today at xreal.com or BestBuy.com to get started. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We launched XREAL AURA, the first wired XR glasses powered by Android XR for your daily tasks. These lightweight glasses project apps onto your field of view while keeping your surroundings clearly visible. You can use Gemini to get help with your apps, documents, and surroundings in real time. A portable compute puck handles processing to provide high performance while you work, watch, or play. You can order these glasses today in the U.S., Canada, and Korea for your personal use. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Shahram Izadi, VP and GM of XR, introduces XREAL AURA, a pair of lightweight glasses that project your apps onto the real world. Because the lenses are transparent, you can see your surroundings while working, watching movies, or playing games on a virtual screen. You can connect these glasses to a portable device to manage multiple windows, use Gemini for help, and view your digital content in 3D anywhere you go. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Today, together with XREAL, we officially launched XREAL AURA , the first wired XR glasses powered by Android XR. 1 AURA is a totally new way to use Android XR. AURA’s XR glasses lenses are transparent, so you can see the real world with your own eyes while projecting spatial content onto your field of view. It makes it natural to use it around your house, at the office, or on a plane. Plus, the 70-degree field of view gives you plenty of room to see more of your spatial and 2D apps all at once. Gemini on Android XR understands what you're seeing and doing, both in the real world and on your screens, so you can have a natural conversation to get help across your apps. AURA’s glasses are also under 95 grams, because the heavy processing happens in a portable compute puck, connected by a cable. It holds the battery and the new Snapdragon® Reality Elite platform from Qualcomm Technologies, Inc., which debuts on AURA, so you get the best of both worlds: high-performance spatial computing and lightweight comfort. Android XR brings the helpfulness of Gemini and millions of your favorite apps from Google Play, including over 150 apps made for XR, to AURA. So wherever you are, you can work, watch, and play with Gemini by your side on AURA’s unbounded canvas. A workspace that travels with you On AURA, you can open up multiple apps at once, like your browser, work documents and your music app, and arrange them around you at any size. Pair a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, or use the puck as a trackpad, for a complete desktop setup anywhere whether you want a massive, multi-monitor display from your couch, at a hotel desk, or on an airplane tray table. With Wired Mirroring, your laptop can join in, too. Plug it into AURA with a USB-C cable that supports video output, and its screen appears as a window you can resize and place anywhere. There’s no software to install and you can use it side-by-side with your Android XR apps on AURA. And because the display is visible only to you, you can open a confidential document in a public space with peace of mind. Plug in your laptop with Wired Mirroring and spread your work across multiple windows. Peacock is only available in the U.S. Gemini works across everything in view, including your laptop window, so you can ask it to tidy up your windows or brainstorm about whatever you're looking at. And starting today, it can do more than talk you through an answer: Share your view, and Gemini can highlight what to focus on, in the room around you or on your screen. Ask Gemini about anything in front of you, like finding places to visit while in Google Maps. A private theater for your shows and memories When it's time to unwind, AURA turns any seat into the best one in the house. Open YouTube, Google TV, or your favorite streaming service and place the screen wherever it's most comfortable. You can dim the lenses to fade out the world around you, and they instantly become transparent again when someone is in view. There's already plenty of immersive content to watch on YouTube and Google TV, from 180- and 360-degree videos to 3D movies. New immersive films and performances made for XR also arrive with AURA today, including “Nevatars”, co-directed by Andy Serkis and Josh Nelson Youssef, “Galapagos: the Last Eden,” narrated by Margot Robbie, from Atlantic Studios, and the San Francisco Ballet's “Nutcracker.” Dim the lenses for a private screen, wherever you’re sitting. For even more, spatial view turns almost any video, photo, or game into 3D with a tap, now supporting higher-resolution content. And with window follow mode, your app will stay centered in front of you allowing you to enjoy your content in any position. It also tucks into a mini view at the edge of your vision when you are on the move, so your path stays clear. Your memories are back in focus too. This year, Google Photos will include a new spatial gallery that wraps your library around you. You can pan from an entire year down to a single day with your hands, then open a favorite memory in 3D. An arcade wherever you are Whether it's getting through a few levels at the airport gate or a long session on the couch, AURA gives your games a bigger screen. Since it's Android, you can play thousands of mobile and tablet games from Google Play or bring in games from your handheld or PC with Wired Mirroring. You can also keep other apps open beside the game, like a YouTube walkthrough or a chat with friends. And if you get stuck while playing an Android title or streaming from your PC or console, just ask Gemini to talk you through your next move, so you don't have to put down your controller. Play your favorites on a bigger screen, or try new games made for XR. Games made for XR, from studios like Owlchemy Labs, and Resolution Games, also appear right in your space, and you can play them naturally with your hands. New ones are coming with AURA, too, including Fallout Factions and Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars. Available to order today XREAL AURA is available for users 18+ to order today in the U.S., Canada, and Korea, and starting November 2 in Japan, with launch pricing starting at USD 1,099 through the end of the year. You can order at xreal.com/aura , or in the U.S. at BestBuy.com with shipments beginning in mid-November. And if you’re looking to bring AURA to your business, check out the Android Enterprise Blog to learn more about scaled deployment options. title: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work
body: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work Oct 28, 2026 | Tina Schuchman CVP, Foundry and Vladimir Fedorov, CTO, GitHub If you want to compete, you need to be multi-model. And if you want to take advantage of everything that different AI models have to offer, you need a great harness. But building one that works seamlessly across multiple models and surfaces is incredibly hard. You need to solve for performance, quality, and cost. And then you have to maintain it, which is even harder. Luckily, the GitHub engineering team built a best-in-class, truly multi-model harness , which we’ve adopted company-wide. The Microsoft Copilot harness powers Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, the GitHub Copilot app, the CLI, VS Code, and more. And today, we’re making that harness available through Microsoft Foundry . That gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. You get the right model for the job without switching the harness or the rest of your tech stack. That frees up your time, energy, and resources to focus on your bottom line. What’s a harness, and why is it hard? If the model supplies the intelligence, the harness is everything around the model. It’s the orchestration layer that gives an agent the right instructions, context, execution environment, and controls to accomplish meaningful work. And a harness worth its salt has support for open standards like MCP and agent skills, as well as agent plugins. This is a fast-moving space. A frontier model today might fall behind tomorrow. And building your own harness or model router to keep up can be painful and slow. Now, you can build on the same harness Microsoft and GitHub ship in our own products, and you don’t have to maintain it. We invest in science and engineering work to continually improve and evolve the harness and ensure high-quality, efficient, and low-cost performance across a range of models and workloads. The benefits compound for us and our customers who use the harness to build and run their own agents. Improve the harness, and every surface it touches benefits. Born in GitHub, battle-tested at enterprise scale The Copilot harness was built by the same GitHub engineers behind new technologies like our multi-model orchestration . And those technologies are only possible because we built our own harness. Designed to be fast, token-efficient, and predictable, it was our original, high-quality harness. And it had the highest satisfaction among our most demanding audience: developers. That’s why we’re standardizing all of our Copilot experiences on the strongest foundation possible. The harness is built to perform across model families , with 20+ frontier models plus bring your own key, so you can use the right model for the right job. Instead of doing the work to keep up with and eval new models, lean on us to intelligently route work to the right model or models based on the task. Our harness is flexible and configurable to any type of app, agent, or service. We recently ported the harness runtime to Rust , which has resulted in industry-leading performance and reductions in both session overhead and time-to-first token. And because the Copilot harness powers surfaces across Microsoft, it’s battle-tested and proven performant at the scale of millions of users and hundreds of real-world use cases. A unified harness lets us ship faster, learn faster, and improve Copilot over time. And because the agents you build in Foundry can run on the same harness we’ve adopted across Microsoft, our continuous harness improvements will benefit your agents, too. Try it yourself The SDK is available to download , or you can run the harness in the cloud, all managed by Foundry. Our platforms remain open and interoperable, so you can continue to bring in any harness and framework you want, too. With the Copilot harness, Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox, with governance and optimization built in from day one. You bring the instructions, skills, tools, and model choice. This is an important step towards our vision of a stronger system around the model that preserves choice. It represents the best of GitHub, brought to the Microsoft platform and beyond. We’ll keep pushing the harness forward, so you can focus on what only you can build. Tags: GitHub , GitHub Copilot , Microsoft Copilot , Microsoft Foundry

title: Thin, Light and Built for Everything: NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows Laptops Gain New Models, Agent Tools and Games
body: Thin, Light and Built for Everything: NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows Laptops Gain New Models, Agent Tools and Games NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Liquid AI’s LFM3 models arrive for local AI; plus, Hermes Agent adds NVIDIA OpenShell and Switchyard, and ‘Phantom Blade Zero’ launches with NVIDIA DLSS 4.5. October 28, 2026 by Shreevar Rastogi 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA RTX Spark powers thin and light laptops built for everything that developers, creators and gamers do. RTX Spark laptops are now available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI. These powerful systems combine an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and an NVIDIA Grace CPU in a single superchip with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance. That puts the NVIDIA CUDA platform, RTX graphics and the capabilities of a personal AI supercomputer inside premium Windows laptops built to go anywhere. New and expected RTX Spark updates, coming soon, include: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open weight speech model for transcription, speaker attribution and translation is available on RTX Spark. The LFM3 family of open models with day-zero support. Resource management controls in NVIDIA App to allocate GPU resources between foreground apps and background agents. Phantom Blade Zero , S-GAME’s highly-anticipated action role-playing game, launches with ray tracing and NVIDIA DLSS 4.5. Experience Minecraft with path tracing and DLSS with RTX Remix1.6, available now for RTX Spark. Turn Recorded Audio Into Useful Information With NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe Introduced today, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a new, open weight speech model that turns recorded conversations into useful information. Instead of needing multiple models for transcription, speaker labels and translation, developers can use one promptable model that handles all three, plus questions about the audio. It transcribes 40 languages, including seven Indic languages. Developers guide the model with plain-language prompts. For example, for a single recorded meeting, users can ask it to: “Transcribe this recording and label each speaker.” “Translate this audio into English.” “List what decisions were made in this meeting.” Prompts can also include product terms and formatting conventions, which helps the model handle specialized vocabulary in fields like healthcare, financial services and customer service. Because the weights are open, developers can choose where audio is processed, from a desktop to the cloud. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ranks No. 1 on the Hugging Face Open ASR and No. 2 among open weight models on Artificial Analysis — delivering leading accuracy with approximately 4.3 billion active parameters, 80% fewer than the No. 1 open weight model, making high-quality, intelligent transcription more practical on local hardware. It’s available today on Hugging Face in the BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 formats, and offers flexible deployment options for developers with support on NVIDIA RTX Spark, DGX Spark systems and Jetson AGX Thor devices. Developers can deploy NVFP4 versions through NeMo-Speech.cpp or vLLM. Learn more in the NVIDIA technical blog . Control How Agents and PC Apps Share GPU Resources On RTX Spark, users can have long-running agents working alongside their favorite applications. Both share the system’s GPU compute, and the right balance of resources depends on what matters to users at that moment. With the new resource management feature in NVIDIA App , users can now choose how GPU resources are shared. They can prioritize their foreground app for the best performance, or give their background-running agent more resources to get work done faster. Access control resource sharing from System > Advanced in the NVIDIA App. This feature requires hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling to be enabled in Windows Settings. Liquid AI : One Model Family, Many Ways to Work Liquid AI’s LFM3 provides a new generation of Liquid Foundation Models designed for specialized tasks. The family spans text, vision, audio, omni and decision models built on one shared backbone, with base and post-trained models available as open weights. The models are compact and fast: Liquid AI’s new 1.7-billion-parameter base model outperforms its previous 2.6-billion-parameter base model. These models support local workflows such as agents running in Hermes Agent, Pi and OpenClaw to triage inboxes and manage calendars, read documents and app screens, transcribe and translate speech, answer spoken questions about handwritten math, and route support tickets or voice requests. Developers can run LFM3 models on RTX Spark with native support through llama.cpp and vLLM, and fine-tune the models locally. ‘Phantom Blade Zero’ Launches With DLSS 4.5 S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero launches tonight, Oct. 28, at 7 p.m. PT on Steam and the Epic Games Store . Players can take on the role of Soul, a swordsman framed for his master’s murder, as he travels the martial world to uncover a conspiracy. NVIDIA worked with S-GAME Studio and S-GAME Publishing to add ray-traced effects to the title. On RTX Spark laptops and GeForce RTX GPU-powered PCs, ray tracing adds more accurate bounced lighting, detailed reflections and realistic shadows on foliage and terrain. The NVIDIA DLSS Dynamic Multi Frame Generation feature boosts frame rates with up to 6x frame generation, or adjusts the multiplier on the fly to hit a player’s target frame rate. Read more on GeForce.com . RTX Remix Breathes New Life Into Classics NVIDIA RTX Remix , the modding platform for remastering classic games with path tracing and DLSS, released version 1.6 last week. This update brought RTX Remix to the world’s largest gaming community: Minecraft . Both creators and players can render Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1 through RTX Remix with DLSS-accelerated path tracing and take full advantage of realistic lighting and materials in their future creations. The update also adds DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, up to 6x Multi Frame Generation, native RTX Spark support and agent-assisted workflows. Starting today, those upgrades come to Portal with RTX and the Half-Life 2 RTX demo. Both now support RTX Spark, with DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering for more lifelike lighting and materials, a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation and new options that speed up path tracing. RTX Remix 1.6 also makes AI-powered modding simpler. A redesigned ComfyUI workflow lets modders generate physically based materials directly inside RTX Remix, with no application programming interface setup, batch processing for full projects and presets for less technical creators. Plus, with NVIDIA agent skills, compatible AI agents can work directly with RTX Remix to help speed up remastering projects. Learn more in the RTX Remix blog . RTX Spark Laptops: Beautifully Designed, Built for Everything RTX Spark laptops come in a range of designs, so users can choose one that fits how they work and play. Options include different screen sizes, colors, touchscreens, pen support and two-in-one convertibles. RTX Spark laptops are as thin as 14mm and as light as three pounds, with all-day battery life. Such slim designs are possible because RTX Spark places the GPU, CPU and up to 128GB of unified memory on one power-efficient superchip. Creative projects and AI models draw from the same memory pool, so a laptop can take on work that used to call for a desktop workstation, even when unplugged. Here’s what this means for: AI developers: Run models and agents locally on NVIDIA CUDA — the same platform that powers AI in the cloud — with a path to deploy across more than 150 million NVIDIA RTX AI PCs and NVIDIA GPUs in the cloud. Creators: RTX Spark can edit camera native 4:2:2 video and render 3D scenes of up to 90GB. Adobe Photoshop and Premiere offer native RTX Spark support through beta releases. Gamers: Hundreds of games run on RTX Spark, with NVIDIA DLSS, ray tracing, Reflex and G-SYNC delivering sharper visuals and smoother, more responsive gameplay. RTX Spark laptops are available now from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599, with 128GB configurations on shelves. Find a laptop on the RTX Spark product page . #ICYMI: More Updates From NVIDIA Local AI 🦆Microducks learn to walk with help from RTX Spark: During the GTC Berlin keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed how AI agents running on RTX Spark can help train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot . A new NVIDIA technical blog walks through the workflow: Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt plan an obstacle course on RTX Spark, Astra builds the 3D assets, NVIDIA Isaac Lab trains the navigation policy and RTX Spark validates it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Watch the demo and try the playbook . ⚡ NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is now available , enabling natural conversations and multistep agent tasks with as little as 4GB of memory. The model powers local voice assistants, game characters and embedded interfaces on RTX Spark, DGX Spark, GeForce RTX GPUs and NVIDIA Jetson devices. It supports llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio, and works with Hermes and OpenClaw. For more demanding agent workloads, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run local agents on RTX Spark. 🖼️Black Forest Labs’ FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6-billion-parameter open weights model that lets users generate and edit images locally. NVIDIA-optimized versions run on RTX GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM. Developers can also fine-tune the model on RTX Spark using an NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel recipe to customize it for specific creative workflows. 🖥️ NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB is now available to purchase from manufacturer partners, giving developers and researchers another way to build and run AI locally. Powered by the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, it combines 64GB of unified memory with DGX OS and the NVIDIA AI software stack for agent development, inference and fine-tuning. Learn more and explore purchase options . Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X , Instagram , TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter . Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X . See notice regarding software product information. title: Treasury Sanctions Facilitators of DPRK IT Worker Fraud Targeting U.S. Businesses
body: October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK’s unlawful weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and ballistic missile programs. “The North Korean regime continues targeting and exploiting American companies through fraudulent activities conducted by its overseas IT operatives, who weaponize sensitive data and extort businesses for substantial payments,” said S ecretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury will continue to use all available tools to protect U.S. businesses from these malicious activities and hold those responsible accountable.” The DPRK continues to rely on fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and fabricated personas to conceal its IT workers and secure employment with legitimate companies, including those in the United States and allied countries.  The DPRK regime then appropriates most of these workers’ wages, generating hundreds of millions of dollars to fund its unlawful WMD and ballistic missile programs.  Today’s action targets key facilitators and financial networks that help sustain these schemes and move illicit proceeds on behalf of the DPRK.  These networks have leveraged sophisticated cryptocurrency transactions, money laundering techniques, and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence tools, to generate and transfer millions of dollars for the DPRK government.  In addition to generating revenue, DPRK IT workers have exploited their access to corporate networks to deploy malware, exfiltrate sensitive data, and steal proprietary information, creating significant risks for businesses worldwide. Today’s action builds on OFAC’s March 12, 2026 designation of a separate DPRK IT worker network and demonstrates Treasury’s sustained commitment to dismantling the networks that generate illicit revenue for the DPRK.  These networks permeate through the global financial system, necessitating a unified response to match the threat.  The United States is joined this month by Australia and the European Union in designating individuals and entities supporting the DPRK’s revenue generation and military activities.  Treasury continues to take these actions in close partnership with the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT) Participating States and other international partners.  Working with allies and partners, the United States will continue to expose and disrupt those enabling the DPRK to evade sanctions and finance its unlawful weapons programs. More information about the tactics utilized by DPRK IT workers and steps that can be taken to protect private networks can be found in advisories and alerts regarding DPRK IT workers issued by the Departments of State, Treasury, and Justice ; the FBI ; and a multilateral consortium of law enforcement . KEY ENABLERS OF GLOBAL DPRK IT WORKER NETWORKS OFAC’s action today targets several DPRK IT worker networks by designating facilitators and DPRK IT workers based in the DPRK and Russia. Vitold Viktorovich Obertas (Obertas) is a Russian intermediary for illicit DPRK financial transactions, including for Amnokgang Technology Development Company (Amnokgang). OFAC designated Amnokgang in its March 12, 2026 action. Since January 2025, Obertas has conducted nearly $2 million worth of cryptocurrency conversions, as well as at least $1.25 million in other currency transactions, for DPRK officials. OFAC is designating Obertas pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, the Government of North Korea. DPRK-national Limited Liability Company Alis (Alis) lead Kim Ki Hyok leads a Russia-based delegation of DPRK IT workers, whose primary duties include monitoring Alis IT workers and ensuring they meet their financial targets. OFAC designated Alis in March 2024 for being subordinate to the Chinyong Information Technology Cooperation Company (Chinyong), which OFAC designated in May 2023. Since 2024, Kim Ki Hyok has transferred cryptocurrency for the delegation valued at nearly $500,000. Additionally, DPRK national Kim Hyo Dong leads a separate Russia-based Chinyong-subordinate delegation. Since at least December 2023 Kim Hyo Dong has provided logistical assistance to the IT worker delegation, engaged in sanctions evasion efforts, and facilitated the transfer of over $100,000 equivalent in financial assets. OFAC is designating Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong pursuant to E.O. 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Chinyong. Since 2024, Russian national Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov (Boykov) has actively supported Alis by exchanging and converting an equivalent of $3.5 million in cryptocurrency transactions, monitoring cryptocurrency transactions, and providing logistical support for Alis. OFAC is designating Boykov pursuant to E.O. 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Alis. Since at least 2024, the **First Financial and Technical Development Center (**FFTDC) is a DPRK-controlled entity located in Russia that uses DPRK IT workers who have generated several millions of dollars on behalf of the DPRK government. The FFTDC has deployed several highly trained DPRK IT workers to Russia who employ Super Intelligence (SI) tools and use sophisticated money laundering methods, including complex cryptocurrency transfers, to facilitate their revenue generation schemes. Since 2025, Russia-based DPRK IT workers Kim Kyong Ju, Ri Thae Chol, So Hyon Jin, Han Yu Song, Kim Sung Gwan, and Hyon Se Il have collectively generated over $750,000 on behalf of the FFTDC. OFAC is designating FFTDC pursuant to E.O. 13722 for having engaged in, facilitated, or been responsible for the exportation of workers from North Korea, including exportation to generate revenue for the Government of North Korea or the Workers’ Party of Korea. Additionally, OFAC is designating Kim Kyong Ju, Ri Thae Chol, So Hyon Jin, Han Yu Song, Kim Sung Gwan, and Hyon Se Il pursuant to E.O. 13722 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, FFTDC. title: Treasury Sanctions Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Financial Institution Supporting M23
body: October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) imposed sanctions on the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society, a Rwandan financial institution that has played a key role in facilitating Rwanda’s support for the March 23 Movement (M23) and its political wing, the Congo River Alliance. “Today, the United States makes good on President Trump’s promise to hold Rwanda accountable for its commitments under the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC. On October 12, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation announced its formation as the successor to the Congo River Alliance.  M23 is a U.S.- and United Nations-designated armed group that has illegally seized territory in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).  With support from Rwanda’s security apparatus, including the deployment of thousands of troops and provision of military equipment, logistics, and training, M23 has captured key population centers and mining areas in eastern DRC, where it has perpetrated human rights abuses, subjected civilians to exploitation and forced labor, and contributed to a severe humanitarian crisis marked by mass displacement. The historic U.S.-brokered Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity (Washington Accords) were signed by the DRC and Rwandan heads of state on December 4, 2025.  In addition to paving the way for a peaceful resolution to the conflict in eastern DRC, the Washington Accords incorporated a regional economic framework to expand trade and investment, enhance transparency in critical minerals supply chains, and promote greater investment in the Great Lakes Region of Africa. THE RWANDAN MINISTRY OF DEFENCE: ENABLING REBELLION IN EASTERN DRC The Rwandan Ministry of Defence ( Rwandan MoD ) is the umbrella organization for Rwanda’s security services, including the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), which OFAC sanctioned on March 2, 2026 .  At the direction of the Rwandan MoD, the RDF has deployed thousands of troops across eastern DRC’s North and South Kivu provinces, where they conduct operations alongside M23 and provide the armed group with military equipment, supplies, logistical support, and training.  The RDF has also introduced advanced weaponry to the battlefield, including surface to air missile systems and jamming equipment, creating risks for civilian aviation in eastern DRC. Since its rebellion reemerged in 2021, M23 has carried out extrajudicial killings, unlawful detentions, and torture or other physical abuses in areas under its control.  In early 2025, M23 captured Goma and Bukavu, the provincial capitals of North and South Kivu provinces, respectively.  M23 has also taken control of mining areas in eastern DRC, including gold mines in South Kivu province and Rubaya, an expansive area for coltan mining in North Kivu province.  In M23-controlled mining areas, civilians have been subjected to forced labor, dangerous working conditions, and illegal “taxation” schemes.  Minerals sourced from M23-controlled territory are integrated into supply chains in Rwanda, whose domestic mining capacity is smaller than export volumes reported since M23’s rebellion began.  On July 8, 2024 , the U.S. Department of State issued a statement of concern related to mineral supply chains that contribute to ongoing instability in eastern DRC. The Rwandan MoD is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13413, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, logistical, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of the RDF. ZIGAMA: FINANCING REBELLION, PARTICIPATING IN MINERALS SMUGGLING Zigama Credit and Savings Society ( Zigama ) is a Rwandan financial institution that operates on behalf of Rwanda’s security services.  Zigama has facilitated payments to entities in China and additional countries for weapons, ammunition, and other military equipment for the RDF.  Zigama has also facilitated payments for RDF travel and accommodation for training activities. As Treasury highlighted in a previous designation , the RDF and M23 control gold mining sites in South Kivu province.  Following the removal of gold from these sites, Rwandan government forces have maintained strict oversight of the gold.  A Zigama branch enabled the transportation of gold sourced from M23-controlled territory in eastern DRC to Kigali.  In addition, Zigama has facilitated financial transactions for M23 and the Congo River Alliance, amounting to tens of millions of dollars. Zigama is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13413, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, logistical, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the RDF, M23, and the Congo River Alliance. title: Indie Games Fund in Africa: Meet the selected studios
body: Indie Games Fund in Africa: Meet the selected studios Oct 28, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Google Play has selected 10 independent game studios across Sub-Saharan Africa for the 2026 Indie Games Fund Africa, providing $1 million in non-dilutive funding, mentorship, and technical support to help scale local talent and bring authentic African games to a global audience. Nicola Julius Head of Ecosystem and Core Partnerships EMEA, Google Play Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Indie Games Fund Africa: Meet the selected studios Sub-Saharan Africa is home to some of the world's most vibrant storytelling, cultural richness, and creative ingenuity, powering one of the fastest-growing game development ecosystems on the planet. Earlier this year, we opened applications for the first-ever Google Play Indie Games Fund in Africa, committing $1 million to help bridge the funding gap, overcome international distribution barriers, and support talented indie developers across the continent. Today, we are thrilled to announce the 10 independent game studios selected for the 2026 cohort. Each of these studios will receive a share of non-dilutive funding, alongside direct access to commercial and growth resources, hands-on 1:1 mentorship from Google Play specialists, and tailored technical support from Unity. This support is designed to help them optimize their titles, scale sustainably, and bring authentic African stories and gameplay mechanics to a worldwide audience. Meet the 10 selected studios From action platformers, cozy puzzles, and rhythm games to immersive simulations, meet the studios shaping the future of African gaming: Clockwork Acorn (South Africa): A South African indie game studio founded in 2014 by industry veterans dedicated to making timeless games, supporting local talent, and creating a positive impact through their work. Jetstream is an elegant puzzle game featuring over 100 hand-crafted levels, a calming minimalist art style, and unique mechanics that challenge players to guide a plane through the clouds. Deluxe Entertainment Studios (Nigeria): An independent studio creating distinct games featuring striking visuals, bold ideas, and unique stories rooted in African imagination for global audiences. Their title Rasta Santa is an action-packed 2D platformer set in Lagos, where you play as an undercover cop disguised as Santa, waging war on traffickers to rescue children and defend an orphanage. Disputed People (South Africa): A South African studio founded in 2023 that is dedicated to crafting rich, character-driven video games filled with creativity, quality, and wonder-filled experiences. Their title Mitts and the Divine Recipes is a 3D retro-inspired adventure game where players explore the cozy world of Epicuria, gathering divine ingredients, cooking meals to gain special abilities, and solving puzzles to advance. Fer Factor (Nigeria): An independent game development studio based in Lagos, Nigeria, dedicated to crafting fun, innovative, and memorable gaming experiences for players worldwide. Their title Chore Master is a cozy and satisfying game where players use intuitive controls to clean spaces, scrub stains, and transform chaotic rooms into spotless, picture-perfect environments. Gazuntype Entertainment (Nigeria): The independent game development alias of Tade Ajiboye, an innovative builder with over a decade of experience crafting immersive video games and VR experiences in Nigeria. Their title Go North is a cozy, story-driven exploration adventure where players guide Dara through beautifully unique mazes, discover magical items, and uncover a sinister mystery. Leti Games Limited (Ghana): A pioneering African creative technology studio based in Ghana, dedicated to bringing authentic African stories and innovations to global audiences through games and interactive experiences. Their title Sweave is a rhythm-based, hyper-casual mobile game inspired by traditional African weaving techniques, where players navigate a dynamic weaving ball across a digital loom while dodging cultural obstacles and battling bosses. Maliyo Games (Nigeria): A Lagos-based studio founded in 2012 that creates engaging, African-inspired gaming experiences celebrating local culture for a global audience. Their title Safari City is a vibrant mobile puzzle and renovation game where players solve match-3 puzzles and restore a rundown town into a beautiful, thriving community. Studio Bo (South Africa): An animation and games company based in Cape Town, South Africa, known for bringing a playful visual style and quirky humor to interactive experiences, animations, and upcoming mobile titles. Their title Idle Sands is a cozy 2D idle-clicker where players manage a fleet of robots to clean up a beach, uncover treasures, and automate their operations with relaxing music and charming artwork. Vetkoek Studios (South Africa): A youth-owned South African game development studio dedicated to creating high-quality, accessible mobile games with authentic African themes while empowering the next generation of local creators. Their title Taxi Ranked is a casual, retro-style driving game capturing the chaos and humor of South African minibus taxis through vibrant comic-book graphics, multiple game modes, and deep vehicle customization. Weza Interactive (Kenya): A Kenyan game studio founded by twin brothers Odongo George Ahere and James Ahere to build original, culturally rich worlds that educate, empower, and entertain global audiences. Their title Riziki is a free-to-play mobile rhythm adventure where players guide twins Nabo and Moja across Africa, tapping and swiping to Afrobeats, Amapiano, and Rhumba to restore harmony and bring vibrant environments to life. Congratulations to all 10 studios. We're excited to champion your vision as you continue crafting unforgettable experiences for players around the world. Posted in:

title: Owner of Now-Closed Adult Family Home Sentenced to Federal Prison for Healthcare Fraud
body: Press Release Owner of Now-Closed Adult Family Home Sentenced to Federal Prison for Healthcare Fraud Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Wisconsin Brad D. Schimel, First Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, announced that on October 22, Lori Butts (age 49) was sentenced to 28 months’ incarceration for committing a healthcare fraud scheme through which she stole $1,253,920.47 from a Medicaid-funded program designed to provide residential care services for disabled Wisconsin residents. Butts previously operated Lordan Care Adult Family Homes, a company that provided residential services to Medicaid beneficiaries. The government authorizes these services on a beneficiary-by-beneficiary basis. All residents in the program are placed in a multi-bedroom apartment that has 24-hour supervision by a caregiver. Some residents also receive one-on-one care from a worker, in addition to this caregiver. Butts admitted that from July 2019 to December 2020, she billed for hours of care work never provided. In particular, she billed for two workers to provide dedicated service, 24 hours per day, to a single resident—but those caregivers were not present.  In addition to personally enriching herself at the expense of taxpayers, Butts took resources away from extraordinarily needy and vulnerable individuals who qualified for a high level of care. Butts’s adult family homes were severely understaffed and experienced frequent police contact, often when staffing levels were insufficient to address volatile or inappropriate resident conduct. In announcing the sentence, United States District Judge J.P. Stadtmueller emphasized the “reprehensible” nature of the conduct. He noted that “the taxpayers were bilked” because they paid for tens of thousands of hours of caregiver time that Butts’s company simply did not provide. By billing for unworked hours and accepting the agency’s money, Butts engaged in conduct that was the “functional equivalent of grand larceny.” Judge Stadtmueller also explained that the significant sentence he imposed was necessary to send a message of deterrence to others considering engaging in fraud against government healthcare programs. In addition to the 28-month prison sentence, Judge Stadtmueller ordered Butts to pay restitution to Medicaid of $1,253,920.47. “When the defendant stole this money, she took it from every American taxpayer and diverted it from individuals who needed help,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Schimel. “The U.S. DOJ is laser focused on punishing those who defraud our federal healthcare benefit programs.” “Lori Butts exploited a government program and stole from the American taxpayers by billing for services never provided to disabled Wisconsin adults,” said FBI Milwaukee Special Agent in Charge Alan Karr. “The FBI is committed to working with our law enforcement partners to hold accountable individuals who defraud the government for personal gain and enrichment. The message is clear, if you steal from American citizens, justice will find you.” “Lori Butts billed for care she never provided and collected money she never earned,” said Robert J. Kuszynski, Acting Special Agent in Charge, IRS Criminal Investigation, Chicago Field Office. “Behind every claim is a promise to care for someone. Butts turned that promise into a payday. Her prison sentence is the price of that choice.” The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigations unit investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorneys Carter B. Stewart and Zachary J. Corey prosecuted the case. On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. # # # For further information contact: Public Affairs Officer Steve Caballero (414) 297-1700 Follow us on X Updated October 28, 2026 Component USAO - Wisconsin, Eastern

title: Fraud Scheme Exposed: 2 From Texas and New York Stole COVID Federal Housing Funds from NC HOPE Program
body: Press Release Fraud Scheme Exposed: 2 From Texas and New York Stole COVID Federal Housing Funds from NC HOPE Program Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of North Carolina USANCE.PublicInfoOfficer@usdoj.gov WILMINGTON, N.C. – Daquan Copeland, 35, of Houston, TX and Esless White Sr., 51, of Jamaica, NY, pleaded guilty in federal court to Conspiracy to Commit Mail Fraud by engaging in a scheme with others to defraud the federal government of more than $187,000. Each faces up to 30 years in federal prison and a fine of up to one million dollars when they are sentenced later this year. “These two leeches bled dollars from federal programs designed to help those in need. Now they sit and wait for the gavel of justice to hammer down their sentence,” said U.S. Attorney, Ellis Boyle. “Anyone who defrauds any of our taxpayer programs will be held accountable. Know this, we are watching, we will catch you, we will prosecute you. Crime Doesn’t Pay! Cheaters. Never. Win.” Copeland and White applied for emergency rental assistance through the North Carolina Housing Opportunities and Prevention of Evictions (NC HOPE) program. As part of their scheme, they and others submitted fake tenant leases for several properties in Lenoir County to support their applications. Between November 2020 and December 2021, Copeland, White, and others submitted 23 fraudulent applications and stole more than $187,000 in government housing funds for their personal use. On March 27, 2020, Congress passed the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act to provide emergency financial support to millions of Americans affected by the economic fallout of the COVID‑19 pandemic. As part of this relief, the CARES Act authorized $5 billion for Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) programs, giving states and local governments flexible federal funding to prevent, prepare for, and respond to the pandemic. The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) manages the CDBG program, which supports economic and community development and provides long‑term recovery funding to states and localities after disasters and emergencies. “Daquan Copeland and Esless White participated in a conspiracy that diverted more than $180,000 in limited taxpayer funds for their own enrichment, depriving a pandemic relief program of resources intended to help people struggling to remain in their homes," said Special Agent in Charge Jerome Winkle with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Inspector General (OIG).  “This was not a victimless crime.  Every dollar stolen was a dollar unavailable to help someone pay rent during an unprecedented national crisis.  HUD OIG remains committed to working alongside our prosecutorial and law enforcement partners to aggressively pursue those who exploit HUD programs for personal gain.” "This case reflects the strength of our partnerships with the USAO-EDNC and HUD-OIG in fighting fraud, waste and abuse that hurts our most vulnerable citizens,” said NCSBI Director, Chip Hawley. “Thanks also to USMS and the Kinston Police Department for their help. We will continue to aggressively target those who steal from hardworking taxpayers." The State of North Carolina’s Office of Recovery and Resiliency, a division of the North Carolina Department of Public Safety under then – Governor Roy Cooper, gave away federal funds made available in the CARES Act to supposedly North Carolina renters to ostensibly let them stay in their homes during COVID-19 by preventing evictions and the loss of utility services.  The NC HOPE program utilized an initial $51.5 million allocation of CDBG funds from the CARES Act to provide housing and utility assistance.  The State of North Carolina also received CRF funds from the CARES Act, of which $66 million was allocated to pay administrative costs associated with the NC HOPE program. Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina made the announcement after Chief U.S. District Judge Richard E. Myers II accepted the plea. The United States Department of Housing and Urban Development – OIG, and the SBI are investigating the case. A copy of this press release is located on our website . Related court documents and information can be found on the website of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina or on PACER by searching for Case No. 4:26-CR-14-M.
