title: Russian Woman Charged With Federal Hate Crimes For Stabbing Multiple Jewish Individuals
body: Press Release Russian Woman Charged With Federal Hate Crimes For Stabbing Multiple Jewish Individuals Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of New York United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Assistant Director in Charge of the New York Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”), James C. Barnacle, Jr., and the Commissioner of the New York City Police Department (“NYPD”), Jessica S. Tisch, announced today that ANNA MOCHALOVA was arrested on charges of committing hate crimes in connection with her assaults of two Jewish men in and around the Diamond District in Manhattan on October 21, 2026.  MOCHALOVA was transferred from state custody earlier today and will be presented in Manhattan federal court before U.S. Magistrate Judge Robert W. Lehrburger. “This Office will continue to seek justice for victims of hate-based crimes and will aggressively prosecute those who seek to spread bigotry through violence,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald.  “As alleged, Anna Mochalova deliberately and viciously targeted Jewish victims with violence.  Mochalova allegedly stabbed two men specifically because they were Jewish, an attack made all the more terrifying because the specific weapon used—and its potential contents—remain unknown pending further investigation. Mochalova’s alleged actions were an attack on the fundamental right to freely and safely express one’s religious identity in public.” “Acts of hate and harassment have no place in our city,” said FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle, Jr. “The alleged hate-motivated crimes committed against Jewish members of our community are unacceptable and have no place in New York.  We will continue to use the full force of the law to protect the safety, security, and rights of every New Yorker, including members of our Jewish community.” “A hate crime is a message written in violence, and this defendant’s message was loud and clear,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch.  “As alleged in the complaint, Anna Mochalova attacked two visibly Jewish New Yorkers, striking fear in an entire community.  Every New Yorker has the right to walk our streets safe from hatred and violence, and the NYPD will always hold those who threaten that right accountable.  I thank the NYPD investigators and our federal partners for responding swiftly to this unacceptable act of hate.” As alleged in the Complaint and other public filings: [1] On or about October 21, 2026, MOCHALOVA attacked two Jewish men in quick succession with a sharp object that is consistent with being a needle in and around the Diamond District in Manhattan.  First, at approximately 5:50 p.m., Victim-1, a Jewish man, was walking along West 47th Street between Fifth and Sixth Avenues when he noticed MOCHALOVA following him and speaking in Russian.  Shortly thereafter, MOCHALOVA stabbed Victim-1 in his lower back with a sharp object, which Victim-1 described as the feeling of a needle prick. At the time, Victim-1, who has a beard, was wearing attire traditionally worn by Orthodox Jewish men, including a black hat, a black suit, a white shirt, and tzitzit. MOCHALOVA then stalked past him towards Sixth Avenue.  A still image of the assault is depicted below: Shortly thereafter, MOCHALOVA approached Victim-2 and a second man (“Individual-1”), who were standing together on the northeast corner of Sixth Avenue and West 45th Street, approximately two blocks south of the location where Victim-1 was assaulted. Victim-2 and Individual-1 are also Jewish men, and both were wearing yarmulkes when MOCHALOVA approached. MOCHALOVA bumped into Victim-2 multiple times. As Victim-2 started to confront MOCHALOVA about her repeated bumps, he observed MOCHALOVA stab him with a sharp object on his right forearm. Victim-2, who speaks Russian, recalls that MOCHALOVA spoke in Russian and told him, in sum and substance, “run away, I have a gun.” MOCHALOVA also asked Individual-1, in sum and substance, if he was Jewish. Individual-1 responded, in sum and substance, “I don’t know, I’m Muslim?” MOCHALOVA told Individual-1 that she “was so sorry” and then fled northbound on Sixth Avenue. *                *                * MOCHALOVA, 32, of Russia, is charged with two counts of committing hate crimes, each of which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. The statutory maximum sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendant will be determined by a judge. Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative work of the FBI and the NYPD. The prosecution of this case is being handled by the Office’s Civil Rights and Human Trafficking Unit in the Criminal Division, with consultation from the Criminal Section of the Civil Rights Division.  Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kaiya Arroyo and Christian Ronald are in charge of the prosecution. The charges contained in the Complaint are merely allegations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. Contact Nicholas Biase, Shelby Wratchford (212) 637-2600 Updated October 28, 2026 Attachment u.s._v._mochalova_-_sealed_complaint.pdf Topics Civil Rights Human Trafficking Component USAO - New York, Southern Press Release Number: 26-305

title: Two Men Ordered to Pay $86,000 in Total Fines and Restitution for Illegal Deer Hunting Operation in Fayette County
body: Press Release Two Men Ordered to Pay $86,000 in Total Fines and Restitution for Illegal Deer Hunting Operation in Fayette County Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Tennessee Jackson, TN – A federal judge has ordered Austin Elrod , 30 , of Somerville, Tennessee, to surrender his hunting license for 5 years and to pay a total of $60,000 for an illegal deer hunting operation. D. Michael Dunavant, United States Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee, announced the sentence today. An investigation by several law enforcement agencies revealed that Elrod was guiding white-tailed deer hunts in the Fayette County area without the required guiding license. The guided hunts were advertised on Facebook and resulted in the illegal harvesting of seven deer throughout the 2021 and 2022 hunting seasons. Elrod’s clients included out-of-state hunters from Georgia. One of these hunters was Thomas Boswell, 39 , of Barnesville, Georgia. Boswell participated in the guided hunts without a Tennessee hunting license and was responsible for the illegal harvesting of five of the deer. The harvested deer would then be transported to Georgia. Fayette County is designated by the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency (TWRA) as a Chronic Wasting Disease Zone. Chronic wasting disease is a fatal neurological illness that is contagious to members of the deer family. There is currently no known cure for the disease. Prosecutors charged Elrod and Boswell with violating the Lacey Act, a federal conservation law that bans the trafficking of illegally harvested wildlife. At Elrod’s sentencing hearing on October 21, 2026, Senior United States District Judge J. Daniel Breen placed him on 1 year of probation and ordered that Elrod’s hunting privileges be suspended for a period of 5 years. In addition, Elrod was ordered to pay a $40,000 fine and $20,000 in restitution. Boswell was sentenced in July 2026 and was ordered by Judge Breen to pay a $15,000 fine and $11,000 in restitution. Boswell’s hunting privileges were ordered suspended for a period of 18 months. U.S. Attorney D. Michael Dunavant said, "The U.S. Attorney’s Office is a full-service federal prosecution office, and we have the ability and intention to charge any violations of federal law, no matter where they occur in the Western District of Tennessee. These prosecutions demonstrate our commitment to upholding the rule of law, and to pursuing any cases that harm and impact our rural communities. We commend the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and TWRA for their diligent and thorough work in this successful investigation and appreciate our partnerships with them." “America’s wildlife belongs to all of us. Those who take it illegally put their own interests ahead of everyone who hunts responsibly, values wildlife, and wants healthy populations for the next generation,” said Assistant Director Doug Ault, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Office of Law Enforcement. “Strong partnerships with our state counterparts make this work possible. Together, we will hold those who violate wildlife laws accountable.” This case was investigated by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency, and the Georgia Department of Natural Resources. Assistant United States Attorney Immanuel Chioco prosecuted this case on behalf of the government. ### For more information, please contact our Media Relations Team at USATNW.Media@usdoj.gov . Follow the U.S. Attorney’s Office on Facebook or on X at @WDTNNews for office news and updates. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Wildlife Component USAO - Tennessee, Western

title: Prior Felon Indicted by Federal Grand Jury for Carjacking and Illegal Gun Possession After Shooting Three Victims in Fayetteville
body: Press Release Prior Felon Indicted by Federal Grand Jury for Carjacking and Illegal Gun Possession After Shooting Three Victims in Fayetteville Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of North Carolina USANCE.PublicInfoOfficer@usdoj.gov RALEIGH, N.C. – On September 22, 2026, a federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Robert Page, 52, of Cumberland County, with attempted carjacking, carjacking, discharging a gun in furtherance of carjacking, and possessing a gun by a convicted felon. According to the first charge, Page tried to steal a Toyota 4Runner from two victims who were sitting at a Hardees drive-thru while intending to kill or seriously injure them. One victim suffered serious injuries during the attempted carjacking. In the second charge, the Grand Jury found probable cause Page stole a Chevrolet Malibu from another victim that same day, again acting with the intent to kill or seriously injure. That victim also suffered serious bodily injury. The third charge alleges that Page fired a gun, shooting a female, during the carjacking of the Chevrolet Malibu. The fourth indictment states that Page, a convicted felon, illegally possessed a gun on August 30, 2026. The events leading to Page’s indictment took place on the morning of August 30, 2026. That morning, Page took part in a domestic shooting in Cumberland County. He then attempted to carjack two victims and stole their Toyota 4Runner. During the attempt, he pulled out a handgun and shot one of the victims as she sat inside the vehicle; the bullet passed through her arm and into her chest. Page fled to a nearby parking lot, where he carjacked another victim by shooting her at point‑blank range and taking the keys to her Chevrolet Malibu. By the grace of God, all three victims survived being shot at close range. After the third shooting, law enforcement located Page driving a Ford Focus in Fayetteville and pulled him over. Page exited the car and surrendered, leaving a handgun on the driver’s seat. If convicted, Page faces up to 25 years in prison for attempting to carjack the Toyota 4Runner and for carjacking the Chevrolet Malibu. He also faces a mandatory minimum of 10 years and up to life in prison for firing a gun during the carjacking of the Chevrolet Malibu, and up to 15 years in federal prison for possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina, made the announcement. The ATF is investigating the case. An indictment is merely an accusation. The defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty. A copy of this press release is located on our website . Related court documents and information can be found on the website of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina or on PACER by searching for Case No. 5:26-CR-194-FL-RJ. title: Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election and Early Voting Announced
body: Press Release Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election and Early Voting Announced Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nebraska The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska , in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division , announced its comprehensive strategy today to oversee federal voting protections and investigate potential election fraud as early voting continues in Nebraska for the 2026 midterm elections . The initiative is part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible voting process. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, alongside federal law enforcement partners, is prepared to enforce federal election laws vigorously while protecting the right of every legal voter to cast their ballot without intimidation or interference. Voters can consult official Department of Justice and state portals to review federal election laws and eligibility requirements. Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election: Protecting Voter Rights: Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion. Voter Eligibility and Enforcement: Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. For detailed information on ongoing reviews, eligibility laws, or federal penalties, please consult official Department of Justice guidelines and state election authority resources. Combating Election Fraud: Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing. Federal oversight will remain active throughout the early voting period to monitor for compliance with the Voting Rights Act and ensure that secure ballot drop boxes and polling locations are unhindered. Reporting Election Irregularities The public plays a critical role in maintaining election security. Anyone who witnesses or has direct knowledge of potential election fraud, voter intimidation, or unlawful voting activity is strongly encouraged to report it immediately. Please visit the official FBI Tips Portal or contact local law enforcement to report potential election fraud or voting irregularities. Complaints regarding voter discrimination or civil rights violations can also be directed to the Civil Rights Division via the Department of Justice Civil Rights Reporting Portal . Contact Amy Donato 402-661-3700 Updated October 28, 2026 Components Civil Rights - Voting Section USAO - Nebraska

title: Federal jury convicts dual U.S.-Jamaican citizen for murder-for-hire and drug-trafficking conspiracy
body: Press Release Federal jury convicts dual U.S.-Jamaican citizen for murder-for-hire and drug-trafficking conspiracy Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Virginia Four other conspirators were previously convicted in this Homeland Security Task Force case NORFOLK, Va. – A federal jury convicted Antwan Denetrick Hue, 42, today on charges of conspiracy to commit murder for hire, murder for hire, murder while engaged in drug trafficking, and conspiracy to manufacture and distribute cocaine. According to court records and evidence presented at trial, from 2015 to 2019, Hue, 42, managed an international drug trafficking organization. Hue and Regina Sade Chen, aka Erica Williams, 36, imported multi-kilogram quantities of cocaine into the United States from the Caribbean, including Jamaica. Hue and Chen employed transporters, including co-defendants Kayla Bedessie, 34, and Deshawn Hassan Mercer, 33, to smuggle cocaine into and money out of the United States. Hue frequently traveled between the United States and Jamaica as well as other Caribbean countries to meet with co-conspirators and oversee the smuggling operation. When Hue applied for a renewal of his expiring U.S. passport in 2016, he was informed that he was not eligible because he was in arrears on child support payments owed to the mother of his minor child. In November 2016, Hue hired Mercer and co-defendant Zquan Leon Steeps, 32, to murder the mother, believing her death would permanently end future child support payments and allow him to renew his passport. On Dec. 4, 2016, Mercer, Steeps, and Denasha Campbell (who is now deceased) traveled to the victim’s home in Norfolk. After Campbell knocked and asked to use the victim’s phone, Mercer and Steeps forced their way into the residence and shot and killed the victim in front of her 9-year-old child. The conspirators fled the residence, leaving the child to call 911. After learning that child support remains effective after the death of a parent, on Dec. 24, 2016, Hue negotiated with the victim’s mother for her to have full custody of his son so long as Hue was discharged from all further child support payments. On Oct. 22, 2018, Hue, citing an urgent need to travel to Montego Bay, Jamaica, applied for and obtained a renewal of his passport. In August 2019, the Department of Homeland Security arrested Hue in Florida as he attempted to take possession of a kilogram of cocaine. Hue faces a mandatory life sentence in prison when sentenced on March 4, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Chen pled guilty on Aug. 29, 2024, to conspiracy to manufacture, distribute and possess with intent to manufacture and distribute cocaine. She faces a mandatory minimum of 10 years and up to life in prison. Bedessie pled guilty on Aug. 29, 2024, to conspiracy to manufacture, distribute and possess with intent to manufacture and distribute cocaine. She was sentenced on Sept. 8, 2025, to seventy months in prison. Mercer and Steeps pled guilty in October 2024 to conspiracy to commit murder for hire. They face a mandatory minimum of life in prison. Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia; Ian Kaufmann, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI’s Richmond Field Office; and Kai Wah Chan, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Washington, D.C., made the announcement after U.S. District Judge Arenda Wright Allen accepted the verdict. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Joseph E. DePadilla and Brian J. Samuels are prosecuting the case. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Washington, D.C., comprises agents and officers from the FBI; Homeland Security Investigations; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; Drug Enforcement Administration; Diplomatic Security Service; U.S. Marshals Service; U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service; Naval Criminal Investigative Service; Transportation Security Administration Federal Air Marshals Service; U.S. Customs and Border Protection; Enforcement and Removal Operations; and Washington Baltimore HIDTA, with the prosecution being led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia. Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 2:24-cr-38. body: Press Release CONVICTED SEX OFFENDER SENTENCED TO 36 MONTHS IN FEDERAL PRISON FOR FAILURE TO REGISTER Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Louisiana Patrick Sullivan, age 32, of Donaldsonville, Louisiana, was sentenced to 36 months in federal prison following his conviction for failing to register as a sex offender. U.S. District Judge John W. deGravelles further sentenced him to serve five years of supervised release following his term of imprisonment. According to admissions made as part of his guilty plea, Sullivan was convicted of sexual assault of a child in Dallas County, Texas, in July 2021, and was sentenced to three years imprisonment. During his plea, he admitted to traveling to Baton Rouge, Louisiana in 2024 and later to Donaldsonville, Louisiana, where he established residency and domicile in January 2025. Sullivan admitted to knowingly failing to register as a sex offender in Louisiana. U.S. Attorney Kurt L. Wall praised the hard work of the United States Marshal’s Service.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Lyman E. Thornton III led the prosecution. title: Venezuelan National Pleads Guilty to Jackpotting Conspiracy and to Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material
body: Press Release Venezuelan National Pleads Guilty to Jackpotting Conspiracy and to Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Alabama PROJECT SAFE CHILDHOOD ANNISTON, Ala.  – A Venezuelan national has pleaded guilty to charges involving ATM jackpotting and child-exploitation, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr. Rodner Josue Centeno Moreno, 22, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Court Judge Corey L. Maze to conspiracy. Moreno’s co-defendant, Deiber Jorhen Castillo Rodriguez, 26, a citizen of Venezuela, was charged with conspiracy and attempt to access a protected computer in furtherance of fraud. As of this date, Rodriguez has not been arrested. Also, in a separate-but-related case, Moreno pleaded guilty to possession of child pornography based on evidence obtained in the course of investigating the jackpotting scheme. According to the plea agreements, in the early morning of June 14, 2026, an officer with the Pell City Police Department observed an SUV parked in front of an ATM at a bank in Pell City, Alabama. The officer turned around to go back to the ATM, and the SUV was not there but the ATM was open with its interior parts exposed.  The officer later discovered the SUV abandoned in the bank parking lot. During the investigation the Pell City Police Department discovered that the ATM had been breached using a technique called “jackpotting” – a criminal scheme that involves breaching the computing compartment of an ATM allowing it to be operated without authorization. A search warrant was obtained for the abandoned vehicle.  During the search of the vehicle, officers discovered tools, gloves, cash, a cell phone, and a wallet containing multiple bank cards and a temporary driver’s license in the name of Moreno with an address in Murfreesboro, Tennessee. Later in the same day, an officer with the Murfreesboro Police Department contacted the Pell City Police Department to inform them that Moreno had called them to turn himself in for attempting to rob the ATM in Pell City.  Officers with the Murfreesboro Police Department drove to Moreno’s residence and took him into custody. Moreno was the passenger in the vehicle driven by Castillo-Rodriguez.  On June 15 th , officers with the Pell City Police Department travelled to Murfreesboro to execute the arrest warrants for Moreno. After Moreno’s arrest, a search warrant was executed on his iPhone and officers discovered dozens of files containing child sexual abuse material. “The defendant’s guilty pleas reflect the seriousness of two distinct crimes – ATM jackpotting, which threatens the security of our financial institutions, and the possession of child sexual abuse material, which compounds the harm the victims have suffered,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “We remain committed to holding offenders accountable and protecting both the security of our communities and the most vulnerable among us – our children.” “ATM jackpotting continues to be a growing threat nationwide, causing significant financial losses and impacting communities across the country,” said U.S. Secret Service Special Agent in Charge Patrick Glaze. “Through a joint investigation conducted by the Pell City Police Department and the U.S. Secret Service Birmingham Cyber Fraud Task Force, investigators identified evidence of child sexual abuse material on Moreno's mobile device. The possession of child sexual abuse material is a serious crime that inflicts lasting harm on victims and their families while undermining the safety and well-being of the community. We are committed to identifying and prosecuting individuals who engage in these offenses and to protecting vulnerable victims from further exploitation.” This case was brought in part in accordance with Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . If you suspect or become aware of the possible sexual exploitation of a child, please contact law enforcement.  Reports can also be filed with the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) or online at www.cybertipline.org . The United States Secret Service investigated the case along with the Pell City Police Department with assistance from the Murfreesboro, Tennessee, Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Ryan P. Niedermair is prosecuting the cases. Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Project Safe Childhood Violent Crime Component USAO - Alabama, Northern

title: Rocky Mount Tax Preparer’s $3.9M Fraud Empire Crumbles, She Confesses Guilt
body: Press Release Rocky Mount Tax Preparer’s $3.9M Fraud Empire Crumbles, She Confesses Guilt Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of North Carolina USANCE.PublicInfoOfficer@usdoj.gov RALEIGH, N.C. – Chowan Watson, 55, of Rocky Mount, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of aiding and assisting in the preparation of a false tax return resulting a tax loss of approximately $3,900,000. Watson faces a maximum penalty of 36 months in federal prison when sentenced later this year.  She has agreed to pay restitution to the IRS. “Watson and Dickens didn’t just bend the rules—they broke the door wide open,” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle. “For years, they engineered a scheme that faked withholdings, pumped up refunds, and drained the U.S. Treasury of nearly four million dollars. They preyed on the trust of hardworking Eastern North Carolinian taxpayers and twisted a legitimate tax preparation service into a personal profit machine. This case sends a clear message to all fraudsters: if you cheat the system and exploit your clients, we will expose your scheme, pursue you, and prosecute you. Cheaters. Never. Win.” Watson and Angela Dickens, who previously pleaded guilty operated Empire Tax Service, later renamed K&J Tax Service, in Rocky Mount. From 2017 to 2023, Watson and Dickens fraudulently filed hundreds of tax returns by inflating “Other 1099 Withholding” amounts. Their scheme inflated taxpayer refunds and allowed them to take excessive fees from those refunds.  Total tax losses are approximately $3.9 million. “Those who attempt to undermine the integrity of the American tax system should understand IRS Criminal Investigation follows the money to uncover fraudulent schemes,” said Special Agent in Charge Donald “Trey” Eakins, IRS Criminal Investigation’s Charlotte Field Office.” IRS-CI, partnered with the U.S. Attorney’s Office, will continue to relentlessly pursue anyone who seeks to defraud the tax system and ensure offenders are brought to justice.” On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina made the announcement after Chief U.S. District Judge Richard E. Myers II accepted the plea. IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case. A copy of this press release is located on our website . Related court documents and information can be found on the website of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina or on PACER by searching for Case No. 5:26-CR-125-M. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Fraud Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - North Carolina, Eastern

title: Accountant Sentenced to Federal Prison for Money Laundering, PPP Fraud
body: Press Release Accountant Sentenced to Federal Prison for Money Laundering, PPP Fraud Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas AUSTIN, Texas – An Austin accountant was sentenced in federal court to 41 months in prison for money laundering and bank fraud that undermined the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, between October 2023 and July 2024, Arun Mago, 47, laundered $150,000 in cash that he knew to be the proceeds of cocaine distribution. The investigation revealed that in addition to his money laundering activities, Mago also engaged in repeated loan fraud during the COVID-19 pandemic. From about April 4 to Nov. 23, 2021, Mago applied for and received several fraudulent PPP loans and Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) for several business entities totaling nearly $1 million. Bank records revealed that Mago transferred the funds into his personal bank account and used them for multiple real estate purchases. “Arun Mago not only defrauded the United States government during the chaotic COVID-19 pandemic but continued down his criminal path to launder a substantial amount drug money,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “Mago thought that he was untouchable and an expert fraudster, but now he knows otherwise. The Trump Administration has prioritized prosecuting fraudsters who steal from the American people, and the Western District of Texas has, once again, met that mission. This office and our federal law enforcement partners will always hold accountable those who steal from the American taxpayer and undermine our federal programs.” “Mago, who was a certified public accountant, wrote a book with a chapter titled ‘Black Money’ and claimed money laundering and tax evasion schemes were untraceable. I can only imagine his shock when we traced his more than $900,000 of COVID loan fraud and also got him on money laundering charges in an undercover operation,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher J. Altemus Jr., of IRS Criminal Investigation's Texas Field Office. “Money always leaves a trace and criminals always think they are smarter than law enforcement. You can earn certifications, you can write books, but, when you break the law, we write the final chapter by taking your money and your freedom.” In addition to the imprisonment, U.S. District Judge Robert Pitman ordered Mago to pay over $900,000 in restitution and a $250,000 fine. IRS-CI and the Office of the Texas Attorney General investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Keith Henneke prosecuted the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Fraud COVID-Related Fraud Financial Fraud Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Texas, Western

title: Justice Department Releases Eighth Annual Elder Justice Report
body: Press Release Justice Department Releases Eighth Annual Elder Justice Report Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Today, the Department of Justice’s Civil Division released its Annual Report to Congress on its efforts to Combat Elder Fraud and Abuse . The report summarizes the department’s extensive enforcement, victim support, training and myriad other efforts to promote elder justice during the reporting period from July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026. This year, the Department pursued nearly 350 criminal and civil enforcement actions involving fraud or abuse that targeted or disproportionately affected older adults. Approximately 96% of the cases were criminal in nature and 45% involved international schemes. These cases named 712 defendants charged with stealing or alleged to have stolen $4,841,305,931 from 711,353 victims. During that same period, the Department also engaged in nearly 1200 public awareness and training events, reaching over 62 million Americans.  The Department also helped to organize and participated in the Never Ever Campaign , a public-private coordinated consumer education effort to raise awareness about government and business imposter scams, collectively reaching over 95 million individuals. The Department continued to develop training and resources to support the efforts of state and local prosecutors, law enforcement, victim service providers, and elder justice multidisciplinary teams. Of note this year, the Department supported the development of an online training titled Toolkit for Law Enforcement and Emergency Medical Services When Called to a Long-Term Care Facility, with over 700 professionals taking the course in the first month of its release.  The Department also continued to actively support older victims, whether harmed by family members or strangers. For example, Victims of Crime Act funded organizations allocated $52 million to elder abuse victim services. Further, the Department was able to return millions to older victims, or freeze millions, through a variety of programs. The Department is committed to advancing elder justice through enforcement, public awareness, resources and training for elder justice professionals, and support for older victims and their families.  The Department stands united in its fight against elder abuse, neglect, financial exploitation and fraud to improve the quality of life for older Americans. For more information on elder fraud and abuse, visit the Department’s Elder Justice Initiative website. If you or someone you know has been the victim elder fraud, please call the National Elder Fraud Hotline at 833–FRAUD–11or or 833–372–8311. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Elder Justice Component Civil Division Press Release Number: 26-1270

title: Convictions through Guilty Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions (October 19 through October 23, 2026)
body: Press Release Convictions through Guilty Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions (October 19 through October 23, 2026) Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico, Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting United States Attorney, in conjunction with our partner agencies in the Homeland Security Task Force (“HSTF”) announce the following prosecutorial results for the week of October 19 through October 23, 2026. The HSTF is a permanent, interagency law enforcement task force created by executive order to combat transnational criminal organizations—including cartels, trafficking networks, and foreign terrorist organizations. Convictions through Guilty Pleas: On October 22, 2026, Steven Nieves-Ríos pleaded guilty to violating 21 U.S.C. §§ 952(a), 960(a)(1), (b)(1)(B)(ii), and 963, and 8 U.S.C. §§ 1324(a)(1)(A)(i), (a)(1)(A)(v)(I), and (a)(1)(B)(i) in Criminal Case 25-393 (SCC).  According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with conspiracy to import 5 kilograms or more of cocaine and conspiracy to illegally bring in aliens. Defendant was arrested on September 12, 2025. SAUSA Cody McKinney in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 23, 2026, Julio Jeury Tejada Contreras pleaded guilty to violating 21 U.S.C. §§ 963, 952(a), and 960(b)(1)(B)(ii), 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(1)(A), and 8 U.S.C. § 1326(a) in Criminal Case 26-265 (CVR). According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with conspiracy to import 5 kilograms or more of cocaine, carrying a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking crime, and attempted reentry of a previously removed alien.  Defendant was arrested on June 11, 2026. The court set defendant’s sentencing date for January 25, 2026. SAUSA Cody McKinney in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 23, 2026, José Ayala-Rivera pleaded guilty to Count one in Criminal Case 26-143 (GMM). According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with Conspiracy to Receive, Transfer and/or send Firearms via a Common Carrier without Written Notice in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 371. Defendant was arrested on April 30, 2026.  The court set defendant’s sentencing date for January 25, 2027. On October 23, 2026, Joselin A. Méndez-De Jesús pleaded guilty to a violation of Title 8, United States Code, Sections 1326(a) and (b)(1) in Criminal Case No. 26-343 (SCC) and was sentenced to time served by United States District Court Judge Silvia Carreño-Coll. According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with an illegal re-entry offense and was found in the United States after being previously removed from the United States subsequent to a felony conviction. Sentencings: On October 20, 2026, Sergio Ramírez-Payano was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Gina Méndez-Miró to 12 months of incarceration for possessing a machinegun. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on 2 October 2025, in Criminal Case 25-409 (GMM), and pleaded guilty on July 21, 2026. AUSA Joseph Russell is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 22, 2026, Yanzie Vázquez-González was sentenced by United States District Court Silvia Carreño Coll to 204 months (17 years) of imprisonment and 10 years of supervised release for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on June 10, 2025, in Criminal Case 25-272 (SCC) and pleaded guilty on July 22, 2026. AUSAs Laura Díaz-González and Andres Orr in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 23, 2026, Carlos Gutiérrez-Santana was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Camille Vélez-Rivé to a term of imprisonment of 120 months (10 years) and five years of supervised release for a federal drug trafficking violation. According to court documents, a superseding indictment was filed against the defendant on February 18, 2026, in Criminal Case 25-462 (CVR), and pleaded guilty on July 21, 2026. AUSAs Antonio Pérez and Myriam Fernández are in charge of the prosecution of the case. These prosecutions are part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Juan comprises agents and officers from the following federal partners: FBI, ICE-HSI, CBP (OFO, AMO and Border Patrol), the U.S. Marshals Service for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, DEA, ATF, IRS, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the Department of State, and the U.S. Secret Service, the Puerto Rico/U.S. Virgin Islands HIDTA, TSA, FAA, and the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The HSTF also has the following state and local law enforcement partners as participating agencies: the Puerto Rico Police Department; the San Juan, Carolina, Guaynabo, Barceloneta, and Ponce Municipal Police Departments, the Puerto Rico National Guard – Counter Drug Program; the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation; the Puerto Rico Internal Revenue Service (Hacienda); the Puerto Rico Port Authority; and the Virgin Islands Police Department. ### Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Homeland Security Task Force Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Puerto Rico U.S. Marshals Service Press Release Number: 2026-116

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio CLEVELAND  - The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio, in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division, announced its comprehensive strategy to oversee federal voting protections and address potential election related violations. As part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible election process, U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer has named Executive Assistant U.S. Attorney Ava Rotell Dustin and Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Shepherd as the 2026 District Election Officers. They will oversee the northern Ohio district’s handling of Election Day complaints in consultation with the Justice Department’s Civil Rights, Criminal, and National Security Divisions in Washington. “My office has partnered with federal, state, and local law enforcement to maintain election security, enforce federal laws, and address credible threats swiftly,” said U.S. Attorney Toepfer. “If you witness—or have direct knowledge of—suspected election fraud, voter intimidation, or unlawful voting activity, we strongly encourage you to report it immediately.” Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election: • Protecting Voter Rights : Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion. • Voter Eligibility and Enforcement: Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. •    Combating Election Fraud: Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing. AUSAs Dustin and Shepherd will be on duty in the Northern District of Ohio while the polls are open Tuesday, Nov. 3, to respond to complaints of voting rights concerns or fraudulent election activity. They will ensure that such complaints are directed to the appropriate authorities. For Northwestern Ohio, call EAUSA Dustin at 419-241-0767; for Northeastern Ohio, call AUSA Shepherd at 216-622-3859. Complaints about possible violations of the federal voting rights laws may also be made directly to the Civil Rights Division in Washington at civilrights.justice.gov or by phone at 1-855-856-1247. In the case of a crime of violence or intimidation, call 911 immediately and before contacting federal authorities as state and local police have primary jurisdiction over polling places. Contact Jessica Salas Novak Jessica.Salas.Novak@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Ohio, Northern

title: Oxford Drug Dealing Felon Sentenced to 8 Years in Federal Prison
body: Press Release Oxford Drug Dealing Felon Sentenced to 8 Years in Federal Prison Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of North Carolina USANCE.PublicInfoOfficer@usdoj.gov NEW BERN, N.C. – A federal judge sentenced Shamar Wayquis Evans, also known as “sly dollar”, 35, to eight years in federal prison for possessing in a gun by a convicted felon and possession with intent to sell crack. He pleaded guilty on June 16, 2026. “This gun toting and drug pushing ne’er–do-well will pose no threat to the law-abiding citizens of Eastern North Carolina. Through hard work, focus, driven efforts by local and federal law enforcement, we removed him from our community,” said Ellis Boyle, EDNC U.S. Attorney. “This case demonstrates our commitment to holding accountable those who endanger our neighborhoods and families through violence and selling deadly drugs. Simple lesson; drugs kill, prison awaits, do better.” From September 2025 through January 1, 2025, ATF and the Oxford Police Department investigated Evans’s drug‑trafficking activities. Law enforcement officers conducted multiple controlled purchases of crack from Evans. On January 3, 2025, officers executed search warrants at two residences connected to Evans. At the first residence, officers found a firearm and drug paraphernalia in his bedroom. At the second residence, officers located Evans with 14 grams of crack inside his jacket. Evans is a previously convicted felon with several North Carolina state court convictions, including assault with a deadly weapon on a government official and selling heroin in 2017, and selling heroin 2018. “When a convicted felon possesses of a gun, the threat of violence increases putting innocent lives at risk,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge Alicia Jones. “ATF is committed to protecting our communities by identifying the biggest threats to our public safety and holding them accountable for their crimes.” "The results of this case are a testament to the hard work and dedication of the law enforcement community at the Local, State, and Federal levels. We understand the unique challenges that come along with drug enforcement, but we will be relentless in our efforts to pursue those who threaten our communities by distributing dangerous drugs and illegally possessing firearms,” said Chief Brandon Goins of the Oxford Police Department. “This investigation took time, resources, and tenacity and highlights our continued commitment to removing dangerous drugs and illegal firearms from our streets. The Oxford Police Department remains committed to working collaboratively with our partners to ensure the safety of our community.” Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina made the announcement after the sentencing before U.S. District Judge Louise W. Flanagan.  ATF and the Oxford Police Department investigated this case. A copy of this press release is located on our website . Related court documents and information can be found on the website of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina or on PACER by searching for Case No. 5:25CR00238FL-1. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Operation Take Back America Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - North Carolina, Eastern

title: Monroe Man Recently Convicted on Federal Drug Trafficking and Firearm Offenses Indicted Again for Alleged Assault in Federal Courthouse of Court-Appointed Defense Attorney
body: Press Release Monroe Man Recently Convicted on Federal Drug Trafficking and Firearm Offenses Indicted Again for Alleged Assault in Federal Courthouse of Court-Appointed Defense Attorney Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Louisiana MONROE — The United States Attorney’s Office announced that Sirkeameo Vandrell Johnson , 32, of Monroe—previously convicted by a federal jury for multiple drug trafficking and firearm offenses—was indicted again on October 21, 2026, for assault allegedly committed during his prior court proceedings. “The Sixth Amendment’s right to counsel requires citizen-attorneys to step up and serve that core constitutional function for our communities, and their safety while performing that important service is essential to maintaining our Constitutional society,” said U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller. “Our Office has zero tolerance for any assault that occurs inside a federal courthouse and will investigate and prosecute any such assault to the fullest extent of the law.” Previously, on September 30, 2026, following a two day trial before United States Chief District Judge Terry A. Doughty, Johnson was found guilty of Conspiracy to Possess with Intent to Distribute Methamphetamine, Distribution of Methamphetamine, Possession with Intent to Distribute Methamphetamine, Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon, and Possession of a Firearm in Furtherance of a Drug Trafficking Offense. For these crimes, Johnson faces a mandatory minimum sentence of at least fifteen years and up to life imprisonment. Sentencing in this case is scheduled for January 6, 2027, and a press release is available here. The new indictment alleges that on September 30, 2026, the same day as his prior conviction and while still in the federal courthouse, Johnson assaulted the victim, a court-appointed Criminal Justice Act attorney who was representing Johnson in a criminal case, by “striking, beating, and wounding him.” U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement. The case is being investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Casey Stelly with assistance from Legal Assistant Kimberly Blanchard. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the United States District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer. The case number for this matter is 3:26-cr-00413. CONTACT: Public Affairs (337) 262-6704 Cara.Alexander@usdoj.gov www.justice.gov/usao-wdla Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Louisiana, Western

title: San Antonio Man Sentenced to Over 15 Years in Federal Prison for Meth Dealing
body: Press Release San Antonio Man Sentenced to Over 15 Years in Federal Prison for Meth Dealing Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Texas SAN ANTONIO – A San Antonio man was sentenced in a federal court to 190 months in prison for conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of a substance containing methamphetamine, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas. According to court documents, Alfredo Landin aka “Fredo,” 28, imported large amounts of methamphetamine, which he called “candy,” from Mexico, and distributed it to numerous dealers in the San Antonio area. Landin arranged to have drivers deliver 10 or more kilograms of narcotics at a time in hidden compartments. On July 19, 2021, the Drug Enforcement Administration and Texas Department of Public Safety found approximately eight kilograms of methamphetamine and 3.5 kilograms of heroin in a car that was on its way to drop narcotics off to Landin in Indian Creek. Landin was arrested on April 19, 2024, and pleaded guilty on March 4, 2025. In June, Landin was sentenced to 151 months in a separate case in which he also pleaded guilty to trafficking methamphetamine. “Alfredo Landin was responsible for importing large amounts of methamphetamine and heroin from Mexico to exploit our communities for financial gain,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “Thanks to the tireless efforts of our DEA and DPS partners, we were able to interdict a large shipment of narcotics just before it was delivered to Landin, who will now spend more than 15 years in federal prison concurrent with another 12 ½-year sentence he is already serving.” “Coordinated law enforcement efforts are critical to keeping our communities safe and removing those who peddle poison in San Antonio neighborhoods,” said Miguel A. Madrigal, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration San Antonio Division. “DEA San Antonio remains relentless in its mission to stay one step ahead of drug traffickers, dismantle criminal networks, and bring those responsible to justice.” The DEA and TX DPS investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Eric Yuen prosecuted the case. ### Contact USATXW.MediaInquiry@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Texas, Western

title: Federal jury finds Indian national guilty of unlawfully voting  in 2024 Presidential Election
body: Press Release Federal jury finds Indian national guilty of unlawfully voting  in 2024 Presidential Election Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas FORT WORTH, Texas – United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a federal jury convicted Indian national Khalwinder Singh Bhengura of voting by an alien in a federal election and making a false claim of U.S. citizenship to register to vote. After a two-day trial before U.S. District Judge Mark T. Pittman, the jury deliberated for several hours and returned its verdict Oct. 27. “Voting in our national elections is reserved for US citizens,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Every unlawful vote undermines the voices of eligible citizens, and this office will hold accountable anyone who undermines our elections. This verdict reflects the jury’s careful consideration of the evidence and our commitment to protecting the integrity of the electoral process in North Texas.” According to evidence presented at trial, Bhengura, a citizen of India, became a lawful permanent resident of the United States on June 29, 2022. He is not a U.S. citizen and has never applied for citizenship. On Aug. 1, 2024, Bhengura applied for a Texas driver license in Tarrant County. In that application, he checked boxes stating that he was a U.S. citizen and wished to register to vote. Based on that application, Bhengura was registered to vote in Texas. Voter Registration Application where Bhengura fraudulently confirmed he was a U.S. citizen On Nov. 5, 2024, the defendant voted in person at the East Library and Recreation Center in Arlington, Texas, in a general election that included races for President, Vice President, U.S. Senate and U.S. House of Representatives. Tarrant County voter info showing Bhengura illegally voted in the 2024 General Election Sentencing is set for Feb. 11, 2027. Bhengura faces up to five years in federal prison and a fine of up to $250,000 for false statements of citizenship in order to register to vote and up to one year imprisonment and maximum fine of $100,00o for voting by an alien in a federal election. Bhengura could also be subject to immigration penalties such as removal from the United States after he serves his term of imprisonment. The HSI Dallas field office conducted the investigation with assistance from the Election Integrity Unit of the Texas Office of the Attorney General and the Tarrant County District Attorney’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Capoccia and Colin Duffy from the Fort Worth Division prosecuted the case. ### Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Fraud Voting and Elections Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Minneapolis Man Sentenced to 33 Months’ Imprisonment for Unlawful Possession of a Machine Gun
body: Press Release Minneapolis Man Sentenced to 33 Months’ Imprisonment for Unlawful Possession of a Machine Gun Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Minnesota ST. PAUL – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that Amiir Mawlid Ali, of Minneapolis, was sentenced to 33 months in prison for one count of unlawful possession of a machine gun. Ali was previously found guilty on April 16, 2026 , by a federal jury trial. According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, on June 3, 2025, Minneapolis Police Department Officers executed a traffic stop on a silver sedan due to multiple traffic violations. The car had three occupants, including the defendant who was in the front passenger seat. When officers removed Ali from the vehicle to conduct a safety sweep, Ali attempted to flee but officers apprehended him before he could escape. Officers found a firearm equipped with a machine-gun conversion device under Ali’s seat during the safety sweep. The backseat squad car video shown at trial shows Ali instructing the other occupants to deny knowledge of the machine gun of which was found to have Ali’s DNA on it. Officers learned the same day that the firearm had been reported stolen. An expert at the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosive examined the firearm and established that it was able to fire multiple rounds of ammunition with a single pull of the trigger, making it operate as a machine gun. One of the officers recognized Ali as a member of the “Muddy” street gang, known to law enforcement for its history of suspected involvement in weapons offenses. Ali was initially released following his arrest for this offense. On June 5, 2025, the United States filed a complaint alleging possession of a machine gun. Law enforcement then executed a federal warrant and arrested Ali on the scene of a suspected gang-related shooting at a Twin Cities high school graduation. Officers heard Ali scream, “you missed,” to an individual believed to be involved in the incident. “The defendant possessed an extremely dangerous weapon that is capable of extreme damage. Today’s sentence ensures that this defendant is held accountable for the public safety threat that he posed to the community,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen. “While violent crime rates are down across the board, we have seen far too much gang violence in the Twin Cities over the past few months,” said FBI Minneapolis Field Office Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson. “As we work relentlessly to secure our neighborhoods, the FBI Safe Streets Task Force and our state and local partners continue to prioritize investigations of gang members driving violence with illegal firearms. Today’s sentence should be a message to gang members across the state—when you carry an illegal firearm, justice will find you.” This case was the result of an investigation by the FBI and Minneapolis Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Albania Concepcion prosecuted the case. Contact usamn.pressoffice@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Minnesota

title: Albuquerque Man Sentenced for Drug Trafficking and Machinegun Offenses
body: Press Release Albuquerque Man Sentenced for Drug Trafficking and Machinegun Offenses Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – An Albuquerque drug trafficker who amassed an arsenal of firearms, including machinegun conversion devices, and hundreds of grams of methamphetamine and fentanyl has been sentenced to nearly 29 years in federal prison. According to court documents, on July 6, 2024, Deundalas Gales , 37, was driving at a high rate of speed in Albuquerque, New Mexico, when he crashed into another vehicle. Immediately after the crash, Gales fired approximately 25 rounds toward the other vehicle from a handgun equipped with a machinegun conversion device. Although the other vehicle sustained multiple gunshots, the other driver was fortunately not struck. Gales then fled the scene on foot, abandoning the vehicle that contained 447.1 grams of methamphetamine with 99% purity, and a stolen shotgun. As he fled, Gales dropped the firearm with the conversion device, his wallet and other personal belongings that allowed investigators to eventually identify him. On July 13, 2024, officers responded to reports that Gales was breaking into a neighbor’s apartment and setting fire to his own apartment. Officers found Gales bleeding, wearing body armor and holding a loaded firearm magazine. After safely detaining him, Albuquerque Police Department officers entered his smoke-filled apartment to check for occupants and observed firearms and fentanyl pills in plain view. Investigators subsequently obtained a search warrant for the apartment and recovered 216.5 net grams of fentanyl, 892.7 net grams of methamphetamine, five firearms, a black powder revolver, approximately 500 rounds of ammunition, digital scales and multiple firearm magazines. During the investigation, detectives also searched Gales vehicle that was parked at the apartment. Investigators recovered approximately 204 grams of fentanyl, 112.8 net grams of methamphetamine and five additional firearms, including a machinegun conversion device. As a previously convicted felon with prior convictions for assault, aggravated robbery, and possession of a controlled substance, Gales was prohibited from possessing a firearm and ammunition. Gales pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, possessing and brandishing a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, unlawful possession of a machinegun and being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition. Upon his release from prison, Gales will be subject to five years of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Robert “Eric” Castañeda of the Drug Enforcement Administration made the announcement today. The Drug Enforcement Administration investigated this case with assistance from the Albuquerque Police Department and FBI’s Albuquerque Field Office. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Mexico prosecuted this case. Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - New Mexico Press Release Number: 26-295

title: Former Waverly Postmaster Sentenced in Wire Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Former Waverly Postmaster Sentenced in Wire Fraud Scheme Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Iowa Federal Conviction is her Sixth Theft Related Conviction The former postmaster of Waverly, Iowa, was sentenced on October 26, 2026, to five years of probation and eight months of home confinement. Merri Ann Burgart, formerly known as Merri Ann Bentley, age 43, from Hazelton, Iowa, received the sentence after a May 13, 2026, guilty plea to one count of wire fraud. In a plea agreement and at her sentencing hearing, Burgart admitted that she stole over $16,000 from the United States Postal Service (“USPS”) in about 2023.  Burgart made false entries in the USPS’s travel mileage system in order to obtain reimbursements for fictitious mileage that she allegedly incurred while delivering mail on rural routes in a personal vehicle.  For example, on August 19, 2023, Burgart falsely claimed reimbursement for 727 miles she had allegedly driven on “Route 1” in the Waverly area, which was not true, and as a result she received mileage reimbursement to which she was not entitled.  Burgart earned nearly $100,000 a year at the time she was stealing from the USPS. In her plea agreement, Burgart also admitted that, in 2022, she recruited a former postmaster to set up a funnel bank account to conceal Burgart’s criminal conflict of interest.  Between August 2022, and September 2023, Burgart caused the USPS to pay more than $2,500 for lawn mowing services by means of the funnel account and in spite of Burgart’s conflict of interest with the ultimate recipients of the funds. Burgart has a significant criminal history.  Burgart has five prior theft convictions.  In 2005, Burgart was working as an in-home hospice worker and repeatedly stole from families while she was providing care to hospice patients in their own homes.  In 2025, Burgart was convicted of operating while intoxicated.  Law enforcement officers responded to a dispute at a bar, outside of which Burgart was beating on a Jeep.  Officers later found Burgart was driving a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol content of .121.  Burgart received probationary sentences in state court for all six of these prior state court convictions. Burgart was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Chief Judge C.J. Williams.  Burgart was sentenced to five years of probation, including eight months of home confinement.  She was ordered to make $16,404.86 in restitution to the USPS and fined $4,000. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars.  Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Timothy L. Vavricek and investigated by the United States Postal Service, Office of Inspector General. Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl . The case file number is 25-CR-2060. Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Iowa, Northern

title: DOJ Honors Northern District of West Virginia Team Member for Superior Performance
body: Press Release DOJ Honors Northern District of West Virginia Team Member for Superior Performance Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of West Virginia CLARKSBURG, WEST VIRGINIA – U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey is proud to announce that a member of his staff has received an Executive Office for United States Attorneys (EOUSA) Director’s Award for her outstanding work in the Northern District of West Virginia. Laurel K. Jones, a Legal Administrative Specialist in Litigation Support in the district’s Clarksburg office, has been honored with the Superior Performance Award in Litigation Support. “Laurel’s teamwork and reliability make her a trusted and valued colleague, and her courtroom expertise has helped improve our litigation support policies and practices.  Laurel takes pride in her own work as well as work of her colleagues, which motivates her to ensure our district performs at its best.  Laurel, thank you for your service, your leadership, and your commitment to our policies and priorities at the Department of Justice,” said U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey. The award is one of the most prestigious honors within the Department of Justice, recognizing exceptional excellence and dedication to the department’s mission. Jones has served the district for nearly 20 years. In her role, she supports trial litigation, organizes discovery, and manages litigation software databases, providing essential assistance to the office’s mission. She is a 2000 graduate of Glenville State University, where she earned an associate’s degree in paralegal studies. The EOUSA Director’s Awards were held on October 28, 2026 at the Robert F. Kennedy Main Justice Building Great Hall in Washington, D.C. EOUSA provides executive and administrative support for the 93 U.S. Attorneys located throughout the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Guam, the Marianas Islands, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Such support includes legal education, administrative oversight, technical support, and the creation of uniform policies. Learn more here . title: Box Elder man sentenced to more than 2 years in prison for unlawfully possessing handgun
body: Press Release Box Elder man sentenced to more than 2 years in prison for unlawfully possessing handgun Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana GREAT FALLS – A Box Elder man who previously had been convicted of multiple felonies and was found with a handgun was sentenced today to two years and 10 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, U.S. Attorney Scott Twito said. Celestion Charlie Ortega, 40, pleaded guilty in April 2026 to unlawfully possessing a firearm. Chief U.S. District Judge Brian M. Morris presided. The government alleged in court documents that Ortega, who has been convicted of five previous felonies, was discovered by law enforcement in a Great Falls parking lot at 2:30 a.m. on Sept. 29, 2025, after someone reported seeing him peering into cars with a handgun. Ortega at first pretended to be asleep but then cooperated with officers, who searched Ortega’s vehicle and found a loaded Hi-Point 9mm pistol between the front right and rear passenger seats on the floorboard. Officers then searched Ortega and found a round of ammunition in his back pocket. The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. The Great Falls Police Department, Montana Department of Corrections Probation and Parole, and ATF conducted the investigation. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. Contact Keri Leggett Acting Public Affairs Officer keri.leggett@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Project Safe Neighborhoods Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Montana Press Release Number: 26-278

title: ILLINOIS MAN SENTENCED TO 76 MONTHS IN FEDERAL PRISON FOR ILLEGAL POSSESSION OF DEVICE MAKING EQUIPMENT
body: Press Release ILLINOIS MAN SENTENCED TO 76 MONTHS IN FEDERAL PRISON FOR ILLEGAL POSSESSION OF DEVICE MAKING EQUIPMENT Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Louisiana Jason Brown, age 40, of Chicago, Illinois, was sentenced to 76 months in federal prison following his conviction for illegally possessing device-making equipment. Judge John W. deGravelles further sentenced him to serve three years of supervised release following his term of imprisonment. According to admissions made as part of his guilty plea and evidence produced at his sentencing, Brown and his conspirators obtained materials necessary to produce counterfeit credit cards, including a credit card encoder and laptop computer. He and his conspirators used a counterfeit credit card to rent a vehicle, traveled to Baton Rouge, and used another counterfeit credit card to rent a room at a hotel on Bluebonnet Boulevard. The true owner of the card alerted the hotel, which alerted the authorities, and the East Baton Rouge Sheriff’s Office and the U.S. Secret Service responded to the scene. There, law enforcement located a fraudulent driver’s license and multiple counterfeit credit cards on Brown’s person. A search of Brown’s vehicle led to the recovery of more counterfeit credit cards, blank credit cards, a credit card encoder, and a laptop computer that contained 4,176 credit card numbers and associated track information used to encode the credit cards. “Clearly this was a professional fraudster,” stated U.S. Attorney Kurt Wall. “Anyone who has had their credit cards compromised will appreciate that this defendant will spend the next six years in prison for his actions.” Wall praised the work of the U.S. Secret Service and the East Baton Rouge Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Elizabeth E. White led the prosecution. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Fraud Component USAO - Louisiana, Middle

title: Derby man asks undercover agent to create fake child pornography
body: Press Release Derby man asks undercover agent to create fake child pornography Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Kansas WICHITA, KAN. – A Kansas man was sentenced to 121 months in prison for distributing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). According to court documents, Cody S. Bingham, 25, of Derby pleaded guilty to one count of distribution of child pornography. In 2025, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) infiltrated an online chatroom named "Filthy Pedo No Limits." Agents observed users exchanging CSAM. One of the users, who the FBI subsequently identified as Cody Bingham, distributed multiple CSAM posts to the group chat and asked users to create fake CSAM pictures of a minor victim. The undercover FBI agent then engaged in private conversations with Bingham, who sent photographs of this minor to the agent. Agents executed a search warrant at Bingham’s home and seized his electronic devices which contained CSAM images of sexual acts with minors as young as infants. “The conduct in this case is revolting,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “One does not stumble into a chatroom called ‘Filthy Pedo No Limits’ by accident. Those that deal in this disgusting material can expect to serve long sentences when they are brought to justice.” The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) investigated the case. Project Safe Childhood This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . ### Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Kansas
