title: Belarusian Woman Sentenced in D.C. for Illegally Exporting U.S.-Sourced Aviation Components to Russia
body: Press Release Belarusian Woman Sentenced in D.C. for Illegally Exporting U.S.-Sourced Aviation Components to Russia Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON — Yana Leonova, 34, a Belarusian citizen most recently residing in Russia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 12 months and one day in federal prison in connection with unlawfully exporting numerous avionics and other aircraft equipment from the United States to Russia, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “While Russia was waging war against Ukraine, Yana Leonova was smuggling U.S.-origin aircraft components to a company ultimately blacklisted by the U.S. government. She used shell companies, false documentation, foreign intermediaries, and overseas bank accounts to conceal the unlawful exports and evade U.S. sanctions,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “But no matter how complex the scheme or how many jurisdictions it crossed, investigators followed the evidence and brought her to justice. Anyone who seeks to exploit U.S. supply chains to support hostile regimes and undermine our national security should take note: we will find you, pursue you across borders, and hold you accountable.” “Those who attempt to hide behind shell companies, falsified documents, or any other form of evasion to move restricted U.S. goods and technology to our adversaries should understand that their actions will be uncovered,” said Special Agent in Charge Chris Ormerod of the FBI Kansas City Field Office. “This case reflects the diligent work of our agents and partners to identify, disrupt, and hold accountable anyone who seeks to undermine our nation’s security.” Leonova, aka “Yana Liavonava,” pleaded guilty on May 20 before the Honorable Loren L. AliKhan to violating the Export Control Reform Act. In addition to the 12-month prison term, Judge AliKhan ordered Leonova to be deported to Belarus following completion of her prison sentence. According to court documents and admissions during the plea hearing, following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Leonova and her U.S. and Armenian co-conspirators procured aircraft components from U.S.-based distributors and unlawfully exported them from the United States to Russia via Armenia, which resulted in dozens of aircraft components being shipped to Russia and millions of dollars being paid in return. Leonova and her co-conspirators devised the transshipment route to conceal that U.S.-origin components were bound for Russia and to evade U.S. export controls. Using companies located in Armenia, Leonova and her co-conspirators re-exported the components to Russia without the required licenses from the U.S. Department of Commerce, in violation of federal law. The exported items were for use on private jets and other aircraft operated or maintained by Leonova’s former employer, a company identified on the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Entity List for engaging in or enabling activities contrary to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. In November 2025, Leonova was extradited to the United States from France in connection with this case. This case was investigated by FBI Kansas City and Commerce Department, Bureau of Industry and Security, Office of Export Enforcement Atlanta and New York. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Emma Dinan Ellenrieder and John W. Borchert of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia and Acting Deputy Chief Sean R. Heiden of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section. Significant assistance was provided by Assistant U.S. Attorney Stuart D. Allen of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia. Further significant assistance on the extradition was provided by French authorities and the Department of Justice Office of International Affairs. The Department expresses deep appreciation for the support of our French allies. 24cr421 Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Export Control Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Federal jury convicts Alexandria man on drug trafficking and firearms charges in Homeland Security Task Force case
body: Press Release Federal jury convicts Alexandria man on drug trafficking and firearms charges in Homeland Security Task Force case Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Virginia ALEXANDRIA, Va. – A federal jury convicted an Alexandria man today on charges of possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine, possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine on a premises where a child is present, possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, two counts of possession of a firearm by a convicted felon, and possession with intent to distribute 1,4-Butanediol (a chemical analogue of gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB)). According to court records and evidence presented at trial, On March 10, Fairfax County Police observed Jeffrey Charles Williams, 42, who was wanted on an outstanding warrant, at a store. Officers detained Williams and saw firearms and ammunition in plain view inside his vehicle. Officers subsequently searched the vehicle and recovered methamphetamine, packaging material, scales, $1,300, a rifle, three shotguns, knives, ammunition and magazines, body armor, and police badges. As a previously convicted felon, Williams cannot legally possess firearms or ammunition. USAO EDVA Drugs and firearms seized from Williams’ vehicle On April 2, investigators searched Williams’ residence that he shares with his child and the mother of his child and recovered from his bedroom 26.8 pounds of methamphetamine, scales, packaging material, a handgun, rifle, ammunition, and $2,271. USAO EDVA USAO EDVA Drugs and firearms seized from Williams’ residence Williams faces a mandatory minimum of 15 years and up to life in prison when sentenced on Jan. 27, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia; Jeffrey L. Tyler, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Washington Field Office’s Criminal Division; and Kevin Davis, Fairfax County Chief of Police, made the announcement after U.S. District Judge Rossie D. Alston Jr. accepted the verdict. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Marc J. Birnbaum and Christopher M. Carter are prosecuting the case. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Washington, D.C., comprises agents and officers from the FBI; Homeland Security Investigations; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; Drug Enforcement Administration; Diplomatic Security Service; U.S. Marshals Service; U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service; Naval Criminal Investigative Service; Transportation Security Administration Federal Air Marshals Service; U.S. Customs and Border Protection; Enforcement and Removal Operations; and Washington Baltimore HIDTA, with the prosecution being led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia. Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 1:26-cr-114. Contact USAVAE.Press@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Virginia, Eastern

title: Former Army Official Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy, Bribery, and Major Fraud Related to Hawaii Defense Contracts
body: Press Release Former Army Official Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy, Bribery, and Major Fraud Related to Hawaii Defense Contracts Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A former civilian U.S. Army official pleaded guilty today to participating in a bribery and major fraud scheme that corrupted the competitive process for a U.S. Army technology innovation lab in the Pacific. According to a plea agreement and information filed in the U.S. District Court in Honolulu, Hawaii, from January 2021 to October 2022, Carlos Duque conspired with two defense contractors — Brian Kent and Leonard Pick — to accept a bribe of approximately $1.25 million over five years. In return, Duque told prime contractors to award subcontracts to Kent and Pick’s company and facilitated their fraudulent inflation of government contracting costs to include Duque’s bribe payments. Duque ultimately received approximately $55,000 in bribes from his coconspirators and the United States Army paid over $3 million to Kent and Pick’s company. “Fraud that deprives the U.S. military of free and fair competition for government contracts harms us all,” said Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward, Jr. “Because of prosecutions like this, Americans can trust that the Department of War and its warfighters maintain the highest standards of integrity.  We expect their contractors to do the same.” “Those who commit fraud on defense contracts don’t just steal from the military or taxpayers; they threaten the public’s confidence in government institutions and hurt our military readiness,” said Acting Deputy Assistant Attorney General Daniel W. Glad of the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division. “The Justice Department’s Procurement Collusion Strike Force will detect and prosecute those who, like the defendant, attempt to illegally take advantage of government programs.” “Americans work hard for their money and have every right to expect that their tax dollars will not be diverted through fraudulent schemes,” said U.S. Attorney Ken Sorenson for the District of Hawaii. “Those who obtain military contracts through fraud undermine both the public trust and the mission of our armed forces, and they will be held accountable.” “Public corruption — especially when it compromises our nation’s military readiness — undermines trust in the institutions built to protect our country,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Ryan C. Noonan of the FBI Honolulu Field Office. “This guilty plea reflects the strength of our partnerships in safeguarding government resources and ensuring integrity in the procurement process. Together with our federal law enforcement and military investigative partners, the FBI remains committed to identifying and stopping schemes that undermine fair competition and betray the public’s trust.” “Public officials are entrusted with a duty to the American people and government service is not an opportunity for personal enrichment at taxpayer expense,” said Director James R. Ives of the Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS), the criminal investigative arm of the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General. “DCIS and our partners remain steadfast in aggressively investigating those who undermine fair and open competition in government contracting.” “Bribery corrupts the federal contracting process that supports the critical missions of our military and civilian agencies,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Ryan Gregg of U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Inspector General (OIG) Western Investigations Division. “GSA OIG special agents will continue to aggressively pursue fraud alongside our law enforcement partners and the Department of Justice.” Duque pleaded guilty to conspiracy, bribery, and major fraud. Under the conspiracy charge, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000. Under the bribery charge, Duque faces a maximum penalty of 15 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000 or not more than three times the monetary equivalent of the bribe, whichever is greater, and disqualification from holding any office of honor, trust, or profit under the United States. Under the major fraud charge, Duque faces a maximum penalty of 10 years’ imprisonment and a fine of up to $5,000,000. In addition, Duque agreed to forfeit $55,166.70 as part of the plea agreement. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors, as well as any restitution to be paid to the Department of War. A federal grand jury returned an indictment against Kent and Pick in May 2026. The case, United States v. Brian Kent, et al. , No. 26-CR-00047-DKW (D. Haw.), is scheduled for trial before the Honorable Derrick K. Watson, Chief United States District Judge of the District of Hawaii, on May 17, 2027. Indictments are only allegations, and all persons charged are presumed to be innocent unless and until found guilty in court. The Antitrust Division’s San Francisco Office and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Hawaii are prosecuting the case, which was investigated with the assistance of the Department of War Office of Inspector General’s Defense Criminal Investigative Service, Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division, and General Services Administration Office of Inspector General. The Justice Department’s Procurement Collusion Strike Force (PCSF) is a joint law enforcement effort to combat antitrust crimes and related fraudulent schemes that impact government procurement, grant and program funding at all levels of government — federal, state and local. To learn more about the PCSF, or to report information on bid rigging, price fixing, market allocation and other anticompetitive conduct related to government spending, go to www.justice.gov/procurement-collusion-strike-force . Anyone with information in connection with this investigation can contact the PCSF at the link listed above. Whistleblowers who voluntarily report original information about antitrust and related offenses that result in criminal fines or other recoveries of at least $1 million may be eligible to receive a whistleblower reward. Whistleblower awards can range from 15 to 30 percent of the money collected. For more information on the Antitrust Whistleblower Rewards Program, including a link to submit reports, visit www.justice.gov/atr/whistleblower-rewards Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Antitrust Components Antitrust Division Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Office of the Associate Attorney General USAO - Hawaii Press Release Number: 26-1274

title: Illegal Alien Associated with Mexican Cartel Pleads Guilty to Drug Trafficking Conspiracy
body: Press Release Illegal Alien Associated with Mexican Cartel Pleads Guilty to Drug Trafficking Conspiracy Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey A Total of Three Defendants Have Pleaded Guilty NEWARK, N.J. – A Mexican national admitted to a cocaine trafficking conspiracy, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced today. Oscar Salvador Pelayo-Guzman, 55, a Mexican national and most recently of Kansas, pleaded guilty today before U.S. District Judge Jamel K. Semper in Newark federal court to a one-count Indictment charging him with conspiracy to distribute controlled substances. Two other defendants charged in the drug distribution conspiracy, Jose Manuel Amaya Villarreal and Reymond Alex Avina Samaniego, both of California, previously entered guilty pleas before Judge Semper to separate Informations charging them with conspiracy to distribute controlled substances. Villarreal was sentenced to 57 months’ imprisonment on August 7, 2026; sentencing for Samaniego is scheduled for November 9, 2026. According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: Pelayo-Guzman is associated with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel operating in Mexico and a principal member of a Kansas City-based drug trafficking organization involved in the international and interstate transportation and distribution of narcotics. Beginning in January 2025, Pelayo-Guzman and his co-conspirators conspired to transport large quantities of cocaine to New Jersey. Specifically, Pelayo-Guzman traveled to New Jersey in April 2025 and arranged for a shipment of approximately 20 kilograms of cocaine to be delivered to Newark, New Jersey from California via a truck driven by Villarreal and Samaniego. After delivering the approximately 20 kilograms of cocaine in exchange for over $300,000 in cash, law enforcement officers arrested Villarreal and Samaniego. Pelayo-Guzman was arrested shortly afterwards. The cocaine conspiracy charge carries a mandatory minimum penalty of 10 years in prison, a maximum potential penalty of life in prison, and a fine of up to $10 million. Sentencing is scheduled for March 1, 2027. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents with the Drug Enforcement Administration, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Towanda R. Thorne-James, with the investigation leading to the guilty plea. He also thanked the Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy; IRS-Criminal Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Jenifer Piovesan in Newark; the Monmouth County Prosecutor’s Office, under the direction of Prosecutor Raymond S. Santiago; the Ocean County Prosecutor’s Office, under the direction of Bradley D. Billhimer; the Asbury Park Police Department, under the direction of Police Director John B. Hayes; the Newark Department of Public Safety, Newark Police Division, under the direction of Public Safety Director Emanuel Miranda; the Middletown Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police R. Craig Weber; the Lakewood Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police Gregory H. Meyer; the Neptune Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police Anthony Gualario; the Ocean Gate Police Department, under the direction of Chief Michael Kuchta; and the Spotswood Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police Philip Corbisiero, for their assistance in the investigation. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Jonathan S. Garelick of the U.S. Attorney’s Office Criminal Division in Trenton. ### Defense counsel: Oscar Salvador Pelayo-Guzman: Adalgiza A. Núñez, Esq., Office of the Federal Public Defender Jose Manuel Amaya Villarreal: Perry Primavera, Esq. Reymond Alex Avina Samaniego: Joseph D. Rotella, Esq. pelayoguzman.indictment.pdf Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-236

title: Illegal Alien Sentenced to Three Years in Federal Prison for Illegally Re-Entering United States After Multiple Deportations
body: Press Release Illegal Alien Sentenced to Three Years in Federal Prison for Illegally Re-Entering United States After Multiple Deportations Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Illinois An illegal alien who was previously convicted of sexually assaulting a minor and attempting to possess child pornography has been sentenced to three years in federal prison for unlawfully re-entering the United States after multiple deportations. FRANCISCO HERNANDEZ-RAMOS, a native of Mexico, was unlawfully present in the United States on Aug. 7, 2021, when he was found in Harvard, Ill., by the Harvard Police Department.  Hernandez-Ramos had been deported from the United States five times and was previously convicted of criminal sexual assault of a minor, attempted possession of child pornography, illegal entry, and illegal re-entry of a removed alien. Hernandez-Ramos, 51, pleaded guilty in June 2026 in federal court in Rockford to one count of unlawful re-entry after removal.  On Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Iain D. Johnston sentenced Hernandez-Ramos to three years in federal prison.  As an alien in the United States illegally, Hernandez-Ramos is expected to face removal proceedings following imprisonment. The sentence was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Frank Padula, Chicago Field Office Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The government was represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys David M. Smith and Vincenza Tomlinson. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Immigration Component USAO - Illinois, Northern

title: Lame Deer man sentenced to 3 years in prison for beating teen with baseball bat
body: Press Release Lame Deer man sentenced to 3 years in prison for beating teen with baseball bat Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana BILLINGS – A Lame Deer man who repeatedly struck a teenage boy with a baseball bat was sentenced today to three years in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, U.S. Attorney Scott Twito said. Cameron Charles Backer, 38, pleaded guilty in June 2026 to assault with a deadly weapon and assault resulting in serious bodily injury. U.S. District Judge Kathleen S. Lane presided. The government alleged in court documents that Backer beat a teenage boy over the head with a baseball bat on Aug. 8, 2025, as the teen was fighting with another person. The assault left the teen with head lacerations that required 20 stitches and an ankle fracture. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jacob Yerger prosecuted the case. The FBI and BIA conducted the investigation. title: 17 Members of a Drug Trafficking Organization Charged with Drug Trafficking and Firearms Violations in Aguadilla, PR, as part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Initiative
body: Press Release 17 Members of a Drug Trafficking Organization Charged with Drug Trafficking and Firearms Violations in Aguadilla, PR, as part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Initiative Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – On October 21, 2026, a federal grand jury in the District of Puerto Rico returned an indictment charging 17 gang members from Aguadilla with conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute, possession and distribution of controlled substances, and firearms violations, announced Héctor Ramírez Carbó, Acting United States Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico. This investigation was led by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Puerto Rico Police Bureau (PRPB) Aguadilla Strike Force, with the collaboration of the Puerto Rico Department of Correction and Rehabilitation, the Puerto Rico & Virgin Islands High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) and The White House Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP). “Drug trafficking organizations like the one alleged in today’s indictment inflict profound harm on our communities—fueling addiction, poisoning our youth, sowing fear, and endangering innocent lives,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Ramírez‑Carbó. “Today’s arrests send a clear message to those who endanger our neighborhoods through drug trafficking and firearms offenses: You will be identified, your organization dismantled and will pay the price.  We will continue working alongside the DEA and our HSTF law enforcement partners to ensure the safety and security of every community in Puerto Rico. Today’s operation just happens to complement DEA’s Red Ribbon Campaign for safer communities and a drug-free life.” “Operation Los Tíos sends a clear message: the DEA’s mission extends throughout Puerto Rico. No community in Puerto Rico is beyond our reach, and no drug trafficking organization is beyond the reach of justice,” said Michael Mayer, Special Agent in Charge, DEA Caribbean Division. “Through the Homeland Security Task Force, the DEA, and our federal, state, and local partners are combining our intelligence, resources, and operational capabilities to dismantle violent criminal organizations. Our commitment to public safety extends across all of Puerto Rico; throughout every municipality, we will continue working together to protect our communities and bring those who threaten them to justice.” The indictment alleges that from 2022, the drug trafficking organization distributed heroin, cocaine base (crack), and fentanyl, within 1,000 feet of the Las Muñecas Public Housing Project (PHP) in Aguadilla, and areas nearby, all for significant financial gain and profit. The object of the conspiracy was to distribute wholesale quantities and street amount quantities of controlled substances and to traffic illegal firearms in Aguadilla and areas nearby. They operated drug points out of different housing projects and wards in or around Aguadilla. The defendants communicated with each other using two-way radios and cell phones, via instant messaging and social media platforms. Leaders conducted meetings to resolve issues, give instructions, and discuss items of interest to the drug trafficking organization. It is alleged that members of the drug trafficking organization participated in acts of violence, including shootings and murders, to further their drug trafficking operations. The defendants acted in different roles to further the goals of the drug trafficking conspiracy, including as leaders, drug point owners, enforcers, runners, sellers, lookouts, and facilitators. Six (6) defendants are facing one charge of possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and one (1) of those defendants is facing one count of possession of a machine gun in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. The defendants charged in the indictment are: [1] Alexander Torres Cintrón, a.k.a. “Guesito/Huesito” [2] Jonathan Pérez Cintrón, a.k.a. “Jona,” [3] Fernando M. Pagán Flores, a.k.a. “Pri/P” [4] Wesley Ortiz-Soto, a.k.a. “Wes/Negro” [5] Jesús Román Marrero, a.k.a. “Chucky” [6] Jeremy D. Medina Acevedo, a.k.a. “Oscuridad” [7] Edwin Y. Santiago Marín, a.k.a. “Yadi/Yadiel/Pacho” [8] Christian Rivera Cardona, a.k.a. “Romántico” [9] José Rosario Bermúdez, a.k.a. “Joker” [10] Yan P. Serrano Vizcarrondo, a.k.a. “Domi/Pipi” [11] Efraín Colón Morales, a.k.a. “Cholón” [12] Lizbeth Dávila Pedrasa, a.k.a. “Lizbeth/Chispa” [13] Bryan Tosado Pedraza, a.k.a. “Chancla/Pichi” [14] Kelvin Torres De Lancer, a.k.a. “Troko” [15] Jorge Christian Acevedo Pérez [16] Ángel L. Román García, a.k.a. “Iche” [17] Raynell Caravallo Vázquez, a.k.a. “Raynell” Assistant U.S. Attorney (AUSA) and Chief of the Asset Recovery and Money Laundering Division Myriam Y. Fernández, and AUSA Andrés Orr are in charge of the prosecution of the case. If convicted on the drug charges, the defendants face a minimum sentence of 10 years, and up to life in prison. If convicted of both the drug and firearms charges in Count Five, the defendants face a minimum sentence of 15 years, and up to life in prison. The defendant charged with possession of machine guns in furtherance of drug trafficking in Count Six faces a mandatory minimum sentence of thirty years in prison to be served consecutive to any sentence imposed on the drug trafficking charges. All defendants are facing a narcotics forfeiture allegation of $4,334,375. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Juan comprises agents and officers from the following federal partners: FBI, ICE-HSI, CBP (OFO, AMO and Border Patrol), the U.S. Marshals Service for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, DEA, ATF, IRS, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the Department of State, and the U.S. Secret Service, the Puerto Rico/U.S. Virgin Islands HIDTA, TSA, FAA, and the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The HSTF also has the following state and local law enforcement partners as participating agencies: the Puerto Rico Police Department; the San Juan, Carolina, Guaynabo, Barceloneta, and Ponce Municipal Police Departments, the Puerto Rico National Guard – Counter Drug Program; the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation; the Puerto Rico Internal Revenue Service (Hacienda); the Puerto Rico Port Authority; and the Virgin Islands Police Department. title: Virginia Mental Health Professional Charged in $49M Medicaid Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Virginia Mental Health Professional Charged in $49M Medicaid Fraud Scheme Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A federal grand jury in the Eastern District of Virginia returned an indictment on Oct. 20 against Mikia Antoneice Noble, 37, of North Chesterfield, Virginia, for a $49 million mental health crisis services fraud scheme targeting Virginia Medicaid. Noble was arrested today. According to court documents, Noble was the co-owner and Chief Operating Officer of Advancing Communities Everywhere LLC (ACE), a mental health provider in the Richmond, Virginia area. In addition to her ownership role, Noble claimed to also work as a mental health professional for ACE. ACE purported to provide mental health services to individuals experiencing acute or significant behavioral health crises but did not provide those services as billed. As alleged in the indictment, Noble conspired with her co-owner to: Bill Virginia Medicaid for crisis services purportedly provided by teams of mental health professionals including a trained and licensed professional, which were instead provided only by a single low-level, less qualified mental health professional; Pay over $2 million for hotel room rentals that were offered to Medicaid beneficiaries to illegally induce that to allow ACE to bill for services purportedly provided to them that they did not actually need; Falsify medical records by adding signatures of licensed professionals who had not actually participated in providing crisis services; Falsify medical records by adding Noble’s own signature falsely representing that she had participated in providing crisis services, when in fact Noble was out of the country; and Lie to Medicaid Managed Care Organizations conducting audits of ACE’s crisis services. From January 2022 through April 2026, Noble allegedly participated in submitting over $49 million in false and fraudulent claims to Virginia Medicaid. Noble is charged with conspiracy to commit health care fraud and three counts of health care fraud. If convicted, she faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison on each count. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos for the Eastern District of Virginia; and Special Agent in Charge Ian Kaufmann of the FBI Richmond Field Office made the announcement. The FBI Richmond Field Office and the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit of the Virginia Office of the Attorney General are investigating the case. Trial Attorneys Lauren Randell and Zachary H. Ray of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert S. Day for the Eastern District of Virginia are prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1275

title: Eastern Shore Felon Indicted on Firearm Charges
body: Press Release Eastern Shore Felon Indicted on Firearm Charges Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Baltimore, Maryland – A Maryland felon faces indictment after making his initial appearance in federal court, today, for firearm possession crimes. Theodore Harcum, 50, of Denton, is charged with possession of a firearm and ammunition by a prohibited person. Harcum is prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition due to a prior felony conviction. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Acting Chief Jamie L. Secrist, Denton Police Department. According to the indictment, on April 13, 2026, Harcum possessed a handgun and nine rounds of ammunition. An indictment is not a finding of guilt.  Individuals charged by indictment are presumed innocent until proven guilty at a later criminal proceeding. Harcum faces a maximum sentence of 15 years in federal prison for possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. U.S. Attorney Kelly O. Hayes commended the ATF and Denton Police Department for their work in the investigation. U.S. Attorney Hayes also thanked Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Arqum Rashid who is prosecuting the federal case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Maryland

title: Two Aliens From Sudan and Afghanistan Charged for Illegal Voting
body: Press Release Two Aliens From Sudan and Afghanistan Charged for Illegal Voting Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – Today, two aliens, one from Sudan and one from Afghanistan, have been charged for illegally voting in a federal election in Nevada. “As these cases show, the public and political narrative that Nevada’s elections are not fraught with fraud is categorically false,” said Sigal Chattah, First Assistant United States Attorney for the District of Nevada. “Let these cases serve as a stark, unmistakable warning: if you deliberately try to subvert the democratic process, my office will hunt you down, expose your actions, and prosecute you to the absolute fullest extent of the law. My office will continue to investigate and charge any individuals who engage in election fraud. We are drawing a hard line in the sand to protect the legal votes of our citizens, and anyone who crosses it will face severe consequences.” “Safeguarding the integrity of federal elections requires a coordinated law enforcement response to alleged violations of election laws,” said Erin Burke, Special Agent in Charge for HSI Los Angeles. “HSI and our FBI partners remain committed to investigating these cases thoroughly and ensuring that those accused of violating federal law are held accountable through the judicial process.” “Protecting the integrity of the American electoral process is among our highest responsibility,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Office. “We will exhaustively pursue and hold accountable anyone who seeks to undermine our elections, ensuring that every citizen's right to a free and fair vote is protected. We will utilize all appropriate resources to investigate credible claims of voter fraud, steadfastly guided by our core values of Fidelity, Bravery, and Integrity. Always remember: Justice will find you.” According to the criminal information, on or about October 29, 2024, Moneir Elzobier Ali Yousif, from Sudan and a lawful permanent resident, voted in an election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of President, Vice President, Member of the Senate, and Member of the House of Representatives. In a separate criminal information, on or about November 5, 2024, Khalida Safi, from Afghanistan and a lawful permanent resident, voted in an election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of President, Vice President, Member of the Senate, and Member of the House of Representatives. Yousif and Safi are each charged with one count of voting by an alien. The maximum statutory penalty is one year of imprisonment, a fine of up to $100,000, or both. An initial appearance date has not yet been scheduled. The FBI and HSI investigated this case. An information is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. ### Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Nevada

title: Fraudulent Document Marketplace Operator Sentenced to Federal Prison
body: Press Release Fraudulent Document Marketplace Operator Sentenced to Federal Prison Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia ATLANTA - Kimani Bracey was sentenced to federal prison for operating a fraudulent document marketplace that provided fake documents used to steal pandemic relief funds and commit other fraud. “Bracey exploited the nation’s struggles during the COVID-19 pandemic by creating and disseminating fake documents that fueled extensive fraud against the government, banks, and other financial institutions,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “My office will continue to hold these criminals accountable for facilitating fraud.” “During a time of unprecedented national peril, Kimani Bracey took advantage of a pandemic and profited off helping others steal hundreds of thousands of dollars in federal funds,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “Years after the pandemic, the FBI and our law enforcement partners continue to hold individuals accountable for committing fraud on the government.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: Bracey operated two websites offering so-called “novelty” documents to the public, including fake tax returns, bank records, and employment verification documents. Bracey knew that customers were ordering and using the documents to commit fraud. The FBI traced multiple fake documents created by Bracey to Paycheck Protection Program loan applications submitted to banks, which resulted in over $380,000 in fraudulent loans. Bracey also created fake pay stubs and counterfeit employer verification documents to allow people to obtain loans through fraud, in addition to phony COVID-19 test results. Today, U.S. District Judge Thomas W. Thrash, Jr. sentenced Kimani Bracey, 49, of Simpsonville, S.C., to two years, three months in prison to be followed by three years of supervised release and ordered him to pay restitution in the amount of $386,960.50. Bracey pled guilty to wire fraud on June 26, 2026. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Assistant United States Attorneys Calvin A. Leipold, III and Angela Adams prosecuted the case. Anyone with information about allegations of attempted fraud involving COVID-19 can report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Complaint Form at: https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form . On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within federal benefit programs. For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Fraud COVID-Related Fraud Financial Fraud Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Georgia, Northern

Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that XIAOQIN YAN, 32, a citizen of China, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Kari A. Dooley in Bridgeport to 10 months of additional imprisonment for escaping from the Federal Correctional Institution in Danbury (FCI Danbury). title: Eagle Butte Man Sentenced to Over 2 Years in Federal Prison  for Assaulting a Federal Officer
body: Press Release Eagle Butte Man Sentenced to Over 2 Years in Federal Prison  for Assaulting a Federal Officer Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota PIERRE - United States Attorney Ron Parsons, announced today that U.S. District Judge Eric C. Schulte has sentenced an Eagle Butte, South Dakota, man convicted of Assaulting, Resisting, and Impeding a Federal Officer.  The sentencing took place on October 26, 2026. Philip Lamar Nordvold, a/k/a PJ Nordvold, age 48, was sentenced to two years and four months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Nordvold was indicted by a federal grand jury in January 2026.  He pleaded guilty on July 27, 2026. The conviction stems from an incident that occurred on May 15, 2025, in the Cheyenne River Sioux Indian Reservation. On that day, a Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe Law Enforcement Services Officer made contact with Nordvald to arrest him on an outstanding warrant.  Nordvold resisted by holding a knife above his head and yelling that he was not going back to jail.  Nordvold was arrested after dropping the knife. This case was investigated by the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe Law Enforcement Services and the FBI.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Wayne Venhuizen prosecuted the case. Nordvold was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Contact usasd.press@usdoj.gov Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Component USAO - South Dakota

title: Illegal Alien from Honduras Sentenced for Illegally Possessing a Firearm and Unlawfully Reentering the United States
body: Press Release Illegal Alien from Honduras Sentenced for Illegally Possessing a Firearm and Unlawfully Reentering the United States Wednesday, October 28, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Missouri KANSAS CITY, Mo. – A Honduran national, illegally living in the Kansas City, Mo. area was sentenced to one year and one day in federal prison for possessing a firearm and violating immigration laws. Kelvin Lopez-Leonardo, 32, pleaded guilty to being an alien in possession of a firearm and unlawfully reentering the United States. On April 13, 2025, officers with the Kansas City, Missouri Police Department arrested Lopez-Leonardo after he was found in a stolen vehicle with a firearm. After confirming Lopez-Leonardo’s identity, officers learned he had previously been removed from the United States. The Kansas City, Missouri Police Department contacted Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) - Enforcement and Removal Operations. In conjunction with ICE - Homeland Security Investigations, it was determined that Lopez-Leonardo had illegally entered the United States on three prior occasions before being removed from the United States each time, with the last removal occurring in October of 2023. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Kelly Collins. It was investigated by the Enforcement and Removal Operations and Homeland Security Investigations divisions of Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and the Kansas City, Missouri Police Department. Operation Take Back America This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN). Updated October 28, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Firearms Offenses Immigration Component USAO - Missouri, Western

title: The platform approach to becoming Frontier
body: The platform approach to becoming Frontier Oct 27, 2026 | Judson Althoff - CEO, Microsoft Commercial Business Last year at Ignite, we introduced the concept of Frontier Transformation and how it is different from any technology-led pursuit, because it requires us to focus on business outcomes first. It starts with a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. There is no path where this notion of infinite cognitive compute replaces human purpose. Frontier Transformation is an opportunity for a wholesale reinvention of how you think about your unique ideas coming to life and how your organization can thrive in your industry. Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. We are taking a platform approach toward enabling the same: Copilot as the place to call home for interacting with AI to empower human ambition; the Microsoft IQ platform to compound and amplify your intelligence from within while protecting your unique differentiation; and Agent 365 to enable Trust and Observability at every layer of the stack so that you can govern, manage, secure and get business value and return out of the capabilities you deliver. Our latest earnings are another important marker on that journey. Behind the numbers are thousands of customers, partners, developers and employees putting AI to work in meaningful ways. We have so many inspiring stories from our customers that highlight these outcomes, and below are some of our favorites. Empowering human ambition with Copilot Volkswagen has scaled Microsoft Copilot to more than 330,000 employees as it expands the role of AI in decision-making and knowledge-based processes across the enterprise. Building on Copilot Chat adoption that reached more than 300,000 monthly active users, employees are now using Copilot with Work IQ for more advanced scenarios, bringing greater organizational context to decision-making and knowledge-based work . Volkswagen is also working with Microsoft to further scale its Intelligent Data Foundation on Microsoft Fabric to make data easier to find, understand and use across the entire company. With this investment, Volkswagen is demonstrating how companies have evolved from using Copilot as a productivity tool to an operating system to empower human ambition. Following a successful pilot, Fujitsu is scaling Microsoft Copilot across its global workforce of approximately 100,000 . Copilot usage has surpassed 90%, and the company is using the tool to connect employees with specialized agents and business systems. AI agents are already automating roughly 75% of initial responses and triage for a service desk that receives nearly 300,000 inquiries annually , while new agents are supporting work across sales, systems engineering, procurement, finance and accounting. As customer zero, Fujitsu is using Copilot as the front door to a multi-agent work environment and using insights from its own AI adoption to better serve its customers. KOHLER is using GitHub Copilot to transform software development, with one organization improving code releases by 25% and reducing error defects by 75%. These engineering breakthroughs are part of a broader effort to embed AI processes across the company, spanning IT, finance, marketing, supply chain and operations. Microsoft Copilot has reached 98% adoption, saving an average of 2 to 5 hours per month as employees are making informed decisions and getting answers faster in the flow of their work . Employees across the company have also created more than 3,000 agents to date, with hundreds active daily . At Krafton , Microsoft Security Copilot and Microsoft Defender XDR are helping the security team respond to a growing volume and complexity of threats. The global gaming company automated key parts of security operations, from alerting and investigation to reporting, combining Microsoft Security solutions with its own systems and data to quickly gather context that helps distinguish real threats from false positives. This approach is having immediate results: security alert recognition time has fallen by approximately 95% to less than one minute, investigation work that previously took tens of minutes now takes about three minutes and roughly 95% of report creation has been automated . By taking on repetitive work, AI is giving Krafton’s security professionals more time to focus on responding to real threats and making critical security decisions. To accelerate discovery across decades of scientific data, NASA is making complex information easier to explore through Microsoft Copilot. NASA employees are using Copilot to sift through massive amounts of academic literature and streamline daily tasks, and specialized assistants are helping researchers navigate complex Earth science data through natural language, extending access to information that once required significant technical expertise. Hydrology Copilot, for example, can analyze variables like precipitation and soil moisture to help communities better understand water conditions, prepare for droughts and anticipate flood risks, while automatically performing calculations and analyses. To transform frontline work, Williams , a US natural gas company, is using Microsoft Copilot to help employees spend less time searching documents and completing manual processes, and more time on critical field operations. Copilot helps teams generate plans, interpret procedures, assess regulatory requirements, troubleshoot issues and complete safety reporting , while employees can create agents tailored to their own workflows. Demonstrating that the person closest to a problem is often the best one to solve it, one operations technician built an anomaly detector using Copilot that compares equipment data against baseline statistics and alerts teams to potential issues before they become costly or dangerous . Since deploying Copilot, AI adoption at Williams has grown from single digits to more than 90%, helping employees accelerate operations, improve reporting and compliance and identify equipment issues earlier. Bristol Myers Squibb has rolled out Microsoft Copilot to 25,000 employees, reaching 96% adoption , and is now putting AI agents to work across everyday use cases such as document review and project management in support of the company’s mission to bring more medicines to more patients faster. One agent, called RABIT, analyzes meeting transcripts, surfaces action items and delivers insights directly within employees’ workflows. Facing rising patient demand and financial pressures, Brown University Health is using Dragon Copilot to give clinicians more time to focus on patients. The health system adopted Dragon Copilot, and an early pilot across 420 clinicians found users spent less time on after-hours documentation and reported lower cognitive burden . Building on that experience, Brown University Health deployed Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio across departments, which led to the creation of more than 24 AI agents to support clinical workflows, hospital policies, patient access and operations . These AI solutions are not only supporting clinicians in the flow of their work but also helping to improve the patient experience and access to care. Microsoft IQ compounds and protects your intelligence BNY has made AI part of how its employees work through Eliza, its in-house AI platform built with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot and GitHub Copilot – with plans to add Work IQ. More than 300 solutions now run on Eliza, ranging from inquiry management to client onboarding, and 100% of employees have been trained on the platform. Across the bank, that scale is translating into meaningful results: client transaction inquiries are being resolved 80% faster and AI-assisted client onboarding is 20% faster on average . Through the Microsoft CEO Co-Innovation program, BNY also worked with Microsoft to develop an AI research capability with Foundry that investigates complex data issues, analyzes context across multiple sources, identifies likely root causes and recommends next steps, bringing AI-assisted reasoning into processes that have traditionally relied on human investigation alone. Docusign is helping 1.9 million customers across 180 countries turn agreement data into actionable business insights. The company built an Intelligent Agreement Management platform on Microsoft Azure and used Microsoft Foundry to shift from general-purpose models to a system of task-specific models that better understand context . This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents in a single day, with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production , while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected. To help marketers create more effective content, Kantar turned decades of proprietary advertising intelligence into action with Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry. Working with Microsoft Frontier Company , Kantar connected its LINK AI platform to its proprietary intelligence, AI models and creative workflows, enabling marketers to evaluate, optimize and generate content before it goes to market. The new approach can process and score large volumes of videos 20x faster while reducing platform operating costs by 4x , helping customers move from insight to action in minutes rather than hours . By bringing its unique intelligence into a continuous loop of observation and improvement, Kantar is creating new ways to help marketers turn insight into better creative and business outcomes. Kinaxis , a Canadian supply chain software company, runs Maestro, its AI-driven supply chain orchestration platform, on Microsoft Azure. Maestro helps businesses make better decisions faster amid constant disruption. It brings together traditionally disparate business data like sales orders, inventory and production capacity with external signals like weather, market shifts and breaking news to give planners a near real-time view of their supply chains . With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change. Moody’s is making more than a century of credit and risk intelligence directly accessible through Microsoft Copilot, giving customers trusted, protected context for complex decisions. Through a federated connector built using Model Context Protocol, customers can access live, decision-grade Moody’s intelligence through Researcher in Copilot and within Word, Excel and Teams, without copying or exporting the underlying data. A single question can synthesize information across credit ratings, company financials, ownership information and physical risk models, helping customers reach insights in minutes instead of spending hours or days on research and analysis . This brings trusted, connected intelligence directly into workflows where customers make complex decisions. To turn conversations into actionable intelligence at global scale, Plaud , an AI hardware and software company, is using Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to power transcription, summarization and AI inference across long-form audio and multilingual scenarios. Serving more than 2 million users worldwide, Plaud increased transcription accuracy and processing speed by 35% and improved inference performance by 30%, helping professionals turn spoken content into structured outputs and insights . Even as its user base doubled, the company used Foundry’s elastic scaling and flexible deployment models to reduce overall compute costs by 35%, while strengthening its ability to meet security, privacy and compliance requirements across global markets . Rockwell Automation built a Maintenance Copilot using Microsoft Foundry to put decades of manufacturing expertise in the hands of employees . The AI assistant brings together expert knowledge from veteran engineers, manufacturing data and machine manuals, allowing technicians to quickly identify likely causes of equipment issues, see how colleagues have solved similar problems and access step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. At its Singapore factory, the approach has helped reduce machine downtime by 33% and cut servicing and spare-part costs by about 25%. Rockwell estimates it has also reduced the time it takes new workers to learn to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three months . With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring . After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide , TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on. Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production , the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence. Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale . With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities . With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation. Insight Enterprises , a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale . As a Microsoft customer zero organization for Agent 365, Insight Enterprises is quick to adopt new capabilities internally and pass those learnings on to clients. With Microsoft engineering, it tested how Microsoft and third-party agents could be observed, managed, governed and secured through a unified control plane. To date, Insight Enterprises has discovered 9,734 agents with visibility into which are active, what data they can access and how to monitor their activity over time. The experience has helped Insight Enterprises build practical AI governance expertise it can bring to customers, including organizations in highly regulated industries. KPMG is adopting Microsoft Agent 365 to manage and secure AI agents across its global organization, providing centralized observability and control as it scales agentic AI . Agent 365 will also strengthen KPMG Workbench, its multi-agent platform built on Microsoft Foundry that coordinates agents across client service delivery platforms. At the same time, KPMG is expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 276,000 professionals worldwide, helping embed AI more deeply across audit, tax and advisory services. Together, these capabilities are giving KPMG the confidence and security to move agents from experimentation into enterprise-wide deployment, while helping clients do the same. Operating in one of the most highly regulated industries, where protecting sensitive customer information is essential, Truist Financial Corporation is using Agent 365 to manage, govern and observe more than 13,000 AI declarative agents across its organization . Truist manages its agent ecosystem with discipline: every agent has an accountable owner and agents are automatically disabled after 45 days of inactivity . That rigor is driving strong retention and adoption, with more than 8,000 agents active each month. Building on this trusted foundation, Truist has advanced its broader AI strategy through their investment of more than 50,000 Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite seats. — Every quarter gives us an opportunity to step back and look at the progress we are making with our customers and partners around the world. What continues to strike me is not simply the pace of change, but the ambition we see from organizations using technology to achieve aspirations that simply weren’t possible before. We look forward to working alongside you on the path to becoming Frontier, and we hope to see many of you at Microsoft Ignite this year in November to share the latest innovations that will enable you to reach that destination. Judson Althoff is the chief executive officer of the commercial business at Microsoft. He is responsible for the product strategy, sales, services, support, marketing, operations and revenue growth of the company’s commercial business, which operates in more than 120 regional and national subsidiaries globally. The health system adopted Dragon Copilot, and an early pilot across 420 clinicians found users spent less time on after-hours documentation and reported lower cognitive burden . Building on that experience, Brown University Health deployed Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio across departments, which led to the creation of more than 24 AI agents to support clinical workflows, hospital policies, patient access and operations . These AI solutions are not only supporting clinicians in the flow of their work but also helping to improve the patient experience and access to care. Microsoft IQ compounds and protects your intelligence BNY has made AI part of how its employees work through Eliza, its in-house AI platform built with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot and GitHub Copilot – with plans to add Work IQ. More than 300 solutions now run on Eliza, ranging from inquiry management to client onboarding, and 100% of employees have been trained on the platform. Across the bank, that scale is translating into meaningful results: client transaction inquiries are being resolved 80% faster and AI-assisted client onboarding is 20% faster on average . Through the Microsoft CEO Co-Innovation program, BNY also worked with Microsoft to develop an AI research capability with Foundry that investigates complex data issues, analyzes context across multiple sources, identifies likely root causes and recommends next steps, bringing AI-assisted reasoning into processes that have traditionally relied on human investigation alone. Docusign is helping 1.9 million customers across 180 countries turn agreement data into actionable business insights. The company built an Intelligent Agreement Management platform on Microsoft Azure and used Microsoft Foundry to shift from general-purpose models to a system of task-specific models that better understand context . This change allows Docusign to process more than a million agreement documents in a single day, with up to eightfold greater throughput and 90% lower AI processing costs. Foundry also supports a model lifecycle designed for continuous improvement, where processes are fine-tuned before deployment and monitored in production , while also providing the governance and traceability needed to meet enterprise requirements for compliance, visibility and control. Now agreement content is structured data that compounds from within, so organizations can use it to make decisions and automate workflows, knowing their IP is protected. To help marketers create more effective content, Kantar turned decades of proprietary advertising intelligence into action with Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry. Working with Microsoft Frontier Company , Kantar connected its LINK AI platform to its proprietary intelligence, AI models and creative workflows, enabling marketers to evaluate, optimize and generate content before it goes to market. The new approach can process and score large volumes of videos 20x faster while reducing platform operating costs by 4x , helping customers move from insight to action in minutes rather than hours . By bringing its unique intelligence into a continuous loop of observation and improvement, Kantar is creating new ways to help marketers turn insight into better creative and business outcomes. Kinaxis , a Canadian supply chain software company, runs Maestro, its AI-driven supply chain orchestration platform, on Microsoft Azure. Maestro helps businesses make better decisions faster amid constant disruption. It brings together traditionally disparate business data like sales orders, inventory and production capacity with external signals like weather, market shifts and breaking news to give planners a near real-time view of their supply chains . With this unified data foundation, planners and analysts can use predictive AI and optimization models to anticipate demand shifts, evaluate constraints and recommend action, while generative AI agents act as assistants to ask questions, explore scenarios and automate parts of the planning process. With this intelligence in one platform, businesses can understand how disruptions ripple across their interconnected operations, weigh trade-offs and adjust plans as conditions change. Moody’s is making more than a century of credit and risk intelligence directly accessible through Microsoft Copilot, giving customers trusted, protected context for complex decisions. Through a federated connector built using Model Context Protocol, customers can access live, decision-grade Moody’s intelligence through Researcher in Copilot and within Word, Excel and Teams, without copying or exporting the underlying data. A single question can synthesize information across credit ratings, company financials, ownership information and physical risk models, helping customers reach insights in minutes instead of spending hours or days on research and analysis . This brings trusted, connected intelligence directly into workflows where customers make complex decisions. To turn conversations into actionable intelligence at global scale, Plaud , an AI hardware and software company, is using Microsoft Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models and Azure Speech in Foundry Tools to power transcription, summarization and AI inference across long-form audio and multilingual scenarios. Serving more than 2 million users worldwide, Plaud increased transcription accuracy and processing speed by 35% and improved inference performance by 30%, helping professionals turn spoken content into structured outputs and insights . Even as its user base doubled, the company used Foundry’s elastic scaling and flexible deployment models to reduce overall compute costs by 35%, while strengthening its ability to meet security, privacy and compliance requirements across global markets . Rockwell Automation built a Maintenance Copilot using Microsoft Foundry to put decades of manufacturing expertise in the hands of employees . The AI assistant brings together expert knowledge from veteran engineers, manufacturing data and machine manuals, allowing technicians to quickly identify likely causes of equipment issues, see how colleagues have solved similar problems and access step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. At its Singapore factory, the approach has helped reduce machine downtime by 33% and cut servicing and spare-part costs by about 25%. Rockwell estimates it has also reduced the time it takes new workers to learn to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three months . With 1.5 billion passengers riding its elevators and escalators every day, TK Elevator knows that every minute of downtime affects how people move through airports, hospitals and offices. Building on a decade of connected-equipment data on Microsoft Azure, the company created AI agents with Microsoft Foundry that brief service technicians before they enter a building, telling them which elevator, which floor, what the issue is and which tools to bring . After each job, a voice agent records the technician’s account of the work in their own words, with no typing, and adds that expertise to a shared record. With 25,000 technicians caring for 1.4 million units worldwide , TK Elevator is turning each technician’s know-how into compounded intelligence every colleague can draw on. Telstra partnered with Microsoft Frontier Company to deploy an AI-powered Migration Payment Agent that helps simplify one of the most complex aspects of customer migration: reconciling billing and payments across legacy and new platforms. The agent uses intelligence across these systems to proactively identify inconsistencies, recommend corrective actions and create enriched cases for human review, combining AI-driven insights with human-in-the-loop validation to maintain operational trust and governance. Already supporting more than 272,000 service migrations and delivering recommendations at 95%+ accuracy in production , the solution demonstrates how Telstra is applying agentic AI at enterprise scale to transform complex operations, improve customer outcomes and build reusable AI capabilities while compounding and protecting Telstra’s operational intelligence. Agent 365 observes AI solutions across the stack To advance its transformation into an AI-powered organization, Manulife is adopting Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite, expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 30,000 employees and leveraging Microsoft Agent 365 to govern, manage and secure AI agents at enterprise scale . With Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry supporting its global enterprise AI platform, Manulife is building a foundation for teams to develop and deploy AI and agentic solutions while maintaining standards for quality, security and cost efficiency. AI is already delivering impact across the business, from generative AI solutions supporting more than 110 million customer calls annually to developers increasing productivity by 30% with assisted and autonomous AI capabilities . With agentic solutions and AI-powered workflows already in production, Manulife is creating the foundation to scale AI responsibly across its global operations and accelerate its next phase of enterprise transformation. Insight Enterprises , a leading solutions integrator and top Microsoft partner, is using Microsoft Agent 365 to govern AI agents at scale . As a Microsoft customer zero organization for Agent 365, Insight Enterprises is quick to adopt new capabilities internally and pass those learnings on to clients. With Microsoft engineering, it tested how Microsoft and third-party agents could be observed, managed, governed and secured through a unified control plane. To date, Insight Enterprises has discovered 9,734 agents with visibility into which are active, what data they can access and how to monitor their activity over time. The experience has helped Insight Enterprises build practical AI governance expertise it can bring to customers, including organizations in highly regulated industries. KPMG is adopting Microsoft Agent 365 to manage and secure AI agents across its global organization, providing centralized observability and control as it scales agentic AI . Agent 365 will also strengthen KPMG Workbench, its multi-agent platform built on Microsoft Foundry that coordinates agents across client service delivery platforms. At the same time, KPMG is expanding Microsoft Copilot to more than 276,000 professionals worldwide, helping embed AI more deeply across audit, tax and advisory services. Together, these capabilities are giving KPMG the confidence and security to move agents from experimentation into enterprise-wide deployment, while helping clients do the same. Operating in one of the most highly regulated industries, where protecting sensitive customer information is essential, Truist Financial Corporation is using Agent 365 to manage, govern and observe more than 13,000 AI declarative agents across its organization . Truist manages its agent ecosystem with discipline: every agent has an accountable owner and agents are automatically disabled after 45 days of inactivity . That rigor is driving strong retention and adoption, with more than 8,000 agents active each month. Building on this trusted foundation, Truist has advanced its broader AI strategy through their investment of more than 50,000 Microsoft 365 E7: The Frontier Suite seats. — Every quarter gives us an opportunity to step back and look at the progress we are making with our customers and partners around the world. What continues to strike me is not simply the pace of change, but the ambition we see from organizations using technology to achieve aspirations that simply weren’t possible before. We look forward to working alongside you on the path to becoming Frontier, and we hope to see many of you at Microsoft Ignite this year in November to share the latest innovations that will enable you to reach that destination. Judson Althoff is the chief executive officer of the commercial business at Microsoft. He is responsible for the product strategy, sales, services, support, marketing, operations and revenue growth of the company’s commercial business, which operates in more than 120 regional and national subsidiaries globally.
