title: We’re announcing Genie 4, our new world model for real-time interactive simulation.
body: We’re announcing Genie 4, our new world model for real-time interactive simulation. Oct 27, 2026 Today, we’re announcing our research on Genie 4, our new world model that brings unprecedented realism and native audio to real-time interactive simulation. The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity. With Genie 4, you can set an event in motion and steer scenes in real time using natural language, like moving the camera, changing the weather, or introducing new characters. Every world also generates native audio on the fly, including ambient sounds, music, and interactive dialogue. Simulating the world is a crucial step toward AGI, enabling safe training environments for robots and agents, and amplifying creative tools across industries like filmmaking, journalism, gaming, and manufacturing. We have started rolling out Genie 4 to a limited group of trusted testers. It’s coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and AI Studio. Explore the demos on the Google DeepMind blog .

title: How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia
body: How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration is working with NVIDIA to deploy open source AI tools to accelerate the science that makes new treatments possible. October 27, 2026 by Anthony Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! There are 57 million people worldwide living with dementia today. For the researchers working to help them, the obstacle isn’t a lack of effort — it’s too much data, too few experts to synthesize it and a pace of discovery that can’t keep up with the disease. The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN), working with NVIDIA, is using AI to change that. Alzheimer’s disease is one of today’s leading global health challenges, with over 10 million new dementia cases diagnosed each year. Despite a 7x increase in National Institutes of Health funding in the last 15 years — reaching $3.9 billion annually — no treatment has been found to stop, prevent or reverse the disease yet. The bottlenecks are not enough high impact scientific findings, too much data living in institutional silos and too slow a pace of synthesis to keep up with the research that is published. C-BRAIN, led by Dr. Randall Bateman and a consortium of 18 member institutions across academic, philanthropic, pharma and research organizations, launched in November 2025 to help scientists make better, faster discoveries by accelerating the research that makes new treatments possible. “We have a window of opportunity with artificial intelligence to do research fundamentally different than we’ve ever done before, in a way that accelerates discoveries to help patients,” said Bateman, founder and director of C-BRAIN and the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Distinguished Professor of Neurology at the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. He described their work as “AI tools built by scientists, for scientists.” The consortium is building a system that harnesses previously untapped Alzheimer’s research data to support scientists’ work. Speeding Research From Weeks to Hours Essential assets in Alzheimer’s research are datasets that have never been publicly accessible to AI tools or human researchers. This includes unpublished findings, negative results and governed proprietary data from member institutions. “A lot of life sciences data doesn’t make its way into the frontier models,” said Dr. Ade Ojewole, chief technology officer of C-BRAIN. “The consequence of that is we’re leaving a lot of intelligence on the table.” C-BRAIN refers to this as “dark data,” which slows down Alzheimer’s research. Some dark data is directly deposited into secure computer systems for AI tools to access. To use this data without compromising patient privacy or institutional governance, C-BRAIN uses a hybrid centralized and federated approach — where AI models learn from data at each institution without that data ever having to leave its walls. This kind of infrastructure is technically demanding to build and scale, which is part of what NVIDIA brings to the collaboration. C-BRAIN currently runs 64 NVIDIA data center GPUs on premises alongside cloud-based nodes on Microsoft Azure, with additional NVIDIA GPU capacity, including NVIDIA Blackwell systems , on the horizon as the consortium’s ambitions scale. To explore how AI and accelerated computing can advance Alzheimer’s research while navigating its technical demands, C-BRAIN is working with NVIDIA to incorporate technologies including the NVIDIA BioNeMo open developer platform and the MONAI framework for C-BRAIN’s research pipelines. “The C-BRAIN collaboration with NVIDIA aims to unlock those models in a way that they can deliver something quite impactful and important,” said Bateman. “A great deal of optimization is going to be needed as we push the boundaries of what today’s spatial omics machine learning architectures can model,” Ojewole said. “NVIDIA software is definitely going to come into play there.” Researchers at C-BRAIN have already built two tools: OpenScientist — built with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in an effort led by research scientist Justin Reese — and InsightEngine , built with 387 Labs. OpenScientist is an open source agentic AI co-scientist that takes a scientist’s research question and dataset, then semi-autonomously generates hypotheses, runs analyses and produces verifiable, auditable insights. InsightEngine is an open source research platform that uses agentic AI to test hypotheses against the scientific literature, analyzing user-supplied datasets, exploring a biomedical knowledge graph and checking every claim against evidence to catch hallucinations before researchers commit to costly experiments. In published case studies, OpenScientist completed analyses in minutes that domain scientists estimated would take weeks to months, at a cost of under $10 per run. At C-BRAIN’s current reach of over 200 research groups, this capability could release substantial research capacity, potentially exceeding one million hours annually at scale. From Correlation to Cause Looking ahead, C-BRAIN aims to build a multimodal biological foundation model trained on the full breadth of its data — neuroimaging, multi-omics, fluid biomarkers and longitudinal clinical measures. By year three, it aims to discover new causal mechanisms of brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease, moving to testable scientific principles using the full scope of available research and data. Bateman said, “ AI that can think and reason has the potential to accelerate discoveries that will lead to powerful and implementable preventions and treatments for the entire population.” Categories: AI Tags: Agentic AI AI for Good Healthcare and Life Sciences Open Source Related News AI How AI Is Changing the Pace of Discovery for Millions Living With Dementia Oct 27, 2026 AI NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models Oct 21, 2026 AI NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations Oct 21, 2026 AI Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction Oct 21, 2026
retained_feed_body: There are 57 million people worldwide living with dementia today. For the researchers working to help them, the obstacle isn’t a lack of effort — it’s too much data, too few experts to synthesize it and a pace of discovery that can’t keep up with the disease. The Consortium for Biomedical Research and AI in Neurodegeneration (C-BRAIN), working with NVIDIA, is using AI to change that. Alzheimer’s disease is one of today’s leading global health challenges, with over 10 million new dementia cases diagnosed each year. Despite a 7x increase in National Institutes of Health funding in the last 15 years — reaching $3.9 billion annually — no treatment has been found to stop, prevent or reverse the disease yet. The bottlenecks are not enough high impact scientific findings, too much data living in institutional silos and too slow a pace of synthesis to keep up with the research that is published. C-BRAIN, led by Dr. Randall Bateman and a consortium of 18 member institutions across academic, philanthropic, pharma and research organizations, launched in November 2025 to help scientists make better, faster discoveries by accelerating the research that makes new treatments possible. “We have a window of opportunity with artificial intelligence to do research fundamentally different than we’ve ever done before, in a way that accelerates discoveries to help patients,” said Bateman, founder and director of C-BRAIN and the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Distinguished Professor of Neurology at the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis. He described their work as “AI tools built by scientists, for scientists.” The consortium is building a system that harnesses previously untapped Alzheimer’s research data to support scientists’ work. Speeding Research From Weeks to Hours Essential assets in Alzheimer’s research are datasets that have never been publicly accessible to AI tools or human researchers. This includes unpublished findings, negative results and governed proprietary data from member institutions. “A lot of life sciences data doesn’t make its way into the frontier models,” said Dr. Ade Ojewole, chief technology officer of C-BRAIN. “The consequence of that is we’re leaving a lot of intelligence on the table.” C-BRAIN refers to this as “dark data,” which slows down Alzheimer’s research. Some dark data is directly deposited into secure computer systems for AI tools to access. To use this data without compromising patient privacy or institutional governance, C-BRAIN uses a hybrid centralized and federated approach — where AI models learn from data at each institution without that data ever having to leave its walls. This kind of infrastructure is technically demanding to build and scale, which is part of what NVIDIA brings to the collaboration. C-BRAIN currently runs 64 NVIDIA data center GPUs on premises alongside cloud-based nodes on Microsoft Azure, with additional NVIDIA GPU capacity, including NVIDIA Blackwell systems , on the horizon as the consortium’s ambitions scale. To explore how AI and accelerated computing can advance Alzheimer’s research while navigating its technical demands, C-BRAIN is working with NVIDIA to incorporate technologies including the NVIDIA BioNeMo open developer platform and the MONAI framework for C-BRAIN’s research pipelines. “The C-BRAIN collaboration with NVIDIA aims to unlock those models in a way that they can deliver something quite impactful and important,” said Bateman. “A great deal of optimization is going to be needed as we push the boundaries of what today’s spatial omics machine learning architectures can model,” Ojewole said. “NVIDIA software is definitely going to come into play there.” Researchers at C-BRAIN have already built two tools: OpenScientist — built with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in an effort led by research scientist Justin Reese — and InsightEngine , built with 387 Labs. OpenScientist is an open source agentic AI co-scientist that takes a scientist’s research question and dataset, then semi-autonomously generates hypotheses, runs analyses and produces verifiable, auditable insights. InsightEngine is an open source research platform that uses agentic AI to test hypotheses against the scientific literature, analyzing user-supplied datasets, exploring a biomedical knowledge graph and checking every claim against evidence to catch hallucinations before researchers commit to costly experiments. In published case studies, OpenScientist completed analyses in minutes that domain scientists estimated would take weeks to months, at a cost of under $10 per run. At C-BRAIN’s current reach of over 200 research groups, this capability could release substantial research capacity, potentially exceeding one million hours annually at scale. From Correlation to Cause Looking ahead, C-BRAIN aims to build a multimodal biological foundation model trained on the full breadth of its data — neuroimaging, multi-omics, fluid biomarkers and longitudinal clinical measures. By year three, it aims to discover new causal mechanisms of brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease, moving to testable scientific principles using the full scope of available research and data. Bateman said, “ AI that can think and reason has the potential to accelerate discoveries that will lead to powerful and implementable preventions and treatments for the entire population.”

Handling complex tasks Using advanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities, Gemini 4 Argon excels in deep comprehension and long-horizon workflows. From a short prompt and with zero assets or libraries, Argon wrote 5,000 lines of math to render a 3D sunlit library from scratch — and then made a video about the process. This allows Argon in Antigravity to code a custom “fur engine” with studio-grade hair dynamics, generating visually rich fur that grows and moves as a character does. We also used Argon in Antigravity to create an interactive musical “G” with fluid physics and reactive sound. It features a recycled aluminum body, water resistance, and a seven-day battery life. You can customize your look with a variety of new bands for any occasion. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer When we set out to design the new Fitbit Edge , 1 we asked ourselves a fundamental question: How do we reimagine the fitness tracker to establish a bold new standard for performance, aesthetics, and comfort? For millions of people, a lightweight, discreet tracker is the ideal health and fitness companion. But active lifestyles demand more than just passive tracking. They require at-a-glance readability, dependable durability, and all-day comfort. With Fitbit Edge, we reconsidered every curve, interaction, and material to create a wearable device that feels as natural during a strenuous workout as it does at a dinner party. Instant glanceability Our first major design focus was the screen. When you’re mid-stride during a run, you shouldn’t have to squint or break your rhythm to check your stats. Our largest, brightest tracker display yet features a brilliant Hybrid OLED panel that’s easy to read, even with a harsh outdoor glare. 2 We paired the screen with a completely overhauled UX and UI, structuring information into glanceable, high-contrast tiles and expressive clock faces that spotlight your key health and fitness information while delivering a distinctive look that elevates Fitbit Edge’s unique form. Precision control and fit We carefully designed the mechanical architecture to include a tactile physical side button. A responsive touchscreen is great for daily navigation, but when you're mid-workout, tactility is everything. Sweaty fingers or wet weather can make on-screen tapping frustrating, but the ergonomic side button ensures that pausing your workout — or taking any other quick actions — is just a click away. To ensure Fitbit Edge fits well, we sculpted the thin chassis and bottom sensor housing with a subtle curve. By contouring the device to match the anatomy of your wrist, we minimized pressure points while ensuring continuous skin contact for 24/7 heart-rate and sleep tracking. Enduring design Water- and dust-resistant, 3 Fitbit Edge balances elegance with active durability. Its chassis is made from 100% recycled aluminum 4 and comes in four finishes: Obsidian, Olive, Canyon, and Fog. Our accessories have also been completely redesigned. 5 Switching up your look is easy whether you opt for a sleek, minimalist look or an active, athletic design. Active Sport Band: Features wide perforations for maximum breathability during intense workouts. Available in Obsidian, Porcelain, Olive, and Hibiscus. Performance Loop Band: 6 Combines stretchable, micro-adjustable fabric with custom swivel lugs to wrap closely to your wrist. Available in Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. Magnet Band : Pairs a premium silicone substrate with soft magnets for an intuitive clasp and a clean, minimalist silhouette. Available in Obsidian, Fog, and Mahogany. Metal Link Band : Brings a classic, refined aesthetic to your daily companion. Available in Matte Black, Brushed Silver, and Champagne Gold. When you're wearing a device 24/7, you need to trust that it's built to last . We thoughtfully crafted every detail of Fitbit Edge to stand up to your toughest days and keep up with your active lifestyle. With up to seven days of battery life, 7 it lets you spend less time plugged in and more time getting after your goals. title: Jury Finds Man Guilty of Bias-Related Hate Crime for Murdering a Homeless Man
body: Press Release Jury Finds Man Guilty of Bias-Related Hate Crime for Murdering a Homeless Man Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Defendant Targeted Homeless People to Shoot WASHINGTON – Gerald Brevard, III, 35, of Washington, D.C., was found guilty today of bias-related hate crimes in the Superior Court for the District of Columbia, on charges stemming from the murder of 54-year-old Morgan Holmes, a homeless man and attacks on two other homeless men, in March 2022, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “This defendant’s deliberate and violent attacks on vulnerable members of our community represent a grave breach of public safety and basic human dignity,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Today’s convictions affirms that such brutality will be met with a firm and decisive response.” Brevard was found guilty of 16 counts to include first-degree murder while armed, assault with intent to kill while armed, aggravated assault while armed, mayhem while armed, and multiple firearm offenses.  Brevard was also found guilty of bias-related hate crimes based on the victims perceived or actual homelessness.  Superior Court Judge Neal Kravitz scheduled sentencing for January 29, 2027. According to the government’s evidence, between March 3 and March 9, 2022, Brevard attacked three homeless men in Washington, D.C.  On March 3, 2022, he shot the first victim, who was asleep under a bridge on New York Avenue, N.E.  On March 8, 2022, again, while armed with a firearm, Brevard shot a second victim at his encampment on H Street, N.E.  The victim suffered serious and permanent bodily injuries as a result of the six gunshot wounds to his head, chest, and body.  Finally, on March 9, 2022, Brevard stabbed and shot the third victim who was lying in bed in his encampment on New York Avenue, N.E., resulting in his death.  The defendant then set the victim’s body and encampment on fire. All three men were homeless and living in Northeast, D.C. at the time they were attacked. Brevard was arrested on March 15, 2022, and has been in custody since. Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department. This case was investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department with assistance from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives Washington Field Division. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Michelle D. Jackson and Sarah C. Santiago. 2022 CF1 001525 Contact USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Non-citizen pleads guilty to unlawful voting in federal election
body: Press Release Non-citizen pleads guilty to unlawful voting in federal election Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Wyoming usawy.pio@usdoj.gov CHEYENNE, Wyo. — Maksim Sergeevich Shakirov , 29, a citizen of Uzbekistan residing in Rawlins, Wyoming, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of voting by an alien, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 611. Shakirov appeared before Chief U.S. District Judge Kelly H. Rankin for his initial appearance and entry of his guilty plea. According to court documents, Shakirov unlawfully cast a ballot in the federal election held on November 5, 2024. “Election integrity is the cornerstone of our Republic. We will not tolerate non‑citizens voting,” said U.S. Attorney Darin Smith. “Anyone who votes illegally in Wyoming will be found out and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.” Shakirov’s sentencing is scheduled for January 14, 2027. The court will determine the appropriate sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other applicable statutory factors. The Carbon County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case in coordination with Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorney Lance Johnston is handling the case. Case No. 26-CR-0070. The U.S. Attorney’s Office reminds the public that federal law protects voters from intimidation, disruption, and fraud at the polls. Individuals with information concerning suspected election crimes or voting rights violations may report those concerns to the Department of Justice or local law enforcement. Information regarding suspected election fraud or unlawful voting may also be reported to the FBI by calling 1-800-CALL-FBI (225-5324) or submitting a tip online at tips.fbi.gov . Updated October 28, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - Wyoming Press Release Number: 26-051

title: Seattle restaurant owner sentenced to prison for failing to pay employment taxes for dozens of employees over ten years
body: Press Release Seattle restaurant owner sentenced to prison for failing to pay employment taxes for dozens of employees over ten years Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Spent the money on an expensive remodel, gambling, travel and more Seattle – The owner of a restaurant in Seattle’s Capitol Hill neighborhood was sentenced Monday in U.S. District Court in Seattle to 13 months in prison and three years of supervised release for willfully failing to pay over more than $1.4 million in unemployment, Social Security, and Medicare taxes – some of which were withheld from employee paychecks, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Ruadhri McCormick, 44, of Seattle, owns and operates Single Shot restaurant. Between 2014 and 2024 he employed as many as 87 people as servers, bartenders, and cooks. While McCormick withheld payroll taxes from employee paychecks, he kept the money and failed to pay it over to the Internal Revenue Service.  At the sentencing hearing U.S. District Judge Kimberly K. Evanson said, “This offense involves a significant breach of public trust…  During the period when taxes were not being paid, he was spending on a home remodel, casino expenses, and travel.” “This defendant chose to use money that should have gone to pay for the employee’s future benefits, to pay to remodel a home on Vashon Island,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “Unfortunately, the employee’s Social Security work records now show gaps where they don’t have credit for the years they put in at McCormick’s restaurant.” McCormick was ordered to pay $1,446,341 in restitution. For at least thirty-six quarters between 2014 and 2024, McCormick failed to pay $1,027,362 in payroll taxes that had been withheld from employee paychecks. McCormick also failed to pay the employer portions of the Social Security taxes, Medicare taxes, and federal unemployment taxes – more than $400,000 – bringing the total tax loss to $1,446,341. McCormick also admitted in his plea agreement that he did not file his personal income taxes from any tax year 2015 through 2024. The investigation found that McCormick spent nearly $400,000 buying and remodeling a home on Vashon Island, nearly $125,000 on casinos expenses, and more than $38,000 on travel. In asking for a 15-month prison sentence, Assistant United States Attorney Lauren Staniar noted that several employees’ Social Security work history appears incomplete for years they worked at Single Shot, meaning their benefits at retirement could be lower. In her sentencing memo AUSA Staniar wrote, “McCormick failed to pay employment taxes for about a decade—from 2014 through 2024. This crime does not reflect a momentary lapse in judgment. Thirty-nine times McCormick’s quarterly taxes came due, and thirty-nine times he made the conscious decision not to pay them. McCormick also deprived his employees of money they earned as servers, bartenders, and cooks. McCormick withheld taxes from his employees’ paychecks, meaning he reduced their take-home pay by an amount he represented he would remit to the IRS on their behalf. In some sense, that money belonged to the employees’—McCormick was supposed to hold it in trust on their behalf and send it to the IRS for their benefits. But, instead of remitting the withheld amounts as promised, the money sat in Single Shot’s bank account, where McCormick spent it on himself.” The case was investigated by the Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigations (IRS-CI). The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Lauren Watts Staniar. Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Tax Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Renton, Washington resident sentenced to 4+ years in prison for drug trafficking
body: Press Release Renton, Washington resident sentenced to 4+ years in prison for drug trafficking Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Investigation reveals a known gang member trafficking drugs to homeless encampments and sex trafficking vulnerable victims Seattle – A 40-year-old Renton, Washington man was sentenced Monday in U.S. District Court in Seattle to 50 months in prison for drug trafficking, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Davon Malbrough was identified as a member of the “Family Mafia Crips” – a criminal gang profiting off the distribution of controlled substances and sex trafficking with ties to the unlawful possession of firearms and various violent crimes. In 2023, the Drug Enforcement Administration and Homeland Security Investigations began investigating drug and sex trafficking by members of the gang. Malbrough was spotted repeatedly selling fentanyl and methamphetamine at a homeless encampment in Bellingham, Washington. At the sentencing hearing U.S. District Judge Kymberly K. Evanson said “This is a very serious offense.  The defendant distributed highly addictive drugs to highly addicted people.” According to records filed in the case, on several days in July 2023, Malbrough was spotted at a transient encampment in Bellingham that was known to be a hotbed of drug use and other criminal activity. On three different occasions Malbrough sold fentanyl powder and pills to a person working with law enforcement. In December 2023, a traffic stop of Malbrough’s Jaguar SUV led to the seizure of 10 grams of pure methamphetamine, 3.5 grams of fentanyl pills, 12.6 grams of fentanyl powder along with two drug scales and $1,250 of drug proceeds. In October 2025, Malbrough was indicted for possession of controlled substances with intent to distribute and two counts of distribution of controlled substances. In June 2026 Malbrough pleaded guilty to possession of controlled substances with intent to distribute. In asking for a 63-month sentence prosecutors wrote to the court, “Malbrough was released from prison in late 2018 following his near 150-month sentence for Assault in the first degree. He ended his term of supervised release on October 18, 2022. Less than one year later, he was selling fentanyl to transients in a homeless encampment and trafficking women for profit. The rapid recidivism shows a heightened risk to community safety.” The case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Zachary Dilon and Kate Crisham. Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Second Defendant in Largest Methamphetamine Seizure in New Jersey History Admits to Drug Distribution Conspiracy
body: Press Release Second Defendant in Largest Methamphetamine Seizure in New Jersey History Admits to Drug Distribution Conspiracy Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey ***260 Pounds of Methamphetamine Seized During April Arrest*** CAMDEN, N.J. – A Mexican national admitted yesterday to conspiring to distribute over 260 pounds of methamphetamine into New Jersey—the largest seizure of methamphetamine in the state’s history—U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Carlos H. Cordero-Gutierrez, 54, of Juarez City, Mexico, pleaded guilty yesterday before U.S. District Judge Karen M. Williams in Camden federal court to a one-count Information charging him with conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine. According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: In April 2026, Cordero-Gutierrez picked up a shipment containing hundreds of pounds of methamphetamine in a tractor-trailer truck in Texas for delivery to New Jersey. Cordero-Gutierrez drove the truck to New Jersey, arriving on April 28, 2026. After Cordero-Gutierrez brought the truck to a pre-arranged delivery location, law enforcement officers arrested Cordero-Gutierrez and another co-conspirator, Marcos Cesar Acosta. Officers seized three black storage boxes, one duffel bag, and a garbage bag from the truck cab, all of which contained methamphetamine. Collectively, the seized methamphetamine from the truck weighed over 260 pounds. The conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine charge carries a mandatory minimum penalty of 10 years in prison, a maximum potential penalty of life in prison, and a fine of up to $10,000,000. Sentencing is scheduled for March 23, 2027. Acosta previously pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine on August 5, 2026 before Judge Williams. Sentencing is scheduled for December 17, 2026. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) MOPOD Enforcement Group 11 and the DEA Camden Resident Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Towanda R. Thorne-James, for the investigation leading to the guilty plea. He also thanked the Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, and IRS-Criminal Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Jenifer L. Piovesan, for their assistance in the investigation. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Jonathan S. Garelick of the U.S. Attorney’s Office Criminal Division in Trenton. ### Defense counsel: Marcos Cesar Acosta: Margaret M. Grasso, Esq. Carlos H. Cordero-Gutierrez: James P. Maguire, Esq., Office of the Federal Public Defender. corderogutierrez.information.pdf Updated October 27, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-235

title: Recidivist Domestic Violence Offender Sentenced To 15 Years In Federal Prison
body: Press Release Recidivist Domestic Violence Offender Sentenced To 15 Years In Federal Prison Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Washington Spokane, Washington – First Assistant United States Attorney Pete Serrano announced that on October 14, 2026, United States District Judge Mary K. Dimke sentenced Michael James Andrews to 180 months in federal prison after Andrews was convicted by a jury of Assault Resulting in Substantial Bodily Injury to an Intimate and Dating Partner in Indian Country; Assault with a Dangerous Weapon in Indian Country; and Use, Brandishing, and Discharge of a Firearm During a Crime of Violence. Judge Dimke also ordered that, following his sentence, Andrews be placed on a five-year term of supervised release. According to court documents, on September 18, 2024, Andrews – a convicted felon who was prohibited from possessing a firearm – pistol-whipped and shot at his intimate partner while inside their shared residence on the Spokane Indian Reservation. Andrews then attempted to obstruct justice by asking potential witnesses to not speak to law enforcement and using a family member to hide the firearm used in the assault. At sentencing, Judge Dimke noted Andrews’ history of assault related convictions, which included a previous federal conviction for Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury. Judge Dimke also noted that Andrews had been charged by the Spokane Tribe of Indians for domestic violence offenses on numerous occasions. Judge Dimke described Andrews’ conduct as a “reign of terror over the community,” and noted the sentence she imposed would put a stop to it. “The successful federal prosecution of a habitual domestic violence offender in Indian Country affirms our duty to fight relentlessly for victims whose safety has been threatened time and again,” stated Serrano. “Each prosecution and conviction reflects a commitment to ensuring that repeat abusers are held accountable and that survivors receive the justice, protection, and dignity they deserve. We proudly stand with our tribal and federal law enforcement partners and will continue to bring these important cases to light.” “It is horrifying that this victim was attacked in her own home by a partner who should have cared about her wellbeing,” said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. “Thanks to the work of the FBI and our tribal law enforcement partners, Mr. Andrews will have the next 15 years in prison to consider the consequences of his actions while the community is protected from his violence. This sentence sends a message to other would-be offenders that we are committed to combatting violent crime on tribal lands and throughout Washington state.” The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Spokane Tribal Police Department. This case was prosecuted by Michael J. Ellis and Michael L. Vander Giessen, Assistant United States Attorneys for the Eastern District of Washington. 2:24-cr-00139-MKD Contact USAWAE.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 27, 2026 Component USAO - Washington, Eastern

title: Texas Woman Sentenced to Prison for Conspiracy to Distribute Fentanyl Pills
body: Press Release Texas Woman Sentenced to Prison for Conspiracy to Distribute Fentanyl Pills Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada LAS VEGAS – A Dallas, Texas, woman was sentenced today by United States District Judge Gloria M. Navarro to 36 months in prison for bringing more than 12,000 fentanyl pills into the Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas and attempting to transport the drugs on an airplane to Texas. The government recommended a sentence of 57 months in prison. “Pumping thousands of lethal doses into our streets isn't just low-level drug dealing—it's a calculation of death for profit,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “A cache of 12,000 fentanyl pills represents thousands of potential overdoses waiting to happen. This sentence serves as a direct warning to anyone pushing this poison through Nevada's communities: federal law enforcement will hunt you down, and you will spend the next chapter of your life behind federal bars." “Protecting the integrity of the American electoral process is among our highest responsibility,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Office. “We will exhaustively pursue and hold accountable anyone who seeks to undermine our elections, ensuring that every citizen's right to a free and fair vote is protected. We will utilize all appropriate resources to investigate credible claims of voter fraud, steadfastly guided by our core values of Fidelity, Bravery, and Integrity. Always remember: Justice will find you.” According to court documents, Aundrea Cymone Hamilton conspired with others to distribute one kilogram or more of fentanyl, a Schedule II controlled substance. On March 18, 2023, Hamilton arrived at the Las Vegas airport with a carryon luggage containing 1321.5 grams of fentanyl she attempted to transport to Texas. During a screening of Hamilton’s carryon luggage, the Transportation Security Administration noticed abnormalities and pulled the carryon luggage for secondary screening. Once Hamilton saw the luggage had been pulled, she left the security checkpoint, exited the airport, and fled to Texas by bus. In January 2025, Hamilton was arrested in Texas. This case was investigated by the FBI. Assistant United States Attorney Melinda Brewer prosecuted the case. ### Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Opioids Component USAO - Nevada

title: No luck in Wyoming: Las Vegas woman sentenced to federal prison for forged treasury check scheme
body: Press Release No luck in Wyoming: Las Vegas woman sentenced to federal prison for forged treasury check scheme Tuesday, October 27, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Wyoming usawy.pio@usdoj.gov CASPER, Wyo. — Katrina Marie Amaya-Lopez , 47, of Las Vegas, Nevada, was sentenced to 24 months’ imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release for passing a stolen U.S. Treasury check that she falsely endorsed and passed at a Wyoming bank. U.S. District Court Judge Scott W. Skavdahl imposed the sentence on Oct. 20, 2026, in Casper. Amaya-Lopez was also ordered to pay $150,590 in restitution. According to court records, investigators tracked Amaya-Lopez across state lines, arresting her in Nevada on May 1, 2026. “If you bring financial fraud to Wyoming, pack a toothbrush for a federal prison stay,” said U.S. Attorney Darin D. Smith, underscoring the state's aggressive stance on cross-border financial crimes. This case was investigated by the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration. Assistant U.S. Attorney Margaret Vierbuchen prosecuted the crime on behalf of the United States. Case No. 26-CR-00069 This case was part of the Department of Justice's National Fraud Enforcement Division, a specialized, data-driven unit that investigates and prosecutes fraud targeting American citizens and taxpayer-funded programs. The division's operations directly support Executive Order 14395, issued by President Donald J. Trump on March 16, 2026. This order established the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government initiative that implements strict eligibility verification and protects federal and state benefit networks from systemic exploitation. ### Updated October 27, 2026 Topics Fraud Financial Fraud Component USAO - Wyoming Press Release Number: 26-050

title: October 2026 euro area bank lending survey
body:
October 2026 euro area bank lending survey Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date PRESS RELEASE October 2026 euro area bank lending survey 27 October 2026 Further tightening of credit standards for loans to firms and consumer credit, owing to higher risks Decline in loan demand across all segments, driven mainly by higher interest rates Gradual but sustained increase in demand for loans to finance AI infrastructure According to the October 2026 bank lending survey (BLS), euro area banks reported a further net tightening of credit standards – banks’ internal guidelines or loan approval criteria – for loans or credit lines to enterprises in the third quarter of 2026 (net percentage of 9% of banks; Chart 1). Banks reported unchanged credit standards for loans to households for house purchase (net percentage of 0%) and a further net tightening for consumer credit and other lending to households (net percentage of 14%). For firms, the net tightening surpassed the expectations reported by banks in the previous survey round (5%). Heightened risk perceptions and banks’ reduced risk tolerance remained the main drivers of tighter credit standards, with some banks reporting increasing pressure as a result of geopolitical uncertainty and energy developments. In a dedicated question on the importance of new lending to finance firms’ adoption or development of artificial intelligence (AI), banks indicated that they are still adapting their lending practices to the growing use of these technologies. Most reported that they had not yet introduced specific quantitative criteria for assessing AI-related lending within their credit standards. A small number noted that AI adoption and its associated risks increasingly feature in qualitative borrower assessments, with IT firms subject to the closest scrutiny. Banks reported broadly unchanged credit standards for housing loans and a further net tightening of credit standards for consumer credit. For housing loans, banks had expected a slight net tightening. Meanwhile, the tightening of credit standards for consumer credit exceeded banks’ expectations, owing mainly to lower risk tolerance and heightened risk perceptions. For the fourth quarter of 2026, banks expect credit standards to tighten further for firms and tighten significantly for both housing loans and consumer credit. Banks’ overall terms and conditions – the actual terms and conditions agreed in loan contracts – tightened for all loan segments, driven mainly by higher interest rates. Banks reported a net increase in the share of rejected loan applications for all borrower groups. The net increase in the share was higher for consumer credit than for loans to firms and housing loans. In the third quarter of 2026, euro area banks reported a net decrease in demand for loans or credit lines to firms (net percentage of -6%; Chart 2). This net decline stood in contrast to banks’ expectations of an increase in the previous survey round (4%) and followed a small net increase in the second quarter (3%). Loan demand was primarily dampened by the general level of interest rates. Weaker demand for fixed investment among small and medium-sized enterprises and the move towards alternative sources of finance also weighed slightly on loan demand. Some banks reported that uncertainty regarding geopolitical and energy developments continued to suppress corporate loan demand, while upward pressure came from demand for inventories and working capital. When asked about the impact of AI adoption on demand, several banks indicated that they expect a gradual but sustained increase in loan demand to finance digital infrastructure, particularly data centres. Banks also reported that their current and prospective AI-related lending is more likely to target infrastructure providers than software developers or firms adopting AI, with this focus expected to become more pronounced over the coming months. Banks reported a strong net decrease in demand for housing loans (net percentage of -27%), which was a more pronounced decline than in the second quarter (-15%) and exceeded the expectations reported by banks in the previous survey round (-12%). Increases in interest rates were the main driver of the decline, followed by falling consumer confidence and worsening housing market prospects. The contribution from interest rates is consistent with policy rate changes being transmitted smoothly to financing conditions. Although substantial, the decline in demand remains well below the peak recorded during the previous rate hiking cycle. Demand for consumer credit and other lending to households fell slightly (net percentage of -2%), contrasting with banks’ expectations in the second quarter that demand would remain unchanged (0%). Developments in interest rates and lower consumer confidence were the main factors behind the decline in demand for consumer credit, followed by subdued spending on durable goods. In the fourth quarter of 2026, banks expect to see more significant declines in demand for housing loans (-36%) and consumer credit (-14%), whereas they anticipate that demand for loans to firms will remain broadly unchanged (-1%). Euro area banks’ access to retail funding, debt securities and money markets decreased further in the third quarter of 2026, while it remained broadly unchanged for securitisations. The deterioration in access to retail funding, although still moderate, was the largest since the beginning of the series in 2011 and slightly higher than the previous peak in the third quarter of 2023, driven by both short and long-term retail funding. Banks expect access to funding across all sources to deteriorate further over the next three months. The reduction in the monetary policy asset portfolio of the European Central Bank (ECB) has had a mildly negative impact on euro area banks’ market financing conditions and liquidity positions over the last 12 months, while prompting a further increase in their holdings of euro area sovereign bonds. The impact on bank profitability has been slightly positive, with higher net interest income being partially offset by small capital losses. Banks expect these effects to persist over the coming 12 months. They also reported a tightening impact on lending conditions across all loan categories, which they expect to increase over the next 12 months. Euro area banks reported a net tightening impact of non-performing loan ratios and other credit quality indicators on their credit standards for loans to firms, housing loans and consumer credit in the third quarter of 2026. This mainly reflected higher risk perceptions. In the fourth quarter of 2026, euro area banks expect credit quality to have a further tightening impact on their credit standards for loans to firms and for consumer credit. In response to a new question on the impact of digital assets, euro area banks reported that digital assets have contributed slightly positively to their business strategy over the past 12 months. They assessed their impact on the broader financial situation over the same period as neutral. For the next 12 months, banks expect digital assets to have an increasingly positive impact on their business strategy and a negative influence on their retail funding business. Digital assets have had a neutral impact on credit standards over the past 12 months and are expected to ease credit standards for housing loans over the next 12 months. The quarterly BLS was developed by the Eurosystem to improve its understanding of bank lending behaviour in the euro area. The results reported in the October 2026 survey relate to changes observed in the third quarter of 2026 and changes expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, unless otherwise indicated. The October 2026 survey round was conducted between 21 September and 6 October 2026. A total of 159 banks were surveyed in this round, with a response rate of 100%. Chart 1 Changes in credit standards for loans or credit lines to enterprises, and contributing factors (net percentages of banks reporting a tightening of credit standards, and contributing factors) Source: ECB (BLS). Notes: Net percentages are defined as the difference between the sum of the percentages of banks responding “tightened considerably” and “tightened somewhat” and the sum of the percentages of banks responding “eased somewhat” and “eased considerably”. The net percentages for “Other factors” refer to an average of the further factors that were mentioned by banks as having contributed to changes in credit standards. Data are for the euro area and for the four largest euro area countries . Chart 2 Changes in demand for loans or credit lines to enterprises, and contributing factors (net percentages of banks reporting an increase in demand, and contributing factors) Source: ECB (BLS). Notes: Net percentages for the questions on demand for loans are defined as the difference between the sum of the percentages of banks responding “increased considerably” and “increased somewhat” and the sum of the percentages of banks responding “decreased somewhat” and “decreased considerably”. The net percentages for “Other factors” refer to an average of the further factors that were mentioned by banks as having contributed to changes in loan demand. Data are for the euro area and for the four largest euro area countries . For media queries, please contact William Lelieveldt , tel.: +49 170 227 9090. Notes A report on this survey round is available on the ECB’s website, along with a copy of the questionnaire , a glossary of BLS terms and a BLS user guide with information on the BLS series keys. The euro area and national data series are available on the ECB’s website via the ECB Data Portal . National results , as published by the respective national central banks, can be obtained via the ECB’s website. For more detailed information on the BLS, see Köhler-Ulbrich, P., Dimou, M., Ferrante, L. and Parle, C., “ Happy anniversary, BLS – 20 years of the euro area bank lending survey ”, Economic Bulletin , Issue 7, ECB, 2023, and Huennekes, F. and Köhler-Ulbrich, P., “ What information does the euro area bank lending survey provide on future loan developments? ”, Economic Bulletin , Issue 8, ECB, 2022. title: Treasury Issues Proposed Rule to Implement Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act
body: October 22, 2026 WASHINGTON– The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) today issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to propose updates to the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) based on direction from Congress in the Comprehensive Outbound Investment Security (COINS) Act, passed as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.  The COINS Act codifies the U.S. Government’s approach to regulating certain outbound investments by U.S. persons and builds upon Treasury’s existing OISP. In passing the COINS Act, Congress made clear that restricting certain U.S. outbound investments into dual-use strategic technologies that benefit a foreign adversary’s military modernization efforts, surveillance states, and human rights abuses is necessary to prevent harm to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. President Trump is committed to protecting our national security and the implementation of the COINS Act is consistent with maintaining a strong, open investment environment that benefits our economy and supports our national security interests. The COINS Act directs the Secretary of the Treasury (the Secretary) to issue regulations that (1) require United States persons to provide notification to Treasury regarding certain transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies, and (2) prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies.  The COINS Act authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations with technical parameters for “prohibited technology” and “notifiable technology” in five technology sectors: semiconductor technologies and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.  The COINS Act also authorizes the Secretary—in consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and subject to notice and comment rulemaking—to add and define technologies beyond those specifically listed in the law that enable the military, intelligence, surveillance, or cyber-enabled capabilities of a country of concern.  Accordingly, the Secretary has added biotechnology to the proposed regulations. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are committed to putting America’s national security first,” said Secretary Scott Bessent .  “The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security.  This important step also helps promote our commitment to an open investment environment by providing clarity to U.S. and foreign investors as well as an opportunity for them to provide feedback on the proposed regulations.” “The proposed regulations are designed to address risks that can arise when foreign adversaries try to benefit from U.S. investment in key technology sectors,” said Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security Christopher Pilkerton.  Pilkerton added, “It will enhance the Outbound Investment Security Program and our efforts to protect U.S. national security.” The NPRM issued today provides details on key concepts and aspects of the program’s proposed implementation, including: Requirements applicable to a U.S. person (including any controlled foreign entities); Categories of covered national security transactions; Definitions; The scope of covered foreign persons; Excepted transactions; Technical specifications to inform the scope of covered national security transactions based on certain technologies and products in the areas of semiconductor technology and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, super intelligence systems, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and supercomputing, and biotechnology; Information that a U.S. person is required to provide to Treasury as part of a notification; The process of requesting non-binding feedback and submitting confidential information; The knowledge standard and expectations for a U.S. person to conduct a reasonable and diligent inquiry prior to undertaking a transaction; and Conduct that would be treated as a violation of the proposed rule and applicable penalties for such conduct. Treasury invites comments from a wide range of stakeholders on all aspects of the NPRM including feedback on the scope of a covered national security transaction, definitions of key terms, the notification requirements, and the penalty and enforcement processes for violations, among other aspects.  Treasury will carefully consider this input before issuing the final implementing regulations. Written comments may be submitted by the deadline in the official NPRM, available at https://www.regulations.gov .  The NPRM will be followed at a later date by final implementing regulations, which will set an effective date for the program. The NPRM, fact sheet, and additional information are available at: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/outbound-investment-program .

title: The Trump Administration is Making Homeownership More Affordable
body: October 22, 2026 Proposed Rules Implement the ROAD to Housing Act and Support Affordable Homeownership in America WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury issued proposed regulations to make homeownership more affordable for hardworking Americans. The proposed regulations implement Section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (ROAD to Housing Act), which restricts large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, codifying key requirements of President Trump’s Executive Order 14376 , Stopping Wall Street from Competing with Main Street Homebuyers . “Under President Trump, this Administration continues to restore the path to affordable homeownership for millions of young and working families,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Treasury is working to ensure American families and workers have a fair shot at purchasing homes in their communities by increasing housing supply and limiting large institutional investors’ role in the market, while supporting a strong, stable housing market and avoiding unnecessary disruption.” RESTORING THE AMERICAN DREAM OF HOMEOWNERSHIP Beginning on January 7, 2027, a large institutional investor generally may not purchase, or enter into a contract to purchase, a single-family home unless the purchase qualifies as an “excepted purchase” under the ROAD to Housing Act. The ROAD to Housing Act defines a large institutional investor by reference to, among other things, whether an entity is engaged in the business of investing in, owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes and has direct or indirect investment control over at least 350 such homes. The ROAD to Housing Act permits several categories of excepted purchases, including purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs, renovate-to-rent programs, homeownership programs, and programs to boost homeownership. Today’s NPRM sets forth Treasury’s proposed framework to: Establish standards for purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs that promote continued investment in new housing; Provide a safe harbor for purchases made pursuant to renovate-to-rent programs that bring neglected homes back into the housing supply and up to code; Clarify the requirements for homeownership programs and programs to boost homeownership, including providing safe harbors for large institutional investors that provide meaningful financial support towards their renters’ purchase of a home; Clarify that an entity is engaged “in the business of” investing in , owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes when it does so for the purpose of receiving income or financial gain, and not incidentally to a different business; Define when an entity may qualify as a passive investor in another entity that owns a home because it does not share directors or officers with the other entity and does not have a property control right over the underlying homes; Clarify certain purchases involving debts previously contracted, loss mitigation, and transfers between large institutional investors that protect the liquidity of the housing market; and Clarify the calculation of the maximum civil penalty where a single prohibited purchase involves more than one large institutional investor. The proposed rule would provide non-exclusive safe harbors for several statutory requirements. These include standards for determining whether a home has been substantially rehabilitated under a renovate-to-rent program, whether a renter has received meaningful financial support under certain homeownership programs, and whether a renter has received a right of first refusal and 30-day first-look period. Treasury’s proposed approach recognizes that housing-market participants use a variety of ownership, investment, construction, servicing, and property-management structures and seeks to provide clarity without unnecessary disruption to housing supply, homebuilding, rehabilitation activity, or capital formation. Members of the public should submit comments in response to the NPRM within 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. The proposed regulations are available here . ###

title: October 22, 2026 - FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus to coordinate agency action on brain and nervous system conditions, with inaugural focus on Alzheimer's prevention For Immediate Release: October 22, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced the launch of the Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus (NAIN) , a new agency program aligned with the Trump Administration’s efforts to accelerate medical innovation and deliver breakthrough treatments. NAIN is designed to advance the science, tools, and regulatory approaches needed to support the development of medical products for conditions affecting the brain and nervous system. NAIN’s inaugural initiative, the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator , will focus on advancing medical products that help delay or prevent Alzheimer's disease. Both efforts support the National Alzheimer’s Project Act (NAPA), the federal government's comprehensive roadmap for coordinated action on Alzheimer's and related dementias. "The launch of NAIN reflects FDA's commitment — in support of the Trump Administration’s drive to transform health care innovation — to making sure our regulatory science and cross-center collaboration keep pace with the rapid advances happening in neuroscience," said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. "Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, we are bringing the full breadth of FDA's expertise to bear on one of the most urgent public health challenges of our time.” Developing medical products for neuroscience indications is associated with complex scientific and clinical challenges, including limited understanding of underlying biology, variable disease presentation, and difficulties in demonstrating meaningful clinical benefit, particularly for conditions that develop over many years. Advances in biomarkers, digital health technologies, and other medical product development tools, however, offer important opportunities to address these challenges. NAIN will bring together scientific and regulatory expertise from the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and Center for Devices and Radiological Health to address scientific and regulatory questions that benefit from coordinated consideration across drugs, biologics, and devices. NAIN will encompass conditions that affect the brain and nervous system broadly, including neurologic and psychiatric disorders, substance use disorders, and pain. NAIN will also support robust engagement with patients, industry, academia and other stakeholders to advance these efforts. As its first initiative, NAIN is launching the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator . This inaugural initiative will draw on perspectives from across the FDA and engage patients and caregivers, researchers, industry, public-private partnerships and other government agencies. The initiative will explore innovative approaches to advancing clinical trials for Alzheimer’s disease prevention and early-intervention drug development with emphasis on trial populations, stage-appropriate endpoints, and evidentiary approaches for demonstrating prevention or delay of cognitive decline due to Alzheimer’s disease. The FDA has long been committed to supporting the development of safe and effective medical products that address diseases and conditions of the brain and nervous system. Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, the agency is taking a proactive, coordinated approach to accelerating progress, bringing together its scientific and regulatory expertise, engaging the broader research and development community, and working in concert with federal partners to meet the scale of this public health challenge. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Shadow Fleet Networks
body: October 21, 2026 Law Firms, Shipping Agents, and Vessels Helped Conceal and Transport Iranian Commodities WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctioned Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis , which has supported illicit Iranian shipping activity for years, indirectly aiding Tehran’s ability to generate revenue to fund its military, weapons, and nuclear programs.  Throughout Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury has continued to coordinate with counterparts in Europe and around the world to sever the Iranian regime’s remaining economic lifelines. “Whether you are conducting illegal oil transfers at sea or sitting in the corner office of a law firm, if you are supporting the Iranian regime, we will find you and sanction you,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Iran’s facilitators must make a choice: Either you are with us or against us. We know who you are, we know what you’re doing, and we will continue to take action.” Treasury today also sanctioned Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents that directly aid Iranian shadow fleet operations.  Today’s actions strike not only the legal and maritime facilitators that sustain Iran's sanctions-evasion networks, but also a fleet of cargo vessels that has helped generate substantial revenue for the Iranian regime. The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum and petrochemical sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. FinCEN is acting in close coordination with European partners, including in Greece, and leveraging existing legal authorities, such as its first issuance of an administrative subpoena pursuant to 31 U.S.C. § 5318(k) of the Bank Secrecy Act, to advance its investigation into a Greek bank’s potential ties to Iran and its proxies. Additionally, FinCEN has issued multiple requests for information concerning banks’ relationships with OFAC-designated Iranian financial institutions. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026 and dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime. Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system.  Operation Economic Outcast also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . LAW FIRM ESTABLISHING SHADOW FLEET ARCHITECTURE Through Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury is targeting law firms and corporate service providers that establish shell and front companies for persons trading in sanctioned Iranian products, an essential service needed for any such malign actor to evade sanctions or regulatory compliance.  Panama- and Greece-based law firm Karnakis and Karnakis has for years leveraged its legal practice to register shipping companies that own shadow fleet vessels responsible for shipping hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian steel, petroleum, and petrochemicals, among other goods.  The firm previously set up the companies Skyros Maritime and Trading S.A. , Corfu Maritime and Trading S.A. , and Elias Shipping and Trading Group S.A. , among others, all of which OFAC has previously designated for their ownership of vessels active in the trade of Iranian petroleum and petroleum products. Elias Shipping and Trading SA, the owner of the RAMONA 1 (IMO: 9233222), served as a front company for the Al-Qatirji Company, a Syrian firm responsible for selling millions of barrels of Iranian oil for the benefit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF) and Houthis.  The Al-Qatirji Company at the time of its designation was one of the main financial channels for the IRGC-QF, enabling the terrorist group to generate and access hundreds of millions of dollars a year in revenue gained from the sale of Iranian oil. Karnakis and Karnakis played a particularly critical role in establishing the corporate architecture for the shipping empire of Iranian liquified petroleum gas (LPG) magnate Seyed Asadoollah Emamjomeh (Emamjomeh), which is collectively responsible for shipping hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian LPG and crude oil.  Karnakis and Karnakis served as the corporate agent for many of Emamjomeh’s firms, including several that were ultimately designated for their role in shipping Iranian petroleum products. Karnakis and Karnakis was founded, and is currently owned, by dual Panamanian-Greek nationals Sofianos Karnakis Kosmas and Konstantinos Karnakis Kosmas , with Panamanian-Greek national Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas and Panamanian national Pedro Ortega Jones serving as employees of the law firm.  Karnakis and Karnakis employees, including Panamanian national Roberto Ortega Jones , act as directors and officers of many of the companies they register in order to obfuscate the true beneficial owners of these companies. Karnakis and Karnakis is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum and petrochemical sectors of the Iranian economy.  Sofianos Karnakis Kosmas, Konstantinos Karnakis Kosmas, Pedro Ortega Jones, Roberto Ortega Jones, and Ioanis Karnakis Kosmas are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Karnakis and Karnakis. CARGO FLEET VESSELS Iran relies on seemingly legitimate cargo vessels to move Iranian petrochemicals and other products, including steel.  Panama- and Greece-based Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. (Roxette), for which Karnakis and Karnakis serves as the corporate agent, is the operator and ship manager of the Panama-flagged vessels ANEMOS (IMO 9205952), GLORIS (IMO 9449510), and PRIDE (IMO 9487407), all of which have shipped various cargos of Iranian-origin goods within the past year, including petrochemicals and steel products.  In addition, Roxette is the ship manager and operator of the Panama-flagged cargo vessels DESTINY (IMO 9385491), FLAMINGO 1 (IMO 9474199), HARMONY (IMO 9449522), and PRINCE (IMO 9548316). Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petrochemical sector of the Iranian economy.  ANEMOS, GLORIS, PRIDE, DESTINY, FLAMINGO 1, HARMONY, and PRINCE are being identified pursuant to E.O. 13902 as blocked property in which Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. has an interest. SHIPPING AGENTS AIDING SHADOW FLEET Shipping agents play a critical role in shadow fleet operations by aiding the transit of illicit Iranian cargo through ports, including oil, petroleum, and other commodities.  Treasury is taking action against two shipping agents that have helped Iran transport its products to buyers around the world. Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. (Amigoz) is a Singapore-based full-range shipping agency that provides port agency services.  Amigoz acted as the agent for a shipment of light crude oil overseen by Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company, which oversees a network of front companies that supports the allocation of billions of dollars’ worth of commodities to Iranian military entities.  As of 2026, Amigoz has been associated with a range of dark fleet actors, including some affiliated with the shipping empire of Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani , and provided bunkering services to the Iranian shadow fleet vessel ZIXUAN (IMO 9317298). Whales Shipping Line LLC (Whales), a Dubai-based maritime and logistics company, acted as the shipping agent for Sparrow Trading FZE, a sanctioned Dubai-based front company that organized the purchase of tens of millions of dollars’ worth of Iranian petrochemicals in coordination with Persian Gulf Petrochemical Industry Commercial Co.  Whales has also conducted business worth hundreds of thousands of dollars with Amigoz.  Whales is the registered owner of two UAE-flagged small support vessels: WHALES DIAMOND (IMO 9375032) and WHALES PEARL (IMO 9483114). Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd. is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy.  Whales Shipping Line LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Amigoz Singapore PTE. Ltd.  WHALES DIAMOND and WHALES PEARL are being identified as blocked property in which Whales Shipping Line LLC has an interest. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List .
